collocations: an extraneous variable in an experiment

words.enDefinition: A broad personality dimension often involving sociability, assertiveness, energy, and engagement with the social environment.

examples.en: The classroom profile illustrates extraversion with several examples of energetic participation during fictional group activities.
examples.zh: 课堂人物画像以虚构集体活动中的几项积极参与表现来说明「外向性」。

examples.en: We discuss how extraversion can be expressed differently in two imaginary students who both enjoy social gatherings.
examples.zh: 我们讨论两名都喜欢社交聚会的虚构学生会如何以不同方式表现「外向性」。

words.enDefinition: Tendency to prefer endpoints of a scale regardless of item content

examples.en: The fictional dataset illustrates extreme responding with repeated selection of the scale endpoints.
examples.zh: 虚构数据用反复选择量表两端选项的情形来说明「极端作答」。

examples.en: Our group discussed why extreme responding alone tells us little about the underlying opinions.
examples.zh: 我们组讨论了为什么只知道有「极端作答」，并不能充分了解实际看法。

words.zhGloss: 艾森克人格三因素模型
words.enDefinition: Eysenck's model organising personality into extraversion, neuroticism, and a broad trait dimension called psychoticism.
acceptedZhAnswers: 艾森克人格三因素模型

examples.en: The lecture compares Eysenck's three-factor model with a five-domain framework on the next slide of the presentation.
examples.zh: 讲座在下一张幻灯片上比较「艾森克人格三因素模型」和一个五维度框架。

examples.en: Our historical reading introduces Eysenck's three-factor model before describing how subsequent researchers proposed other broad trait structures.
examples.zh: 历史读物先介绍「艾森克人格三因素模型」，再讲后来的研究者如何提出其他宽泛的特质结构。

words.enDefinition: Extent to which a measure appears relevant to its intended purpose

examples.en: The worksheet discusses face validity by asking what the fictional test seems to measure.
examples.zh: 习题通过询问虚构测验看起来测什么来讨论「表面效度」。

examples.en: Our tutor explained why face validity alone cannot justify the proposed interpretation of scores.
examples.zh: 老师解释了为什么仅凭「表面效度」不能证明预定的分数解释合理。

collocations: distinguish face validity from empirical evidence

words.enDefinition: Coefficient linking an observed variable to a latent factor in a model

examples.en: The model assigns a factor loading to each arrow linking an item to a factor.
examples.zh: 模型为连接题目和因子的每个箭头分配一个「因子载荷」。

examples.en: We compared the factor loading for the same item across two simulated models.
examples.zh: 我们比较了同一道题在两个模拟模型中的「因子载荷」。

words.enDefinition: Pattern specifying underlying factors and how observed items relate to them

examples.en: The article compares the factor structure of two fictional scales with similar content.
examples.zh: 文章比较了内容相似的两个虚构量表的「因子结构」。

examples.en: Our group drew the proposed factor structure before inspecting the loadings table.
examples.zh: 我们组先画出拟定的「因子结构」，再查看载荷表。

words.enDefinition: A condition defined by one combination of factor levels.

examples.en: The worksheet labeled one factorial cell as large text on a plain background in the simulated design.
examples.zh: 习题将模拟设计中的一个「析因设计单元」标为纯色背景上的大号文字。

examples.en: We recorded a mean response time for each factorial cell before comparing the two display factors.
examples.zh: 我们比较两种显示因素前，先记录了每个「析因设计单元」的平均反应时间。

collocations: a mean for each factorial cell

words.enDefinition: A design that studies combinations of levels from two or more factors.

examples.en: We used a factorial design to compare every combination of two font sizes and two backgrounds.
examples.zh: 我们采用「析因设计」，比较两种字体大小与两种背景的所有组合。

examples.en: The instructor drew the factorial design as a grid so we could see all four combinations.
examples.zh: 老师把「析因设计」画成方格，让我们可以看到全部四种组合。

collocations: compare conditions in a factorial design

words.enDefinition: The proportion of signal-absent trials on which a signal is reported.

examples.en: The class computed the false alarm rate from yes responses in trials containing only background sound.
examples.zh: 全班根据仅有背景声却回答有信号的试次，计算了「虚报率」。

examples.en: The model produced a higher false alarm rate when observers accepted weaker evidence for a signal.
examples.zh: 观察者根据较弱证据也会报告存在信号时，模型给出的「虚报率」较高。

words.enDefinition: a task testing whether a person can predict behavior based on someone else's inaccurate belief

examples.en: The false-belief task asks where the absent character will look after an object was moved in the story.
examples.zh: 「错误信念任务」问，在故事里物品被移动之后，此前不在场的人物会去哪里寻找。

examples.en: We compared two false-belief task versions to see how their language demands differed in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 我们比较课堂示例的两个「错误信念任务」版本，观察它们在语言要求上有何差异。

words.enDefinition: A tendency to overestimate how many other people share one's own opinions, preferences, or behaviour.

examples.en: The worksheet illustrates the false consensus effect with fictional estimates of how many classmates prefer group assignments.
examples.zh: 练习单用“多少同学喜欢小组作业”的虚构估计值说明「虚假共识效应」。

examples.en: We compared the estimated and observed preferences when discussing the possible false consensus effect in class.
examples.zh: 课堂讨论可能存在的「虚假共识效应」时，我们对比了估计的偏好与实际观察到的偏好。

collocations: evidence of a false consensus effect

words.enDefinition: Recollection of something that did not occur or occurred differently

examples.en: The worksheet counts recalling an unshown picture as a false memory in the task.
examples.zh: 习题将任务中回忆起一张从未呈现的图片计为一次「虚假记忆」。

examples.en: The seminar discusses how a false memory can feel convincing despite being inaccurate.
examples.zh: 研讨课讨论「虚假记忆」为何虽然不准确，却依然能让人确信。

words.enDefinition: A tendency to underestimate how many others share one's own valued qualities or favourable behaviour.

examples.en: Our fictional survey example illustrates the false uniqueness effect using estimates of how many students volunteer regularly.
examples.zh: 虚构调查示例用对定期做志愿活动的学生人数的估计，说明「虚假独特性效应」。

examples.en: The class discusses the false uniqueness effect after comparing the fictional student's confident guess with the summary table.
examples.zh: 全班对照虚构学生自信给出的估计值与汇总表，然后讨论「虚假独特性效应」。

collocations: evidence for a false uniqueness effect

words.enDefinition: A hypothesis that could be contradicted by a possible observation.

examples.en: The tutor asked which possible classroom result would count against each proposed falsifiable hypothesis in the worksheet.
examples.zh: 辅导老师问，哪种可能的课堂结果能够反驳习题中提出的各项「可证伪假设」。

examples.en: Our claim became a falsifiable hypothesis when we identified a result that could contradict the prediction.
examples.zh: 我们确定什么结果可能与预测冲突后，提出的主张就成了「可证伪假设」。

collocations: the criteria for a falsifiable hypothesis

words.enDefinition: Reduced or altered performance associated with tiredness during repeated or prolonged testing.

examples.en: The slower responses near the end suggested a possible fatigue effect in the synthetic session data.
examples.zh: 合成实验记录中，临近结束时反应变慢，提示可能存在「疲劳效应」。

examples.en: We considered a fatigue effect before attributing every late error to the more complicated display.
examples.zh: 我们先考虑「疲劳效应」，再判断后期的错误是否都来自更复杂的显示方式。

collocations: a fatigue effect late in testing

words.enDefinition: Visual search for a target defined by a single distinguishing feature.

examples.en: The feature search example asked students to find the only red circle in an otherwise green display.
examples.zh: 在「特征搜索」示例中，学生要在其余全为绿色的图中找唯一的红色圆形。

examples.en: The simulated feature search results showed little change in response time as more distractors appeared.
examples.zh: 在模拟的「特征搜索」结果里，干扰项增多后反应时间变化不大。

collocations: compare feature search with conjunction search

words.enDefinition: The model in which sensation magnitude grows logarithmically with stimulus intensity.

examples.en: The curve from Fechner's law rises slowly even when the intensity increases by a large amount.
examples.zh: 即使刺激强度增加很多，「费希纳定律」给出的曲线也只缓慢上升。

examples.en: In the reading, Fechner's law described sensation magnitude on a different scale from physical intensity.
examples.zh: 阅读材料中的「费希纳定律」用不同于物理强度的尺度描述感觉量。

collocations: a curve predicted by Fechner's law

words.enDefinition: awareness of holding information even when you cannot recall it

examples.en: The exercise asks about a feeling of knowing after the participant cannot recall a word.
examples.zh: 参与者未能回忆起单词后，练习询问是否有「知晓感」。

examples.en: We compared ratings of feeling of knowing with recognition scores from the later test.
examples.zh: 我们把「知晓感」评分与随后测验中的再认分数作了比较。

words.enDefinition: The perceptual separation of a figure from the background against which it appears.

examples.en: The first image illustrated figure-ground organization because the dark shape stood out against the pale surrounding area.
examples.zh: 第一幅图中的深色形状在浅色区域的衬托下显得突出，说明了「图形与背景组织」。

examples.en: We discussed figure-ground organization after seeing how a single border could belong to either adjacent region.
examples.zh: 看到同一条边界可以归属任一相邻区域后，我们讨论了「图形与背景组织」。

words.enDefinition: An alternation in perception that exchanges which region is figure and which is ground.

examples.en: The vase drawing showed figure-ground reversal when two dark profiles became the figure instead of the vase.
examples.zh: 花瓶图中，两个深色侧脸取代花瓶成为主体，展示了「图形背景反转」。

examples.en: Several students reported a figure-ground reversal even though the picture itself stayed unchanged on the screen.
examples.zh: 尽管屏幕上的图没有变化，几名学生仍报告看到了「图形背景反转」。

words.enDefinition: Distortion of the published evidence when studies with unremarkable findings remain unpublished.

examples.en: The file drawer problem arose in the simulation because fictional studies with negligible effects remained unpublished.
examples.zh: 模拟中，效应微乎其微的虚构研究并未发表，出现了「文件抽屉问题」。

examples.en: We discussed how the file drawer problem could make an effect look stronger across the available studies.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么在现有可获得的研究中，「文件抽屉问题」可能让效应看起来更强。

collocations: evidence of a file drawer problem
the file drawer problem in psychology

words.enDefinition: development of controlled small movements, such as coordinated hand and finger actions

examples.en: The timeline illustrates fine motor development with increasingly precise ways of placing small pieces on a picture.
examples.zh: 时间线用把小拼块放到图上越来越精确的动作，说明「精细运动发展」。

examples.en: We compared the fictional examples of fine motor development while discussing speed and precision in separate tasks.
examples.zh: 我们讨论两个不同任务的速度和精确度时，比较了「精细运动发展」的虚构示例。

words.enDefinition: A model organising broad personality differences into openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism.

examples.en: The seminar compares the five-factor model with a fictional chart containing only three broad personality dimensions.
examples.zh: 研讨课比较了「人格五因素模型」和一张只含三种宽泛人格维度的虚构图表。

examples.en: Our textbook chapter introduces the five-factor model before discussing narrower characteristics within each broad domain.
examples.zh: 教材这一章先介绍「人格五因素模型」，再讨论各宽泛维度内较具体的特征。

words.enDefinition: A cross-shaped marker indicating where an observer should direct their gaze.

examples.en: The fixation cross stayed in the center while the classroom demonstration showed pictures on either side.
examples.zh: 课堂演示在两侧呈现图片时，「注视十字」一直留在中央。

examples.en: We marked the fixation cross on the blank frame that appeared before each example trial.
examples.zh: 我们在每个示例试次前出现的空白画面上标出了「注视十字」。

words.enDefinition: Schedule reinforcing the first response after a constant time interval

examples.en: The game simulation uses a fixed-interval schedule tied to a regular countdown.
examples.zh: 游戏模拟使用与规律倒计时相连的「固定时距时程」。

examples.en: The graph shows responses building near each interval's end under a fixed-interval schedule.
examples.zh: 图表显示，在「固定时距时程」下，反应在每个时段临近结束时增多。

words.enDefinition: Reinforcement schedule requiring a constant number of responses per reinforcer

examples.en: In the simulation, the fixed-ratio schedule requires the same number of matches each time.
examples.zh: 在模拟中，「固定比率时程」每次都要求相同的匹配次数。

examples.en: We identified the fixed-ratio schedule by counting responses between successive point deliveries.
examples.zh: 我们通过数两次得分之间的反应次数来识别「固定比率时程」。

words.enDefinition: Clustering near the lowest possible score that limits differentiation among low scorers

examples.en: The simulated test shows a floor effect because many scores cluster near zero.
examples.zh: 模拟测验中许多分数聚集在零分附近，出现了「地板效应」。

examples.en: We identified a floor effect when the hardest item set yielded nearly identical low scores.
examples.zh: 最难的一组题产生了几乎一样的低分，我们由此辨认出「地板效应」。

words.enDefinition: the ability to reason through novel problems and detect relationships beyond the use of acquired factual knowledge

examples.en: The classroom puzzle was chosen to illustrate fluid intelligence by using unfamiliar patterns and very little background information.
examples.zh: 课堂选择这个谜题来说明「流体智力」，其中采用陌生图案，所需背景信息很少。

examples.en: We compared fluid intelligence tasks with tasks relying heavily on learned word meanings in the test examples.
examples.zh: 我们把智力测验示例中的「流体智力」任务与高度依赖已学词义的任务比较。

words.enDefinition: an observed historical rise in average performance on some intelligence tests across successive cohorts in many populations

examples.en: The lecture shows the Flynn effect using older and newer score distributions from the same hypothetical population.
examples.zh: 讲义用同一假设群体较早和较新的分数分布说明「弗林效应」。

examples.en: We discussed the Flynn effect while noting that trends can differ across tests, locations and calendar periods.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「弗林效应」，并指出趋势可随测验、地区与年代不同而变化。

collocations: changes associated with the Flynn effect

words.enDefinition: an everyday convention with relatively mild social consequences for violating it

examples.en: The classroom example describes greeting people in a customary way as a folkway with informal enforcement.
examples.zh: 课堂示例把按习惯问候他人描述为一种以非正式方式维持的「民俗规范」。

examples.en: We discussed a folkway by comparing responses to breaking it with responses to breaking a serious rule.
examples.zh: 我们通过比较违反一种「民俗规范」和违反严重规则时得到的反应，讨论这种习惯。

words.enDefinition: Item requiring selection between alternatives instead of independent ratings for each

examples.en: In the exercise, each forced-choice item asks students to choose between two statements.
examples.zh: 在练习中，每道「强迫选择题」要求学生在两项陈述之间作选择。

examples.en: The worksheet compares ratings of both statements with a single forced-choice item.
examples.zh: 习题比较了对两个陈述分别评分与做一道「强迫选择题」的区别。

words.enDefinition: the application of psychological knowledge and methods to questions arising in legal and justice settings

examples.en: The forensic psychology lecture examined how memory research can inform discussion of a fictional witness account.
examples.zh: 「司法心理学」讲义考察记忆研究如何为讨论一份虚构证人陈述提供依据。

examples.en: We explored forensic psychology through a classroom comparison of psychological questions and legal decision standards.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂上对照心理学问题与法律决定标准，以认识「司法心理学」。

words.enDefinition: Graph showing how retention of learned information changes as time passes

examples.en: Our group sketched a forgetting curve from the simulated recall scores across several days.
examples.zh: 我们组根据几天的模拟回忆分数画了一条「遗忘曲线」。

examples.en: The textbook compares the first steep drop with the flatter part of the forgetting curve.
examples.zh: 教材把「遗忘曲线」开头的陡降与之后较平缓的部分相比较。

words.enDefinition: a concept whose membership is set by explicit criteria, as with many mathematical categories

examples.en: The geometry example illustrates a formal concept by listing the precise properties required of every category member.
examples.zh: 几何示例列出各类别成员必须具备的精确性质，用来说明「形式概念」。

examples.en: We tested the boundary of the formal concept by checking whether the new shape satisfied each rule.
examples.zh: 我们逐条核对新图形是否符合规则，以检验「形式概念」的边界。

words.enDefinition: an expectation for conduct explicitly stated in a rule, policy or other official form

examples.en: The signed classroom policy provides an example of a formal norm governing use of shared equipment.
examples.zh: 签署的课堂政策是约束共享设备使用的「正式规范」的一个例子。

examples.en: We identified a formal norm by checking which expectation appeared in the fictional group's written policy.
examples.zh: 我们查阅虚构群体的书面政策，确认哪项行为要求属于「正式规范」。

words.enDefinition: Piaget's proposed stage involving increasingly systematic reasoning about abstract relations and hypothetical possibilities

examples.en: The reading illustrates the formal operational stage with a fictional learner reasoning about cases that could never occur.
examples.zh: 阅读材料以虚构学习者对不可能发生的情形进行推理为例，说明「形式运算阶段」。

examples.en: We discussed how tasks differed in abstract demands when evaluating claims about the formal operational stage.
examples.zh: 我们在评估有关「形式运算阶段」的主张时，讨论各任务在抽象要求上怎样不同。

collocations: reasoning in the formal operational stage

words.enDefinition: a change in judgment or choice caused by different presentations of substantively equivalent information

examples.en: The framing effect appeared when two equivalent descriptions led the fictional groups to choose different options.
examples.zh: 两种等价描述导致虚构小组选择了不同选项，出现了「框架效应」。

examples.en: We compared the choices under both wordings to estimate the framing effect in the simulated survey.
examples.zh: 我们对照两种措辞下所作的选择，估计模拟调查中的「框架效应」。

words.enDefinition: Retrieval of studied items without specific cues or a required order

examples.en: In the free recall task, students list remembered words in any order.
examples.zh: 在「自由回忆」任务中，学生可以按任意顺序写下记得的单词。

examples.en: We chose free recall because the exercise focused on remembering items without hints.
examples.zh: 因为练习关注没有提示时能想起哪些项目，我们选用了「自由回忆」。

words.enDefinition: conduct presented to an audience in accordance with the expectations of a particular social setting

examples.en: The diagram describes greeting visitors at the desk as front-stage behavior in the fictional service setting.
examples.zh: 示意图把虚构服务情境中在柜台问候来访者的做法描述为「前台行为」。

examples.en: We examined changes in front-stage behavior when a second audience arrived in the classroom vignette.
examples.zh: 课堂短情景中，第二批观众到来时，我们考察「前台行为」发生的变化。

words.enDefinition: difficulty seeing a familiar object as useful in ways different from its usual function

examples.en: The example illustrates functional fixedness when the learner overlooks that a box could also support a small object.
examples.zh: 当学习者没想到盒子也能支撑一个小物体时，示例说明了「功能固着」。

examples.en: We compared two presentations of the same materials to see which one produced less functional fixedness in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们比较呈现同样材料的两种方式，观察哪种引起的「功能固着」程度较低。

words.enDefinition: an early approach investigating what mental activities and behaviors do for an organism in its environment

examples.en: The history lecture relates functionalism to questions about how habits help people adapt to changing situations.
examples.zh: 心理学史讲义将「机能主义心理学」与习惯如何帮助人们适应变化情境的问题联系起来。

examples.en: We introduced functionalism by asking what role a particular mental process serves during a routine task.
examples.zh: 我们询问某一心理过程在常规任务中起什么作用，由此介绍「机能主义心理学」。

words.enDefinition: The tendency to overemphasise personal dispositions and underestimate situational influences when explaining other people's behaviour.

examples.en: The seminar discusses fundamental attribution error when observers in a fictional scenario overlook a changed timetable.
examples.zh: 研讨课讨论「基本归因错误」时，给出了虚构观察者忽视日程变动的一幕。

examples.en: Our case note asks which missed situational detail could explain the apparent fundamental attribution error in the example.
examples.zh: 案例笔记询问，哪个被忽视的情境细节可能解释示例中疑似的「基本归因错误」。

words.enDefinition: one's perception of the time and opportunities remaining in the future

examples.en: The classroom task assessed future time perspective by asking how open or limited the fictional person's future seemed.
examples.zh: 课堂任务通过询问虚构人物的未来看起来有多开放或有限，考察「未来时间视角」。

examples.en: We discussed how a change in future time perspective could alter priorities in the sample developmental model.
examples.zh: 我们讨论样例发展模型中，「未来时间视角」的改变怎样可能影响优先事项。

words.enDefinition: wording that emphasizes what is gained, retained or achieved relative to a reference point

examples.en: The gain frame described how many places would remain available in the fictional choice about a workshop.
examples.zh: 在关于工作坊的虚构选择题里，「收益框架」描述将保留多少座位。

examples.en: We rewrote the outcome using a gain frame while keeping the numbers equivalent to the first version.
examples.zh: 我们用「收益框架」改写结果，同时保持数字所传达的结果与第一版等价。

collocations: compare a gain frame with a loss frame

words.enDefinition: the mistaken belief that a run of outcomes makes the opposite outcome more likely on a new independent trial

examples.en: The student illustrated the gambler's fallacy by predicting tails just because the simulated coin repeatedly showed heads.
examples.zh: 学生仅因模拟硬币连续出现正面便预测下次会出现反面，说明了「赌徒谬误」。

examples.en: We discussed the gambler's fallacy after confirming that each spin in the classroom model was independent.
examples.zh: 在确认课堂模型中每次转动彼此独立后，我们讨论了「赌徒谬误」。

words.enDefinition: a sentence that encourages an initial grammatical interpretation which later words force the reader to revise

examples.en: The garden-path sentence made readers reinterpret the opening phrase after encountering an unexpected verb in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中，读者遇到一个意外的动词后，「花园路径句」使他们重新理解开头短语。

examples.en: We recorded longer reading times at the point where the garden-path sentence first contradicted the initial interpretation.
examples.zh: 「花园路径句」首次与读者最初解读不符的位置，记录到的阅读时间更长。

words.enDefinition: a statistical factor proposed to explain the positive correlations often observed across different cognitive test performances

examples.en: The textbook model represents the general intelligence factor as a shared influence across several kinds of tasks.
examples.zh: 教材模型把「一般智力因素」表示为几种不同任务中的共同影响。

examples.en: We linked the general intelligence factor to the pattern of positive score correlations in the synthetic table.
examples.zh: 我们将「一般智力因素」与合成表中各得分呈正相关的模式相联系。

collocations: evidence for a general intelligence factor

words.enDefinition: Framework for separating sources of score variation across multiple measurement conditions

examples.en: The lecture uses generalizability theory to examine variation across tasks and raters together.
examples.zh: 讲座用「概化理论」同时考察不同任务和评分者带来的波动。

examples.en: We compared a generalizability theory example with an analysis assuming one undifferentiated error source.
examples.zh: 我们比较了一个「概化理论」示例和一个将误差来源合在一起分析的例子。

words.enDefinition: Pattern relating response strength to similarity with a learned cue

examples.en: The generalization gradient peaks at the original shade and falls toward the other colors.
examples.zh: 「泛化梯度」在原来的色调处达到峰值，向其他颜色逐渐下降。

examples.en: Our team plotted the generalization gradient using the response scores from the simulation.
examples.zh: 我们组用模拟中的反应分数画出了「泛化梯度」。

words.enDefinition: in Mead's theory, the organized expectations of a broader group that a person takes into account when acting

examples.en: The learner's reference to what teammates normally expect illustrates the generalized other in the fictional group activity.
examples.zh: 在虚构小组活动中，学习者提到队友通常有什么预期，说明了「概化他人」。

examples.en: We identified the generalized other when the example referred to group rules shared beyond any single relationship.
examples.zh: 示例涉及不限于某段个人关系的群体共有规则时，我们辨认出「概化他人」。

collocations: take the perspective of the generalized other

words.enDefinition: Memory advantage for information learners produce themselves rather than simply read

examples.en: The worksheet illustrates the generation effect by comparing completed words with words already printed.
examples.zh: 习题比较自行补全的单词和已经印全的单词，以说明「生成效应」。

examples.en: We discussed the generation effect after examining recall for answers students generated themselves.
examples.zh: 我们考察学生自己得出的答案在回忆中的表现后，讨论了「生成效应」。

words.enDefinition: Erikson's proposed adult conflict involving contribution to later generations or experiencing a lack of such engagement

examples.en: The lecture connects generativity versus stagnation with whether the fictional adult contributes to the next generation's development.
examples.zh: 讲义将「关怀下一代对停滞」与虚构成人是否为下一代的发展作出贡献联系起来。

examples.en: We identified generativity versus stagnation as the theme linking teaching and community contributions in the theoretical example.
examples.zh: 我们在理论示例中将「关怀下一代对停滞」识别为联系教学与社区贡献的主题。

words.enDefinition: General tendencies governing how people group elements and organize perceptual scenes.

examples.en: We used the Gestalt principles of perception to explain why the same dots formed different groups.
examples.zh: 我们用「格式塔知觉原则」解释为何同样的圆点形成了不同分组。

examples.en: The tutor reviewed the Gestalt principles of perception before showing a drawing with an ambiguous foreground.
examples.zh: 辅导老师先复习「格式塔知觉原则」，再展示一幅前景难以确定的图。

collocations: examples of Gestalt principles of perception

words.enDefinition: a school of psychology emphasizing how elements are organized into meaningful perceptual or mental wholes

examples.en: The introduction to Gestalt psychology used an incomplete figure that viewers tended to organize as a whole.
examples.zh: 「格式塔心理学」导论使用了一幅不完整图形，观看者倾向于将其组织成一个整体。

examples.en: We connected Gestalt psychology with the impression of a pattern that emerges from several separate marks.
examples.zh: 我们将「格式塔心理学」与从多个独立记号中产生整体图案印象的现象联系起来。

words.enDefinition: A theory linking consciousness to information becoming widely available to otherwise specialized cognitive processes.

examples.en: Under global workspace theory, information about a visible symbol can become available beyond initial visual processing.
examples.zh: 按「全局工作空间理论」，可见符号的信息可以供初步视觉加工之外的其他过程使用。

examples.en: The seminar compared global workspace theory with another account of how experiences become available for report.
examples.zh: 讨论课比较了「全局工作空间理论」与另一种解释体验如何能够被报告的理论。

collocations: an account from global workspace theory
a prediction of global workspace theory

words.enDefinition: the configuration a solver is trying to reach, as defined in the representation of a problem

examples.en: The diagram labels the goal state as the arrangement in which every colored piece reaches its destination.
examples.zh: 图中将每个彩色拼块都到达指定位置的布局标为「目标状态」。

examples.en: We traced two different paths from the same starting arrangement to the goal state in the worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们在练习中追踪从同一初始布局到「目标状态」的两条不同路径。

words.enDefinition: The tendency to group edge segments forming a smooth path.

examples.en: The crossing lines demonstrated good continuation because the smooth paths looked like two uninterrupted strokes.
examples.zh: 交叉线条说明了「良好连续原则」，因为两条平滑走向各自看起来都是连贯的一笔。

examples.en: We discussed good continuation after comparing a smooth path with an abrupt turn at the crossing.
examples.zh: 在交叉点比较了平缓路径和急转弯后，我们讨论了「良好连续原则」。

words.enDefinition: the degree to which environmental demands and support match an individual's temperament or other characteristics

examples.en: The example improved goodness of fit in development by changing the pace of transitions for a fictional learner.
examples.zh: 示例通过改变虚构学习者在各活动间转换的节奏，提高「发展中的适配度」。

examples.en: We compared goodness of fit in development across two classroom contexts with different expectations for participation.
examples.zh: 我们对照对参与有不同预期的两个课堂情境中的「发展中的适配度」。

collocations: assess goodness of fit in development
consider goodness of fit in development
improve goodness of fit in development

words.enDefinition: Item response model using cumulative probabilities for ordered response categories

examples.en: The workbook uses a graded response model for the fictional scale's ordered answer categories.
examples.zh: 练习册对虚构量表中的有序答案类别采用了「等级反应模型」。

examples.en: We discussed how a graded response model describes the probability of choosing higher categories.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「等级反应模型」如何描述选择较高类别的概率。

collocations: assumptions of the graded response model
thresholds in a graded response model

words.enDefinition: development of abilities involving large muscle groups and coordinated whole-body movement

examples.en: The classroom chart illustrates gross motor development with changes in balance during fictional play and movement activities.
examples.zh: 课堂图用虚构游戏和运动活动中平衡能力的变化，说明「大运动发展」。

examples.en: We placed walking and jumping under gross motor development on the graphic organizing childhood skills.
examples.zh: 我们在整理儿童技能的图中，将走路和跳跃归入「大运动发展」。

words.enDefinition: The strength of the bonds and commitment that help keep members of a group together.

examples.en: The classroom vignette illustrates group cohesion through a fictional team's continued commitment to a shared campus project.
examples.zh: 课堂材料以虚构团队对一项共同校园项目持续投入的例子说明「群体凝聚力」。

examples.en: Our discussion asks whether group cohesion changed as the fictional team began sharing responsibility for the exhibition.
examples.zh: 讨论询问，虚构团队开始共同承担展览工作后，「群体凝聚力」是否发生了变化。

words.enDefinition: The degree to which someone experiences a particular group membership as an important part of who they are.

examples.en: The fictional questionnaire illustrates group identification using students' reports about their connection to a campus art society.
examples.zh: 虚构问卷用学生们对自己与校园艺术社团联系的自述说明「群体身份认同」。

examples.en: Our seminar separates group identification from simply being listed as a member in the fictional meeting records.
examples.zh: 研讨课把「群体身份认同」与仅在虚构会议记录上被列为成员区别开。

words.enDefinition: A shift after group discussion toward a more extreme position in the direction of the group's initial inclination.

examples.en: The textbook uses group polarization to describe fictional ratings that become more strongly favourable after a discussion.
examples.zh: 教材用「群体极化」描述经过讨论后变得更为积极的虚构评分。

examples.en: Our class compares initial and final preferences before discussing whether group polarization occurred in the fictional committee.
examples.zh: 全班先比较最初与最终的偏好，再讨论虚构委员会是否发生了「群体极化」。

words.enDefinition: A proposed group decision pattern in which pressure for agreement discourages scrutiny of alternatives and concerns.

examples.en: The seminar illustrates groupthink with a fictional committee that sets aside alternatives before evaluating them carefully.
examples.zh: 研讨课用虚构委员会尚未仔细评估就搁置备选方案的例子来说明「群体迷思」。

examples.en: Our textbook treats groupthink as a possible explanation for the omissions in the fictional meeting notes.
examples.zh: 教材把「群体迷思」视为虚构会议记录出现遗漏的一种可能解释。

words.enDefinition: An item response model parameter representing the lower asymptote of the probability of a correct response.

examples.en: The sample model uses a guessing parameter to represent the curve's lower limit.
examples.zh: 示例模型用「猜测参数」表示答对概率曲线的下限。

examples.en: We discussed why a guessing parameter does not identify who actually guessed.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么「猜测参数」不能辨认出谁确实是猜的。

collocations: lower asymptote determined by the guessing parameter

words.enDefinition: learning through involvement in a shared activity supported by a more experienced person or community

examples.en: The reading describes guided participation as the child takes a small role in a shared planning activity.
examples.zh: 阅读材料把儿童在共同规划活动中承担一小部分任务描述为「引导式参与」。

examples.en: We compared guided participation with independent practice using two examples of the same classroom activity.
examples.zh: 我们用同一课堂活动的两个示例，对照「引导式参与」与独立练习。

collocations: guided participation in a shared activity

words.enDefinition: Declining response to a repeated stimulus through a learning process

examples.en: In the simulation, habituation shows up as a weaker response to each identical tone.
examples.zh: 在模拟中，「习惯化」表现为对每次相同音调的反应越来越弱。

examples.en: The student asked whether the declining response reflected habituation or temporary fatigue.
examples.zh: 学生问，反应减弱究竟反映了「习惯化」还是短暂疲劳。

words.enDefinition: a research design that measures declining responses across repeated exposure and tests whether a different stimulus renews responding in suitable comparisons

examples.en: The lecture's habituation paradigm graph shows looking time decreasing before a novel picture is presented in the example.
examples.zh: 讲义的「习惯化范式」图显示，示例中呈现新图片之前，注视时间逐渐减少。

examples.en: We compared response recovery across two fictional conditions using the classroom illustration of a habituation paradigm.
examples.zh: 我们依据课堂的「习惯化范式」示意图，比较两种虚构条件下反应恢复的情况。

collocations: interpret results from a habituation paradigm

words.enDefinition: in Bourdieu's theory, durable learned dispositions through which social experience shapes perception and action

examples.en: The seminar uses habitus to explain why certain classroom routines felt immediately familiar to some fictional learners.
examples.zh: 研讨课用「惯习」解释为什么某些课堂惯例让部分虚构学习者立刻感到熟悉。

examples.en: We discussed how habitus could shape everyday choices without requiring a conscious rule for each choice in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们讨论「惯习」怎样影响日常选择，而每项选择无须遵循一条有意识的规则。

words.enDefinition: A tendency for a favourable overall impression or quality to influence judgments of other characteristics.

examples.en: The class illustrates the halo effect by comparing unrelated ratings of the same fictional club member.
examples.zh: 课堂比较了对同一虚构社团成员若干无关特征的评分，用来说明「光环效应」。

examples.en: In our example, the halo effect could explain why a positive impression coloured judgments about unrelated qualities.
examples.zh: 在示例中，「光环效应」可能解释为什么良好的总体印象影响了对无关特征的判断。

words.enDefinition: the study of how psychological and social processes relate to health behavior, illness and care

examples.en: The health psychology example compared how two groups understood the same fictional messages about physical activity.
examples.zh: 「健康心理学」示例对比两个小组如何理解有关体力活动的相同虚构信息。

examples.en: We reviewed a health psychology study asking how social support relates to reported habits over time.
examples.zh: 我们回顾一项「健康心理学」研究，它考察社会支持与一段时间内所报告习惯的关系。

words.enDefinition: An action intended to provide assistance to someone who needs or could benefit from it.

examples.en: The classroom vignette illustrates helping behaviour when a fictional student offers to carry some shared materials.
examples.zh: 课堂材料用虚构学生主动提出帮忙搬运部分共用材料这一幕说明「助人行为」。

examples.en: The tutor counted instances of helping behaviour in fictional accounts of a busy studio session.
examples.zh: 老师统计了关于一场繁忙工作室活动的虚构记述中出现了几次「助人行为」。

words.enDefinition: a simplifying rule or shortcut used to make a judgment or search for a solution

examples.en: The participants used a heuristic to narrow the options before checking the details of the remaining choices.
examples.zh: 参与者先用一条「启发式规则」缩小选项范围，再核对剩余选项的细节。

examples.en: We examined when the heuristic saved time and when it led to a systematic error in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们考察这条「启发式规则」何时节省时间、何时导致系统性误差。

words.enDefinition: A six-domain model of personality that includes Honesty-Humility alongside five other broad factors.

examples.en: The personality seminar compares the HEXACO model with the Big Five using separate charts for each framework.
examples.zh: 人格研讨课用两张分别展示各框架的图比较「HEXACO人格六因素模型」与大五人格。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which domain gives the HEXACO model its first letter in the written acronym.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，「HEXACO人格六因素模型」的缩写中第一个字母对应什么维度。

words.enDefinition: the implicit expectations, values and behavior learned through schooling beyond the formal subject content

examples.en: The example identifies waiting for permission to speak as part of a hidden curriculum in the fictional classroom.
examples.zh: 示例把先等到允许再发言，认作虚构课堂「隐性课程」的一部分。

examples.en: We compared the hidden curriculum with goals stated explicitly in the teacher's written lesson plan in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们将「隐性课程」与老师书面教案明示的目标作比较。

words.enDefinition: A model in which broad personality traits are organised above groups of more specific traits.

examples.en: The diagram introduces a hierarchical trait model by connecting each broad domain with several more specific tendencies.
examples.zh: 示意图把各宽泛维度和几项更具体的倾向联系起来，介绍了「层级特质模型」。

examples.en: In our classroom example, a hierarchical trait model places similar tendencies together without treating them as identical.
examples.zh: 在课堂示例中，「层级特质模型」把相似倾向归在一起，同时保留它们之间的区别。

collocations: levels of a hierarchical trait model

words.enDefinition: Learning in which an established conditioned cue supports conditioning of another cue

examples.en: The chart illustrates higher-order conditioning by adding a second cue after the first is learned.
examples.zh: 图表用学会第一个线索后加入第二个线索来说明「高阶条件作用」。

examples.en: Our lecturer distinguished higher-order conditioning from repeating the original pair of events.
examples.zh: 老师区分了「高阶条件作用」与反复呈现最初的一对事件。

words.enDefinition: a search strategy that repeatedly chooses a move that immediately improves an evaluation of progress toward the goal

examples.en: The hill-climbing heuristic chose the move that looked closest to the goal on each step of the exercise.
examples.zh: 「爬山启发式」在练习的每一步都选择看起来最接近目标的操作。

examples.en: We used the graph to show where a hill-climbing heuristic could stop at an inferior local solution.
examples.zh: 我们用图说明「爬山启发式」可能停在较差的局部解上。

words.enDefinition: the tendency to view an outcome as more predictable after learning that it occurred

examples.en: The class demonstrated hindsight bias when learners rated the revealed result as more obvious than they had beforehand.
examples.zh: 结果揭晓后，学习者认为结果比事前预想的更明显，课堂上由此展示了「事后偏差」。

examples.en: We measured hindsight bias by asking separate groups to estimate predictability before and after reading the outcome.
examples.zh: 我们让不同小组在看到结果前后评估它的可预测性，以测量「事后偏差」。

words.enDefinition: The proportion of signal-present trials correctly answered with a signal report.

examples.en: We calculated the hit rate using only trials that actually contained the faint classroom tone.
examples.zh: 我们只统计确实播放了课堂微弱音调的试次，计算「命中率」。

examples.en: A higher hit rate did not settle which simulated listener was more sensitive in the example.
examples.zh: 在例题中，更高的「命中率」无法单独确定哪位模拟听者更敏感。

words.enDefinition: The drive for sleep that generally builds during wakefulness and declines during sleep.

examples.en: The classroom model showed homeostatic sleep pressure increasing over the simulated period of wakefulness before bedtime.
examples.zh: 课堂模型显示，睡前模拟清醒期内，「稳态睡眠压力」逐步上升。

examples.en: We compared homeostatic sleep pressure before and after the sleep interval shown on the model's graph.
examples.zh: 我们比较了模型图中睡眠时段前后的「稳态睡眠压力」。

collocations: a build-up of homeostatic sleep pressure
a model of homeostatic sleep pressure

words.enDefinition: In the HEXACO model, a domain including tendencies toward sincerity, fairness, modesty, and lower interest in status or material gain.

examples.en: The personal qualities chart uses Honesty-Humility to group several related characteristics in the fictional classroom profiles.
examples.zh: 个人品质图用「诚实—谦逊」把虚构课堂画像中的几种相关特征归在一起。

examples.en: Our class compares Honesty-Humility with another HEXACO dimension by reading the descriptions side by side.
examples.zh: 全班并排阅读维度描述，将「诚实—谦逊」与另一个 HEXACO 维度作比较。

words.enDefinition: movement between social positions of approximately similar rank under the framework being used

examples.en: The lecture uses horizontal mobility to describe an occupational change within the same status bracket.
examples.zh: 课堂用「水平流动」描述地位层级相同的职业变动。

examples.en: We compared horizontal mobility with a move to a visibly higher position in the fictional ranking exercise.
examples.zh: 我们将「水平流动」与虚构排序练习中转往明显较高地位的变动作比较。

words.enDefinition: A tendency for an unfavourable impression or quality to influence judgments of other characteristics negatively.

examples.en: The fictional case illustrates the horns effect when one unfavourable impression lowers ratings on several unrelated qualities.
examples.zh: 虚构案例中，一种负面印象拉低对几项无关特征的评价，用以说明「负面光环效应」。

examples.en: Our classroom discussion asks whether the horns effect could explain the pattern reported in the fictional ratings.
examples.zh: 课堂讨论询问，「负面光环效应」能否解释虚构评分呈现的模式。

collocations: ratings affected by the horns effect

words.enDefinition: an approach emphasizing personal agency, subjective experience and the capacity for psychological growth

examples.en: The historical reading links humanistic psychology with the student's interest in choice, meaning and personal growth.
examples.zh: 历史阅读材料将「人本主义心理学」与例中学生对选择、意义及个人成长的关切联系起来。

examples.en: We read an example of humanistic psychology that centered on the fictional person's own account of experience.
examples.zh: 我们阅读了一个以虚构人物本人对其经历的叙述为中心的「人本主义心理学」示例。

words.enDefinition: A graph showing how sleep stages change over a recording.

examples.en: The lecturer used a hypnogram to show how sleep stages changed across the fictional night.
examples.zh: 老师用「睡眠分期图」展示了虚构的一整夜中睡眠阶段如何变化。

examples.en: We read the time axis of the hypnogram before comparing the duration of the marked stages.
examples.zh: 我们先看「睡眠分期图」的时间轴，再比较标出的各阶段的持续时间。

words.enDefinition: proposing hypotheses, deducing predictions from each and comparing predictions with observations

examples.en: The classroom example uses hypothetico-deductive reasoning to derive distinct predictions from two alternative explanations of the pattern.
examples.zh: 课堂示例用「假设演绎推理」，从该模式的两种不同解释推出不同的预测。

examples.en: We followed the steps of hypothetico-deductive reasoning before comparing the expected outcomes with the supplied observations.
examples.zh: 我们先依次完成「假设演绎推理」的各步，再将预期结果与给出的观察对照。

words.enDefinition: Very brief retention of visual information after a display disappears

examples.en: The slide uses a brief letter display to illustrate iconic memory in class.
examples.zh: 课堂幻灯片用短暂显示的字母来说明「图像记忆」。

examples.en: We discussed how the delay in a simulated task affects measures of iconic memory.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了模拟任务中的延迟会如何影响对「图像记忆」的测量。

words.enDefinition: in Weberian sociology, an analytical model emphasizing selected features for comparison with complex actual cases

examples.en: The reading uses an ideal type of organization as a comparison point for the two fictional cases.
examples.zh: 阅读材料用组织的「理想类型」作为两项虚构案例的比较基准。

examples.en: We discussed why an ideal type could be useful even though neither example matched every feature in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们讨论即使两例都不符合每一项特征，「理想类型」为何仍有用途。

collocations: compare a case with an ideal type

words.enDefinition: in Marcia's framework, an identity status involving a commitment made after meaningful exploration of alternatives

examples.en: The example classifies a fictional learner's plan as identity achievement after documented exploration and a clear eventual commitment.
examples.zh: 示例将留有探索记录并最终形成明确承诺的虚构学习者计划归为「认同达成」。

examples.en: We discussed identity achievement separately for each domain rather than labeling the entire fictional person with one status.
examples.zh: 我们分别讨论各个领域的「认同达成」，虚构人物在不同领域可以处于不同状态。

words.enDefinition: a relatively stable choice and investment in particular values, roles or goals as part of one's identity

examples.en: The interview excerpt illustrates identity commitment when the fictional student describes a decision and continued investment in it.
examples.zh: 访谈节选中，虚构学生描述一个决定并持续投入，体现了「认同承诺」。

examples.en: We identified identity commitment in the worksheet after the participant described which goals they had decided to pursue.
examples.zh: 练习里的参与者描述已经决定追求的目标后，我们辨认出「认同承诺」。

words.enDefinition: in Marcia's framework, an identity status with little active exploration and little commitment in a given domain

examples.en: The classroom chart places identity diffusion in the example with low exploration and low commitment about career plans.
examples.zh: 课堂表将职业规划上探索和承诺都低的示例归入「认同弥散」。

examples.en: We interpreted identity diffusion for the stated domain rather than assuming the same pattern applied to all domains.
examples.zh: 我们按题设领域解读「认同弥散」，不同领域可以出现不同模式。

words.enDefinition: trying out values, roles and commitments while forming an identity

examples.en: The fictional student showed identity exploration by considering several academic pathways before deciding which held personal meaning.
examples.zh: 虚构学生先思考几条学业道路，再判断哪条对自己有意义，表现出「认同探索」。

examples.en: We compared identity exploration with having already decided which commitments to keep in the developmental model.
examples.zh: 在发展模型中，我们将「认同探索」与已经决定保留哪些承诺作对照。

words.enDefinition: in Marcia's framework, commitment to an identity choice without substantial prior exploration

examples.en: The discussion illustrates identity foreclosure when a fictional student commits to a plan without considering available alternatives.
examples.zh: 讨论情形中，虚构学生未考虑可选替代方案就确定计划，体现了「认同早闭」。

examples.en: We compared identity foreclosure with an equally strong commitment reached after exploration in a second classroom example.
examples.zh: 我们将「认同早闭」与第二个课堂示例中探索后形成的同等强度的承诺对照。

words.enDefinition: in Marcia's framework, an identity status in which active exploration continues without a settled commitment in the domain

examples.en: The worksheet describes identity moratorium when a fictional learner actively considers several options and postpones a final decision.
examples.zh: 习题中，虚构学习者积极考虑若干选项并暂缓最终决定，示例将其称为「认同延缓」。

examples.en: We marked identity moratorium as high in exploration and low in commitment on the class matrix.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂矩阵中把「认同延缓」标为高探索、低承诺。

words.enDefinition: Erikson's conflict between building a coherent self and feeling lost about roles

examples.en: The reading describes identity versus role confusion through a fictional young person considering different commitments about study.
examples.zh: 阅读材料通过一个虚构年轻人考虑不同学业承诺的情形，描述「认同对角色混乱」。

examples.en: We discussed identity versus role confusion in relation to adolescent exploration on Erikson's theoretical timeline in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们在埃里克森的理论时间线上联系青少年探索，讨论「认同对角色混乱」。

collocations: stage of identity versus role confusion
challenge of identity versus role confusion

words.enDefinition: a problem whose goals, allowable steps or criteria for a satisfactory answer are not fully specified

examples.en: The assignment presented an ill-defined problem because groups had to decide for themselves what success would mean.
examples.zh: 作业给出了一个「界定模糊的问题」，因为各小组必须自行确定成功意味着什么。

examples.en: We compared an ill-defined problem about designing a shared space with a puzzle having a single correct solution.
examples.zh: 我们把设计共享空间的「界定模糊的问题」与只有一个正确答案的谜题作比较。

words.enDefinition: overestimating one's ability to influence outcomes that are largely or wholly outside one's control

examples.en: The illusion of control appeared when participants thought choosing a card position changed a simulated random outcome.
examples.zh: 参与者认为选择卡片位置会改变模拟的随机结果，出现了「控制错觉」。

examples.en: We discussed the illusion of control after comparing perceived influence with the rules of the classroom game.
examples.zh: 我们将感知到的影响力与课堂游戏规则对比后，讨论了「控制错觉」。

collocations: illusion of control over chance events

words.enDefinition: A tendency to overestimate the extent to which others can detect one's private thoughts or feelings.

examples.en: The class discusses the illusion of transparency after comparing a fictional speaker's feelings with reported audience impressions.
examples.zh: 全班对照虚构发言者的感受与报告所列的听众印象，然后讨论「透明度错觉」。

examples.en: Our tutorial illustrates the illusion of transparency using a character who assumes their surprise is immediately apparent.
examples.zh: 辅导课以一名认为自己的惊讶马上会被看出来的角色，说明「透明度错觉」。

collocations: example of the illusion of transparency

words.enDefinition: A perceived edge lacking a corresponding physical boundary in the stimulus.

examples.en: The classroom triangle produced an illusory contour where there was no line drawn on the page.
examples.zh: 课堂上的三角形图案在纸上未画线的位置产生了「主观轮廓」。

examples.en: Students traced an illusory contour around the white region even though its brightness never changed along that edge.
examples.zh: 即使白色区域在那条边两侧的亮度一样，学生仍描出了它的「主观轮廓」。

words.enDefinition: in Elkind's account of adolescent egocentrism, the belief that others closely notice or judge one's appearance or actions

examples.en: The example describes an imaginary audience when a fictional teenager expects classmates to notice a barely visible change.
examples.zh: 虚构青少年预期同学会注意到一个几乎不可见的变化，示例由此描述了「假想观众」。

examples.en: We discussed the imaginary audience separately from actual attention received in the classroom story about self-consciousness.
examples.zh: 在有关自我意识的课堂故事中，我们把「假想观众」和实际受到的关注分别讨论。

words.enDefinition: Retrieval attempted directly after presentation or study of the target material

examples.en: The instructor recorded immediate recall as soon as the study list disappeared.
examples.zh: 学习列表一消失，老师就记录了「即时回忆」的表现。

examples.en: We compared immediate recall with performance after completing another short classroom activity.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「即时回忆」与完成另一项简短课堂活动后的表现。

words.enDefinition: An evaluation that operates relatively automatically and may not be accessible to conscious report.

examples.en: The seminar discusses an implicit attitude by comparing two kinds of information in a fictional research summary.
examples.zh: 研讨课对照虚构研究摘要中的两种信息，讨论一种「内隐态度」。

examples.en: Our tutor notes that the fictional records about an implicit attitude are interpreted as indirect evidence of evaluation.
examples.zh: 老师提醒，虚构档案中有关「内隐态度」的资料被理解为对评价的间接证据。

words.enDefinition: Acquisition of patterns or rules without conscious awareness of that knowledge

examples.en: The implicit learning task tests whether people pick up patterns they cannot describe.
examples.zh: 「内隐学习」任务检验人们能否习得自己说不出的规律。

examples.en: Our seminar used a mock sequence game to discuss evidence for implicit learning.
examples.zh: 研讨课用模拟序列游戏讨论「内隐学习」的证据。

words.enDefinition: Effects of previous experience on performance without conscious retrieval of that experience

examples.en: The model illustrates implicit memory when earlier exposure changes performance without deliberate remembering.
examples.zh: 模型用先前接触影响表现而没有刻意回忆的情形说明「内隐记忆」。

examples.en: We compared evidence for implicit memory with the participants' reports of remembered items.
examples.zh: 我们把「内隐记忆」的证据与参与者报告记得的项目作了比较。

words.enDefinition: A person's informal assumptions about which personality characteristics are likely to go together.

examples.en: The handout illustrates implicit personality theory through a fictional student's assumption that cheerful people are also outgoing.
examples.zh: 讲义借虚构学生认为开朗的人也很外向这一假设，说明「内隐人格理论」。

examples.en: Our discussion of implicit personality theory considers how a reader connects traits that are never explicitly linked.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「内隐人格理论」时，探讨了读者怎样把未曾明确关联的特质联系起来。

collocations: assumptions in an implicit personality theory

words.enDefinition: The process of combining information about a person to develop an overall impression of them.

examples.en: The worksheet illustrates impression formation by presenting students with several descriptions of the same fictional person.
examples.zh: 练习单向学生提供同一虚构人物的几种描述，用以说明「印象形成」。

examples.en: Our discussion of impression formation considers which details students treated as most relevant in the written exercise.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「印象形成」时，探讨了学生在书面练习中认为哪些细节最相关。

words.enDefinition: Revising an existing view of a person in light of new information.

examples.en: The fictional diary describes impression updating after a later scene provided information missing from the opening chapter.
examples.zh: 虚构日记描述了「印象更新」，因为后来的情节补充了开篇一章缺失的信息。

examples.en: Our exercise compares impression updating after a single counterexample with revisions after several fictional observations over time.
examples.zh: 练习比较了一个反例后发生的「印象更新」和经过多次虚构观察后作出的修正。

words.enDefinition: A tendency to evaluate or treat members of one's own group more favourably than comparable outsiders.

examples.en: Students rate similar contributions more favourably when they come from their own team, illustrating in-group favouritism.
examples.zh: 学生对贡献相近的两队评价有别，给本队打分更高，体现了「内群体偏好」。

examples.en: Our class asks whether the comparison offers evidence of in-group favouritism in the fictional art clubs.
examples.zh: 全班讨论，该比较能否为虚构艺术社团存在「内群体偏好」提供证据。

words.enDefinition: A conditional commitment to publish a Registered Report after satisfactory review of its research plan.

examples.en: The fictional journal offered in-principle acceptance after reviewing the research plan and before seeing any results.
examples.zh: 虚构期刊审阅研究计划后，在看到结果以前给出了「原则性接收」。

examples.en: We discussed which requirements still applied after in-principle acceptance in the classroom example of a Registered Report.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了课堂注册报告示例获得「原则性接收」后还有哪些要求适用。

words.enDefinition: Failure to notice a visible unexpected item while attention is directed elsewhere.

examples.en: Inattentional blindness explained why some viewers missed the extra shape while counting events elsewhere in the clip.
examples.zh: 「非注意盲视」解释了为什么一些观众在数片段中其他位置的事件时，漏看了额外图形。

examples.en: The tutor distinguished inattentional blindness from a failure to see because an item was physically hidden.
examples.zh: 辅导老师区分了「非注意盲视」与物体实际被遮住而看不见的情况。

words.enDefinition: Acquisition of information without an intention to learn that information

examples.en: Our reading exercise measured incidental learning for words that nobody expected to be tested on.
examples.zh: 阅读练习测量了参与者对那些未料到会考查的单词的「偶然学习」。

examples.en: We discussed incidental learning after recognizing pictures that appeared alongside the assigned reading.
examples.zh: 认出随指定读物出现的图片后，我们讨论了「偶然学习」。

words.enDefinition: Additional useful information from a measure beyond that provided by existing measures

examples.en: The class asks whether the new score has incremental validity beyond two existing scores.
examples.zh: 课堂探讨新分数在两个既有分数之外是否具有「增量效度」。

examples.en: We compared two models to discuss incremental validity in the fictional assessment report.
examples.zh: 我们通过比较两个模型来讨论虚构测验报告中的「增量效度」。

words.enDefinition: improved problem-solving performance after a break during which the problem is set aside

examples.en: The study compared immediate retries with delayed retries to test for an incubation effect on the same puzzle.
examples.zh: 研究对照立即重试和延迟重试，检验在同一谜题上是否出现「酝酿效应」。

examples.en: We discussed whether the incubation effect measured in the example depended on what people did during the break.
examples.zh: 我们讨论示例测得的「酝酿效应」是否取决于人们在休息期间做什么。

words.enDefinition: reasoning from observations or examples toward a generalization or prediction supported with some degree of uncertainty

examples.en: The class used inductive reasoning to suggest a general rule after observing several patterns in the activity.
examples.zh: 全班观察活动中的若干规律后，用「归纳推理」提出一条一般规则。

examples.en: We compared a larger sample with a smaller one to see how each supported the inductive reasoning.
examples.zh: 我们对照较大和较小的样本，观察两者如何支持「归纳推理」。

words.enDefinition: the study and application of psychology in workplaces, including work design, assessment and organizational behavior

examples.en: The industrial-organizational psychology seminar discussed how different task designs might affect cooperation in a fictional workplace.
examples.zh: 「工业与组织心理学」研讨课讨论了不同任务设计可能如何影响虚构工作场所的合作。

examples.en: We read an industrial-organizational psychology study that evaluated feedback across several simulated work settings in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们阅读一项「工业与组织心理学」研究，它分析了数个模拟工作情境下的反馈。

words.enDefinition: Erikson's proposed conflict between developing competence through valued tasks and experiencing doubts about one's relative ability

examples.en: The example illustrates industry versus inferiority through a fictional child's changing sense of competence on classroom projects.
examples.zh: 示例以虚构儿童在课堂项目中的能力感变化来说明「勤奋对自卑」。

examples.en: We placed industry versus inferiority in the school years on the chart of Erikson's theoretical sequence.
examples.zh: 在埃里克森理论顺序图上，我们将「勤奋对自卑」放在学龄时期。

words.enDefinition: an expectation for conduct learned through social interaction and practice without official codification

examples.en: The group followed an informal norm of waiting for others to finish speaking in the fictional meeting.
examples.zh: 虚构会议的小组遵循让别人说完再开口这一「非正式规范」。

examples.en: We identified the informal norm from recurring reactions to interruptions rather than from any written rule.
examples.zh: 我们根据每次插话后反复出现的反应，辨认出没有写入规则的「非正式规范」。

words.enDefinition: an approach modeling cognition in terms of how incoming information is transformed, stored and used

examples.en: The information-processing approach divided the classroom task into recognizing the signal, comparing it and giving a response.
examples.zh: 「信息加工观点」把课堂任务拆为辨认信号、比较信号和给出回应三个环节。

examples.en: We used the information-processing approach to explain which part of the task might account for slower responses.
examples.zh: 我们用「信息加工观点」解释任务的哪一部分可能造成反应变慢。

words.enDefinition: Social influence arising when people treat others' responses as information about what is correct or appropriate.

examples.en: The fictitious orientation exercise illustrates informational social influence when a newcomer treats other students' choices as useful evidence.
examples.zh: 虚构迎新练习中，新生把其他学生的选择当作有用证据，用以说明「信息性社会影响」。

examples.en: Our worksheet discusses informational social influence when characters rely on a group answer in an ambiguous situation.
examples.zh: 练习单通过角色在模糊情境中依赖群体答案的一幕讨论「信息性社会影响」。

words.enDefinition: Slower responses to targets at a recently cued location after an interval under some conditions.

examples.en: The plot illustrated inhibition of return when responses slowed at the previously cued location after a delay.
examples.zh: 图中，经过一段延迟后，对先前提示位置的反应变慢，说明了「返回抑制」。

examples.en: Our reading discussed inhibition of return as a possible bias toward looking at new locations.
examples.zh: 阅读材料认为，「返回抑制」可能使观察者更倾向于看新的位置。

collocations: a measure of inhibition of return
a task measuring inhibition of return

words.enDefinition: the configuration or situation a solver begins with before taking any steps toward a solution

examples.en: The instructor drew the initial state of a problem before showing any of the available actions in class.
examples.zh: 老师在课堂上先画出「问题初始状态」，再展示可采取的行动。

examples.en: We compared the initial state of a problem with the desired outcome to identify what needed to change.
examples.zh: 我们将「问题初始状态」与预期结果对照，确定需要改变什么。

collocations: specify the initial state of a problem
draw the initial state of a problem
describe the initial state of a problem

words.enDefinition: Erikson's proposed conflict concerning the development of initiative while navigating limits and feelings of guilt

examples.en: The textbook illustrates initiative versus guilt through a fictional child proposing a new activity and encountering limits.
examples.zh: 教材以虚构儿童提出一项新活动并遇到限制为例，说明「主动对内疚」。

examples.en: We discussed initiative versus guilt as a theoretical theme in the classroom story about starting group play.
examples.zh: 我们把「主动对内疚」作为理论主题，讨论课堂上关于发起小组游戏的故事。

words.enDefinition: A perceived or shared expectation about which behaviours others approve of or disapprove of.

examples.en: The class uses an injunctive norm to describe what members of the fictional club consider acceptable behaviour.
examples.zh: 全班用「指令性规范」描述虚构社团成员认为什么行为可以接受。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks whether the injunctive norm and the group's observed behaviour coincide in the imaginary situation.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，在假设情境中，「指令性规范」和观察到的群体行为是否吻合。

collocations: behaviour approved under an injunctive norm

words.enDefinition: solving a problem through a relatively sudden shift in understanding that makes a solution apparent

examples.en: In the insight problem solving example, the learner suddenly noticed a new way to group the lines.
examples.zh: 在「顿悟式问题解决」示例中，学习者突然注意到可以用一种新的方式对线条分组。

examples.en: We compared reports of insight problem solving with accounts describing a gradual sequence of explicit steps in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们将「顿悟式问题解决」的报告与逐步明确推进的叙述作对照。

words.enDefinition: unequal access, treatment or outcomes produced by rules and routines within a particular institution or type of institution

examples.en: The example describes institutional inequality when recurring administrative rules create different opportunities within the same fictional organization.
examples.zh: 示例描述在同一虚构组织内，例行行政规则造成不同机会的「制度性不平等」。

examples.en: We examined the repeated decision pattern before calling it institutional inequality in the classroom exercise about schools.
examples.zh: 在把学校相关课堂练习里的情况称为「制度性不平等」前，我们考察了反复出现的决策模式。

words.enDefinition: cultural capital recognized in a formal credential or qualification, in Bourdieu's framework

examples.en: The worksheet identifies a recognized certificate as institutionalized cultural capital in the fictional example of educational selection.
examples.zh: 习题将受到认可的证书列为虚构教育选拔示例中的「制度化文化资本」。

examples.en: We contrasted institutionalized cultural capital documented by a degree with skills demonstrated informally in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 我们将学位证明的「制度化文化资本」与课堂示例中以非正式方式展示的技能对照。

words.enDefinition: temporary support adapted to a learner's current needs and gradually withdrawn as competence develops

examples.en: The classroom example used instructional scaffolding when the tutor provided a cue and then reduced the help.
examples.zh: 课堂示例中，老师先提供一个提示，再逐渐减少帮助，采用了「教学支架」。

examples.en: We compared instructional scaffolding across two tasks that required different levels of support from the teacher.
examples.zh: 我们比较两个任务中的「教学支架」，这两个任务需要老师提供程度不同的支持。

collocations: adapt instructional scaffolding to a learner

words.enDefinition: In dissonance theory, the absence of an adequate external reason to explain an action inconsistent with one's attitude.

examples.en: Our seminar uses a fictional account to discuss insufficient justification after a character acts against a preference.
examples.zh: 研讨课借虚构记述，讨论角色违背个人偏好后出现的「外在理由不足」。

examples.en: The textbook introduces insufficient justification to explain why a person might reconsider an attitude after an inconsistent action.
examples.zh: 教材引入「外在理由不足」，说明一个人在做出不一致行为后可能重新考虑态度的原因。

collocations: propose insufficient justification as an explanation

words.enDefinition: Acquisition of information with a deliberate goal of remembering or mastering it

examples.en: The intentional learning group knew that a vocabulary quiz would follow the reading.
examples.zh: 「有意学习」组知道阅读之后会有一次词汇小测。

examples.en: Our worksheet labels the deliberate study condition as intentional learning in the comparison.
examples.zh: 在这项对比练习里，习题把刻意学习的条件标为「有意学习」。

collocations: compare intentional learning with incidental learning

words.enDefinition: A pattern in which one factor's effect depends on another factor's level.

examples.en: The interaction effect appeared because larger text helped much more on the patterned background in the example.
examples.zh: 例子中，在有图案的背景上加大字体更有帮助，因此出现了「交互效应」。

examples.en: We plotted the two factors together to see which conditions contributed to the interaction effect.
examples.zh: 我们把两个因素画在同一张图上，以查看哪些条件促成了「交互效应」。

words.enDefinition: an approach explaining behavior or development through combined and interdependent influences from the person and environment

examples.en: The interactionist perspective helped the class explain why two learners responded differently to the same classroom change.
examples.zh: 「交互作用观点」帮助全班解释为什么两名学习者对同样的课堂变化作出不同反应。

examples.en: We used an interactionist perspective to discuss how practice and previous ability might jointly shape improvement.
examples.zh: 我们用「交互作用观点」讨论练习和已有能力怎样共同影响进步。

collocations: explain behavior from an interactionist perspective

words.enDefinition: The difference in sound level at the two ears.

examples.en: The simulated high tone showed an interaural level difference because its measured level varied between the ears.
examples.zh: 模拟高音在两耳测得的声级不同，因此存在「双耳声级差」。

examples.en: In the diagram, the interaural level difference was visible as unequal amplitudes on the two traces.
examples.zh: 图中两条曲线的振幅不同，体现了「双耳声级差」。

collocations: a cue from interaural level difference
compare interaural level difference with timing cues

words.enDefinition: The difference in when a sound reaches the two ears.

examples.en: The model illustrated interaural time difference by showing a click reaching one ear shortly before the other.
examples.zh: 模型展示同一咔嗒声先到达一只耳朵，片刻后才到另一只，用以说明「双耳时差」。

examples.en: The class labeled the interaural time difference on two traces of the same recorded pulse.
examples.zh: 全班在同一录制脉冲的两条曲线上标出了「双耳时差」。

collocations: localization based on interaural time difference

words.enDefinition: changes in social position measured by comparing people with those of another generation, often their parents

examples.en: The intergenerational mobility exercise compares the occupations of adult children with those of parents in the synthetic data.
examples.zh: 「代际流动」练习对比合成数据中成年子女与父母各自的职业。

examples.en: We read the intergenerational mobility table by checking both the parent's group and the adult child's group.
examples.zh: 我们读取「代际流动」表时，同时核对父母所属群体和成年子女所属群体。

words.enDefinition: Interaction between people with different group memberships, studied in relation to attitudes and social relations.

examples.en: The fictional campus programme provides a case for discussing intergroup contact between members of two student societies.
examples.zh: 虚构校园项目为讨论两个学生组织成员之间的「群际接触」提供了案例。

examples.en: Our seminar compares different forms of intergroup contact in the readings before considering their possible associations with attitudes.
examples.zh: 研讨课先比较读物中的不同「群际接触」形式，再讨论它们与态度可能有何关联。

words.enDefinition: Unfair differential treatment of people because of their membership in a social group.

examples.en: The reading defines intergroup discrimination by separating unfair treatment from the attitudes that may accompany it.
examples.zh: 读物通过区分不公平对待与可能伴随它的态度，定义「群际歧视」。

examples.en: Our fictional classroom scenario uses intergroup discrimination to illustrate an unequal decision based on group membership.
examples.zh: 课堂虚构情境借「群际歧视」说明依据群体身份作出的不平等决定。

words.enDefinition: A negative evaluation or feeling directed toward members of another social group because of their membership.

examples.en: The seminar defines intergroup prejudice using fictional groups and an example of unfounded dislike based on membership.
examples.zh: 研讨课借助虚构群体及因群体归属而无端反感的例子，定义「群际偏见」。

examples.en: Our worksheet analyses intergroup prejudice separately from the overt actions recorded in the same fictional scenario.
examples.zh: 练习单把「群际偏见」与同一虚构情境中记录的公开行为分开分析。

words.enDefinition: Reinforcement provided following only some occurrences of a specified response

examples.en: The simulation depicts intermittent reinforcement by leaving some correct matches without a point.
examples.zh: 模拟用部分正确匹配不得分的情形说明「间歇强化」。

examples.en: We compared intermittent reinforcement with a game that rewarded every correct selection.
examples.zh: 我们把「间歇强化」与每次选对都得分的游戏作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Extent to which item scores on a composite measure covary

examples.en: The article discusses internal consistency without assuming that correlated items prove a single factor.
examples.zh: 文章讨论了「内部一致性」，没有把题目分数相关当作单一因子的证明。

examples.en: We compared internal consistency estimates for two sets of items in the same workbook.
examples.zh: 我们比较了同一本练习册中两组题目的「内部一致性」估计值。

words.enDefinition: Findings about how relationships among items align with the proposed score structure

examples.en: The article presents internal structure evidence by checking whether items cluster as expected.
examples.zh: 文章通过检查题目是否按预期聚在一起提供「内部结构证据」。

examples.en: We read the fictional report's internal structure evidence alongside the matrix of item correlations.
examples.zh: 我们对照题目相关矩阵，阅读了虚构报告的「内部结构证据」。

words.enDefinition: The extent to which a study supports its proposed causal conclusion.

examples.en: The class questioned internal validity because the fictional groups differed in both lighting and room noise.
examples.zh: 全班对「内部效度」提出疑问，因为虚构的两组不仅光照不同，房间噪声也不同。

examples.en: We reviewed internal validity before concluding that the background caused the difference in the example.
examples.zh: 在断定差异由背景引起之前，我们先检查了这个例子的「内部效度」。

words.enDefinition: a mental representation of relationships, incorporating expectations about one's own role and how attachment figures may respond

examples.en: The theory uses an internal working model of attachment to explain expectations about whether others will respond reliably.
examples.zh: 理论用「依恋内部工作模型」解释对他人是否会可靠回应的预期。

examples.en: We discussed the internal working model of attachment alongside new experiences that could alter those expectations over time.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「依恋内部工作模型」，同时考察可能随时间改变这些预期的新经历。

collocations: form an internal working model of attachment
change an internal working model of attachment
study an internal working model of attachment

words.enDefinition: The extent to which independent observers assign matching records to the same behavior.

examples.en: We calculated interobserver agreement by checking how often two classroom observers applied the same code independently.
examples.zh: 我们统计两名课堂观察者分别编码时使用相同编码的频率，以计算「观察者间一致性」。

examples.en: The worksheet showed lower interobserver agreement on the segments where the target action was difficult to classify.
examples.zh: 在目标动作难以分类的时段，习题显示「观察者间一致性」较低。

words.enDefinition: A depth cue in which one object partly blocks another from view.

examples.en: Interposition made the partly hidden notebook look farther away than the mug in the photograph.
examples.zh: 「遮挡深度线索」让照片中被部分挡住的笔记本看起来比马克杯更远。

examples.en: The example used interposition, so students could tell which object was nearer without judging its exact distance.
examples.zh: 示例运用了「遮挡深度线索」，学生无需判断确切距离，也能分辨哪个物体更近。

collocations: use interposition as a depth cue

words.enDefinition: Similarity of scores different raters assign to the same test responses

examples.en: The class checked interrater agreement by comparing the actual categories assigned by both readers.
examples.zh: 课堂通过对照两位阅卷者实际给出的类别来检查「评分者间一致度」。

examples.en: We distinguished interrater agreement from merely putting the fictional responses in the same order.
examples.zh: 我们区分了「评分者间一致度」与只是给虚构答案排出同样的顺序。

words.enDefinition: Consistency with which different raters distinguish the same targets using their ratings

examples.en: The tutorial estimates interrater reliability from two readers scoring the same fictional answers.
examples.zh: 辅导课用两位阅卷者给同一组虚构答案打出的分数估计「评分者间信度」。

examples.en: We discussed interrater reliability when the two raters ranked the scripts similarly.
examples.zh: 两位评分者对答卷排序相近时，我们讨论了「评分者间信度」。

words.enDefinition: Comparing repeated measurements before and after a defined change to examine possible effects.

examples.en: The interrupted time series design tracked fictional participation counts before and after a change in classroom layout.
examples.zh: 「中断时间序列设计」追踪改变教室布局前后虚构的参与次数。

examples.en: We looked at the earlier trend before interpreting the jump in the simulated interrupted time series design.
examples.zh: 我们先查看早期趋势，再解读模拟「中断时间序列设计」中的突然上升。

collocations: use an interrupted time series design
an interrupted time series design with a comparison series
evaluate an interrupted time series design

words.enDefinition: an approach analyzing how social categories and systems of power intersect to shape particular experiences or inequalities

examples.en: The seminar uses intersectionality to examine jointly shaped experiences in two fictional situations involving different institutional rules.
examples.zh: 研讨课使用「交叉性」考察两个制度规则不同的虚构情境中，个体经历如何受多方面共同塑造。

examples.en: We discussed intersectionality when separate averages obscured a distinct pattern for one subgroup in the synthetic table.
examples.zh: 当分列均值掩盖了合成表中某个子群体独特的模式时，我们讨论了「交叉性」。

words.enDefinition: The time from the end of one stimulus to the start of the next.

examples.en: The slide marked the interstimulus interval between the disappearance of one shape and the appearance of another.
examples.zh: 投影片标出了一个形状消失到另一个出现之间的「刺激间隔」。

examples.en: We compared the interstimulus interval across conditions even though each picture stayed visible for the same time.
examples.zh: 尽管每张图的显示时长相同，我们仍比较各条件下的「刺激间隔」。

collocations: the length of the interstimulus interval

words.enDefinition: The period between the end of one trial and the start of another.

examples.en: The intertrial interval ran from the closing of the response window to the beginning of the next trial.
examples.zh: 「试次间隔」从有效作答时段结束起，到下一试次开始为止。

examples.en: We checked the intertrial interval separately from the gap between pictures within the same trial.
examples.zh: 我们分别核对了「试次间隔」和同一试次中两幅图之间的空档。

words.enDefinition: Requesting a participant report at specified, prearranged times.

examples.en: The interval-contingent sampling example asked fictional participants to report their current activity at regular times each day.
examples.zh: 「定时取样」示例要求虚构参与者在每天的固定时间报告当时正在进行的活动。

examples.en: We recognized interval-contingent sampling because the reporting times had already been listed on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 报告时间已列在习题上，我们据此辨认出这是「定时取样」。

words.enDefinition: Dividing an observation period into intervals and scoring each according to a behavior rule.

examples.en: The interval recording sheet divided the fictional session into equal segments with a score for each.
examples.zh: 「区间记录」表把虚构活动划分为等长时段，为每段记录一个分值。

examples.en: We discussed whether interval recording could show how long each individual action lasted in the simulation.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「区间记录」是否能显示模拟中每次行为持续了多久。

words.enDefinition: Erikson's proposed conflict concerning close mutual relationships and possible difficulty establishing or maintaining them

examples.en: The seminar uses intimacy versus isolation to discuss the fictional young adult's changing expectations about close relationships.
examples.zh: 研讨课用「亲密对孤立」讨论虚构青年对亲近关系的预期如何改变。

examples.en: We compared intimacy versus isolation with the earlier identity theme in the chart summarizing Erikson's model.
examples.zh: 我们在总结埃里克森模型的图中，将「亲密对孤立」与较早的认同主题对照。

words.enDefinition: Family of statistics describing reliability or agreement of clustered or repeated measurements

examples.en: The worksheet uses an intraclass correlation coefficient to summarize ratings from several readers.
examples.zh: 习题用「组内相关系数」概括几位阅卷者给出的评分。

examples.en: Our group compared two versions of the intraclass correlation coefficient for the same simulated ratings.
examples.zh: 我们组对同一组模拟评分比较了两个版本的「组内相关系数」。

words.enDefinition: change in one person's social position over their own lifetime

examples.en: The timeline illustrates intragenerational mobility by showing the same fictional person moving between occupational groups during their career.
examples.zh: 时间线展示同一个虚构人物在职业生涯中如何变换职业群体，说明「代内流动」。

examples.en: We compared intragenerational mobility for two fictional people using early and later positions in the classroom records.
examples.zh: 我们用课堂记录中初期与后期的地位，对照两个虚构人物的「代内流动」。

words.enDefinition: deliberate observation or reporting of one's own conscious experiences or mental processes

examples.en: In the history exercise, introspection meant describing the immediate experience reported after hearing a simple tone.
examples.zh: 在历史练习中，「内省」指听到简单音调后报告当下的体验。

examples.en: We discussed whether introspection alone could establish which mental steps had occurred during the classroom task.
examples.zh: 我们讨论仅凭「内省」能否确定课堂任务中发生了哪些心理步骤。

words.enDefinition: A tendency toward the lower end of extraversion, often involving lower social expressiveness or preference for less stimulation.

examples.en: The handout discusses introversion through fictional participants who prefer quieter settings while still enjoying close friendships.
examples.zh: 讲义用偏好安静环境、同时也重视亲密友谊的虚构参与者来讨论「内向性」。

examples.en: Our personality seminar distinguishes introversion from discomfort about speaking in one particular classroom setting.
examples.zh: 人格心理学研讨课区分了「内向性」和在某个特定课堂环境中发言时的不自在。

words.enDefinition: A cue indicating a location or time other than the one containing the target.

examples.en: An invalid cue pointed left, but the target in the classroom animation appeared on the right.
examples.zh: 「无效线索」指向左边，但课堂动画中的目标出现在右边。

examples.en: The graph showed slower responses when an invalid cue directed attention away from the actual target.
examples.zh: 图中显示，「无效线索」把注意引离实际目标时，作答速度更慢。

collocations: a trial with an invalid cue
the cost of an invalid cue

words.enDefinition: Evaluation of how individual assessment questions function in observed response data

examples.en: Our class uses item analysis to explain why two sample questions behave differently.
examples.zh: 课堂用「项目分析」解释两道样题为何表现不同。

examples.en: The workbook presents item analysis results before discussing the hypothetical test as a whole.
examples.zh: 练习册先给出「项目分析」结果，再讨论假想测验的整体表现。

words.enDefinition: Organized repository of assessment items maintained for use in test development

examples.en: The simulated item bank stores practice questions along with their estimated difficulty levels.
examples.zh: 模拟「题库」储存了练习题和各题的估计难度。

examples.en: Our tutor showed how two sample forms drew from the same item bank.
examples.zh: 老师展示了两份样卷如何从同一个「题库」选题。

collocations: select items from an item bank

words.enDefinition: Systematic item disadvantage attributable to factors unrelated to the intended construct

examples.en: The class treated item bias as a question about causes, not just statistical patterns.
examples.zh: 课堂把「项目偏差」看作一个涉及成因的问题，不能仅凭统计模式判断。

examples.en: We discussed item bias after noticing that the fictional item required unrelated background knowledge.
examples.zh: 发现虚构题目要求无关的背景知识后，我们讨论了「项目偏差」。

words.enDefinition: Estimation of item parameters from response data under a measurement model

examples.en: The workbook uses synthetic responses to illustrate item calibration under a specified model.
examples.zh: 练习册用合成作答数据说明在已设定模型下的「项目校准」。

examples.en: We read the item calibration results before comparing the difficulty estimates across items.
examples.zh: 我们先阅读「项目校准」结果，再比较各题的难度估计。

words.enDefinition: Graph relating the probability of a scored response to latent trait level

examples.en: The item characteristic curve rises as the model's estimated skill increases in the example.
examples.zh: 在该示例中，「项目特征曲线」随模型估计技能水平的提高而上升。

examples.en: We compared the slope of each item characteristic curve using the same horizontal scale.
examples.zh: 我们用相同刻度的横轴对比了各条「项目特征曲线」的斜率。

collocations: shape of an item characteristic curve

words.enDefinition: Extent to which an assessment question is hard for respondents

examples.en: In the classroom example, item difficulty is summarized using the proportion answered correctly.
examples.zh: 课堂示例用答对比例来概括「项目难度」。

examples.en: We compared item difficulty for two questions covering the same fictional lesson.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两道考查同一虚构课程内容的题目的「项目难度」。

words.enDefinition: Extent to which an item differentiates respondents at different measured trait levels

examples.en: The sample chart shows stronger item discrimination for one of the two questions.
examples.zh: 样本图表显示，两题中有一题的「项目区分度」更高。

examples.en: We discussed item discrimination separately from how many students answered the item correctly.
examples.zh: 我们把「项目区分度」和这道题有多少学生答对分开讨论。

words.enDefinition: Selection of an affirmative or higher agreement response to an item

examples.en: The table reports item endorsement for each statement in the simulated agreement questionnaire.
examples.zh: 表格报告了模拟态度问卷中每项陈述的「题项赞同」情况。

examples.en: We compared item endorsement across two statements dealing with the same classroom topic.
examples.zh: 我们比较了围绕同一课堂主题的两条陈述的「题项赞同」情况。

words.enDefinition: Degree of agreement between observed item responses and model expectations

examples.en: The worksheet compares observed and predicted responses to discuss item fit for one question.
examples.zh: 习题对比一道题的实际作答与预测作答，讨论其「项目拟合」。

examples.en: Our group checked item fit before interpreting the model values in the table.
examples.zh: 我们组先检查「项目拟合」，再解读表中的模型数值。

words.enDefinition: Model-based quantity reflecting how precisely an item measures at a trait level

examples.en: The graph shows item information peaking near the middle of the simulated scale.
examples.zh: 图表显示，「项目信息量」在模拟量表中部附近达到峰值。

examples.en: We compared item information for two questions that had different response curves.
examples.zh: 我们对比了两道反应曲线不同的题目的「项目信息量」。

collocations: item information at a trait level

words.enDefinition: Collection of candidate items being considered for inclusion in a measure

examples.en: Our class reviewed an item pool containing several draft questions for each topic.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂上审阅了一个「备选题集合」，每个主题下都有几道拟定的问题。
