examples.en: We grouped the item pool by content before discussing possible versions of the test.
examples.zh: 我们按内容给「备选题集合」分类，再讨论测验的可能版本。

words.enDefinition: Framework relating item response probabilities to latent traits and item characteristics

examples.en: The lecture introduces item response theory through probability curves for two hypothetical questions.
examples.zh: 讲座用两道假想题目的概率曲线来介绍「项目反应理论」。

examples.en: We compared item response theory with a framework focused mainly on total scores.
examples.zh: 我们将「项目反应理论」与主要关注总分的框架作了比较。

words.enDefinition: coordinated attention between people toward the same object or event, with awareness of their shared focus

examples.en: The video example shows joint attention when the child follows a pointing gesture and checks the partner's gaze.
examples.zh: 视频示例中，儿童顺着指向手势看过去，再核对同伴的注视方向，体现了「共同注意」。

examples.en: We identified joint attention by noting that both actors oriented toward the same object and one another.
examples.zh: 我们观察到两人既朝向同一个物体，也相互关注，从而辨认出「共同注意」。

words.enDefinition: Estimate of how well recently studied information will be remembered later

examples.en: After studying the pair, each student recorded a judgment of learning before taking the quiz.
examples.zh: 学习词对后，每位学生在参加小测前记录了一次「学习判断」。

examples.en: We compared each judgment of learning with actual later recall in the fictional dataset.
examples.zh: 我们用虚构数据对照了各项「学习判断」及随后实际的回忆表现。

collocations: accuracy of a judgment of learning

words.enDefinition: The belief that outcomes generally reflect what people deserve, which can shape judgments about events.

examples.en: The seminar introduces just-world belief with fictional explanations for why two students received different project outcomes.
examples.zh: 研讨课用对两名学生项目结果不同的虚构解释介绍「公正世界信念」。

examples.en: Our class asks whether just-world belief could affect interpretations of a fictional outcome distributed completely by chance.
examples.zh: 全班询问，「公正世界信念」是否会影响人们解读一种完全随机分配的虚构结果。

words.enDefinition: The fair distribution of burdens and benefits associated with research.

examples.en: The seminar discussed justice in research when a fictional study placed repeated demands on only one group.
examples.zh: 研讨课用一个只对一个小组反复提出要求的虚构研究讨论「研究中的公正原则」。

examples.en: We connected justice in research with asking who bore the study's burdens and who might benefit.
examples.zh: 我们将「研究中的公正原则」与谁承担研究负担、谁可能受益的问题联系起来。

collocations: the principle of justice in research
a concern about justice in research

words.enDefinition: A distinctive large brain wave commonly associated with N2 sleep.

examples.en: Our tutor labeled the K-complex on a synthetic trace next to a clearly different rhythmic burst.
examples.zh: 辅导老师在合成波形上标出「K复合波」，旁边是一段明显不同的节律波。

examples.en: The worksheet asked whether the marked feature was a K-complex or part of the background activity.
examples.zh: 习题问，标出的特征是「K复合波」还是背景活动的一部分。

words.enDefinition: a sociological approach examining how social responses and labels shape the meaning and consequences of perceived deviance

examples.en: The lecture applies labeling theory to a fictional example in which an official label changed later social interactions.
examples.zh: 讲义将「标签理论」用于一个虚构示例，其中正式标签改变了后续社会互动。

examples.en: We used labeling theory to distinguish the initial act from the responses that altered the character's opportunities.
examples.zh: 我们运用「标签理论」区分最初行为与后来改变人物机会的社会回应。

words.enDefinition: the mental processes used to derive meaning from spoken, written or signed language

examples.en: The classroom task tested language comprehension by asking learners to choose which picture matched the heard sentence.
examples.zh: 课堂任务请学习者选出与听到的句子相符的图，以检验「语言理解」。

examples.en: We compared language comprehension across two contexts that gave the same word different plausible meanings in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们对比两种情境中的「语言理解」，其中同一个词在不同情境下各有合理意思。

words.enDefinition: the mental processes that convert intended meaning into spoken, written or signed language

examples.en: The language production trial began with a picture that the fictional participant had to describe aloud.
examples.zh: 「语言产生」试次以一幅图开始，虚构参与者需要大声描述那幅图。

examples.en: We discussed how choosing a word and arranging a sentence both contribute to language production in the example.
examples.zh: 我们在示例中讨论选词与组织句子怎样共同参与「语言产生」。

words.enDefinition: an unintended and generally unrecognized consequence of a social practice or institution in functional analysis

examples.en: The seminar discussed building informal networks as a possible latent function of the recurring fictional event.
examples.zh: 研讨课把建立非正式关系网作为这项例行虚构活动的一种可能「潜功能」讨论。

examples.en: We identified a latent function that benefited participants even though it was absent from the stated aims.
examples.zh: 我们找出一项让参与者受益的「潜功能」，它并未列入对外明示的目标。

collocations: latent function of a social practice

words.enDefinition: Acquisition of knowledge that becomes apparent only in later performance

examples.en: The simulation depicts latent learning during maze exploration before any timed test.
examples.zh: 模拟展示了在限时测验前探索迷宫的过程中发生的「潜伏学习」。

examples.en: We discussed whether latent learning could explain the improvement shown on the later trial.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「潜伏学习」能否解释后面试次中表现的改善。

words.enDefinition: Unobserved individual characteristic modeled along a scale using observed responses

examples.en: The model places each simulated respondent at a point on the latent trait scale.
examples.zh: 模型将各个模拟作答者放在「潜在特质」量尺上的某个位置。

examples.en: We discussed how an estimated latent trait differs from a directly observed answer.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了估计得出的「潜在特质」与直接观察到的回答有何不同。

words.enDefinition: Using selected orders so each condition appears equally often in each ordinal position.

examples.en: The worksheet used Latin square counterbalancing to give each of the four tasks every position once.
examples.zh: 习题用「拉丁方平衡安排」让四项任务在每个顺序位置都恰好出现一次。

examples.en: We checked the columns of the Latin square counterbalancing chart to see whether any task repeated.
examples.zh: 我们检查「拉丁方平衡安排」表的各列，看看是否有任务重复出现。

collocations: a schedule for Latin square counterbalancing
check a Latin square counterbalancing scheme

words.enDefinition: The tendency to perceive incomplete elements as forming a complete shape.

examples.en: The broken ring illustrated the law of closure because students still saw a single complete shape.
examples.zh: 轮廓有缺口的圆环说明了「闭合律」，因为学生仍把它看成一个完整形状。

examples.en: Our example of the law of closure used several gaps that did not prevent recognition of the square.
examples.zh: 我们用有几个缺口的正方形来展示「闭合律」，这些缺口并未妨碍识别。

collocations: grouping under the law of closure
an example of the law of closure

words.enDefinition: Principle that satisfying consequences increase the likelihood of preceding behavior

examples.en: The lecture traces the law of effect to Thorndike's early work on learning.
examples.zh: 讲座追溯了「效果律」与桑代克早期学习研究的联系。

examples.en: We used a points game to illustrate the law of effect without running an experiment.
examples.zh: 我们用积分游戏说明了「效果律」，没有实际开展实验。

collocations: historical account of the law of effect

words.enDefinition: The tendency to group elements that are close together in space.

examples.en: The law of proximity explained why the closely spaced marks looked like pairs in the diagram.
examples.zh: 「接近律」解释了为什么图上相距较近的记号看起来成双成对。

examples.en: Our instructor showed the law of proximity by changing the spacing while keeping every mark identical.
examples.zh: 老师让记号本身保持一致，只调整间距，以展示「接近律」。

collocations: an example of the law of proximity
grouping by the law of proximity

words.enDefinition: The tendency to group elements with similar perceptual features.

examples.en: The law of similarity explained why students grouped circles by color even when all distances matched.
examples.zh: 「相似律」解释了为什么圆点间距一致时，学生仍按颜色分组。

examples.en: In the figure, the law of similarity made the repeating triangles look separate from the surrounding circles.
examples.zh: 在图中，根据「相似律」，重复出现的三角形看起来与周围的圆形分属不同组。

collocations: an example of the law of similarity
grouping by the law of similarity

words.enDefinition: The distinct values or categories at which an independent variable is studied.

examples.en: The three levels of the independent variable in the exercise corresponded to three different display sizes.
examples.zh: 练习中，「自变量的各个水平」分别对应三种不同的显示尺寸。

examples.en: We counted the levels of the independent variable before drawing the table of possible experimental conditions.
examples.zh: 绘制可能的实验条件一览表前，我们先确定「自变量的各个水平」共有几个。

collocations: compare levels of an independent variable
specify levels of an independent variable
assign different levels of an independent variable

words.enDefinition: Framework relating later memory to qualitative differences in how material is processed

examples.en: The levels of processing framework distinguishes looking at a word from considering its meaning.
examples.zh: 「加工层次」框架区分观察词的字形与思考词意。

examples.en: Our lab notes compare proposed levels of processing for a simulated word memory task.
examples.zh: 我们的实验笔记对比了模拟单词记忆任务中设定的「加工层次」。

words.enDefinition: different scales of explanation for behavior, such as physiological mechanisms, individual processes and social context

examples.en: The course organized the same classroom observation under three levels of psychological analysis in its overview table.
examples.zh: 课程在总览表中用三个「心理学分析层次」整理对同一课堂现象的观察。

examples.en: We compared levels of psychological analysis by writing a neural explanation and a social explanation of behavior.
examples.zh: 我们各写了一种关于行为的神经解释和社会解释，以比较「心理学分析层次」。

collocations: explain behavior across levels of psychological analysis

words.enDefinition: retrieving stored word information during language comprehension or production

examples.en: The experiment measured lexical access by timing how quickly fictional participants recognized a common word in print.
examples.zh: 实验通过记录虚构参与者辨认出常见印刷词形所需的时间来测量「词汇通达」。

examples.en: We discussed how a related preceding word might speed lexical access for the target in the sample task.
examples.zh: 我们讨论样例任务中，先出现一个相关词怎样可能加快目标词的「词汇通达」。

words.enDefinition: reflecting on and evaluating experiences from across one's life, especially in some accounts of later-life development

examples.en: The reading presents life review through a fictional older narrator reconsidering the meaning of several earlier events.
examples.zh: 阅读材料通过一位虚构老年叙述者重新思考几件往事的意义，呈现「人生回顾」。

examples.en: We distinguished life review from simply recalling the details of one recent event in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 我们区分课堂示例中的「人生回顾」与仅记起一件近期事件的细节。

words.enDefinition: human change and continuity across the whole of life, or the study of that process

examples.en: The lifespan development course compares changes in thinking and social roles across several periods of life.
examples.zh: 「毕生发展」课程比较人生数个时期中思维和社会角色的变化。

examples.en: We used a timeline in lifespan development class to connect childhood experiences with later transitions.
examples.zh: 在「毕生发展」课上，我们用时间线联系童年经历与之后的转变。

words.enDefinition: Perceiving a surface as reflecting a similar proportion of light under different illumination.

examples.en: Lightness constancy explained why the white paper still looked white in the shaded part of the demonstration.
examples.zh: 「明度恒常性」解释了为什么演示中处于阴影里的白纸看起来仍是白色。

examples.en: The shadow example illustrated lightness constancy even though the two paper patches sent different amounts of light back.
examples.zh: 尽管两块纸片反射的光量不同，这个阴影示例仍展示了「明度恒常性」。

words.enDefinition: Single statement rated on an ordered scale of agreement

examples.en: The demo presents one Likert item with ordered options from disagreement to agreement.
examples.zh: 演示给出一个「李克特式题项」，选项按从不同意到同意排列。

examples.en: We distinguished a single Likert item from the score across multiple related items.
examples.zh: 我们把单个「李克特式题项」与多道相关题目合成的得分区分开来。

words.enDefinition: Summated rating scale built from multiple items with ordered agreement options

examples.en: The sample Likert scale combines responses to several related classroom preference statements.
examples.zh: 示例「李克特量表」将有关课堂偏好的几项陈述的回答合在一起计分。

examples.en: We compared responses on one item with scores for the whole Likert scale.
examples.zh: 我们对比了单题的作答与整个「李克特量表」的分数。

words.enDefinition: Stated circumstances in which information cannot remain confidential or may need to be disclosed.

examples.en: The fictional information sheet explained limits to confidentiality using plain wording in its privacy section.
examples.zh: 虚构信息表在隐私部分用直白的语言说明了「保密的适用限制」。

examples.en: We discussed why limits to confidentiality should be clear before anyone decides to join a study.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么应在人们决定是否加入研究前说清「保密的适用限制」。

collocations: a statement of limits to confidentiality

words.enDefinition: A depth cue in which parallel lines project as converging with distance.

examples.en: The railroad drawing used linear perspective to make the parallel tracks appear to converge farther away.
examples.zh: 铁路图通过「线性透视」使平行的铁轨看起来在远处会合。

examples.en: We identified linear perspective in the classroom drawing by following the edges of the long tiled hallway.
examples.zh: 在课堂图画里，我们沿着长长的铺砖走廊两边看，辨认出「线性透视」。

words.enDefinition: the idea that features of a language can influence habitual perception, categorization or thought

examples.en: The lecture on linguistic relativity asks whether familiar labels influence how speakers group a set of colors.
examples.zh: 有关「语言相对性」的讲义询问，熟悉的名称是否影响说话人对一组颜色的归类方式。

examples.en: We discussed evidence for linguistic relativity without assuming that speakers could only think in their familiar categories.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「语言相对性」的证据，同时考虑说话人也能使用不熟悉的类别思考。

words.enDefinition: resources accessible through ties across differences in formal power or authority, such as links to institutions

examples.en: The example illustrates linking social capital when a campus group gains meeting space through an institutional contact.
examples.zh: 校园小组通过机构联系人获得会议场地，示例说明了「联结型社会资本」。

examples.en: We used linking social capital to discuss access across levels of authority in the classroom network model.
examples.zh: 我们运用「联结型社会资本」讨论课堂网络模型中跨不同权力层级获取资源的情况。

collocations: institutional ties supporting linking social capital

words.enDefinition: Assumption that item responses are independent conditional on the modeled trait levels

examples.en: The tutor explains local independence by distinguishing residual links from shared ability effects.
examples.zh: 老师通过区分残差关联和共同能力的影响来解释「局部独立性」。

examples.en: We looked for violations of local independence in the shared passage example.
examples.zh: 我们在共用同一篇材料的题目示例中寻找违反「局部独立性」的迹象。

words.enDefinition: Score references based on a particular school, institution, or local population

examples.en: The fictional school reports local norms alongside the reference values from a national sample.
examples.zh: 虚构学校在全国样本的参照值旁列出了「地方常模」。

examples.en: We checked why the percentile differed when the example used local norms.
examples.zh: 我们核对了为什么示例使用「地方常模」时，百分等级会不同。

words.enDefinition: A general expectation about whether outcomes depend on one's own actions or forces outside one's control.

examples.en: The textbook illustrates locus of control through beliefs about whether effort or chance determines classroom outcomes.
examples.zh: 教材用人们认为成绩取决于努力还是运气的信念，说明「控制点」这一概念。

examples.en: Our diagram places perceived personal influence and external forces along the dimension labelled locus of control.
examples.zh: 示意图将感知到的个人影响和外部力量放在标为「控制点」的维度上。

collocations: individual differences in locus of control

words.enDefinition: Storage of information that remains accessible beyond brief immediate retention

examples.en: The review sheet distinguishes facts and skills as examples of long-term memory.
examples.zh: 复习资料将事实和技能归为「长时记忆」的不同例子。

examples.en: Our tutor discussed long-term memory when we recalled diagrams from last semester's course.
examples.zh: 我们想起上学期课程里的示意图时，老师讲解了「长时记忆」。

words.enDefinition: Cooley's idea that people develop self-understanding partly by imagining how others see and judge them

examples.en: The looking-glass self example shows a learner revising their self-image after imagining how classmates judged their contribution.
examples.zh: 「镜中自我」示例展示一名学习者想象同学如何评价自己的贡献后，调整了自我形象。

examples.en: We connected the looking-glass self with imagined judgments rather than only the comments explicitly made in the story.
examples.zh: 我们将「镜中自我」与想象他人的评价联系起来，故事中明确说出的评论只是其中一部分。

words.enDefinition: wording that emphasizes what is lost, reduced or missed relative to a reference point

examples.en: The loss frame described how many places would become unavailable in the fictional choice about a workshop.
examples.zh: 在关于工作坊的虚构选择题里，「损失框架」描述将有多少座位无法使用。

examples.en: We used a loss frame to present the same numerical outcome from the perspective of places removed.
examples.zh: 我们用「损失框架」，从减少座位的角度呈现同一个数字结果。

words.enDefinition: A dream in which the dreamer realizes they are dreaming.

examples.en: The fictional report described a lucid dream in which someone realized they were dreaming before waking up.
examples.zh: 虚构报告描述了一个「清醒梦」，做梦者醒来之前就意识到自己正在做梦。

examples.en: We distinguished a lucid dream from an unusually vivid dream in the classroom discussion of awareness.
examples.zh: 在课堂上讨论觉察时，我们区分了「清醒梦」与异常逼真的梦。

collocations: a report of a lucid dream
the experience of a lucid dream

words.enDefinition: the study of large-scale patterns, institutions and changes in societies or across them

examples.en: The macrosociology reading compared changes in education and employment across several fictional regions over a long period.
examples.zh: 「宏观社会学」阅读材料对照了数个虚构地区长期以来教育和就业的变化。

examples.en: We used macrosociology to interpret the broad institutional patterns behind differences in the classroom's synthetic dataset.
examples.zh: 我们用「宏观社会学」解释课堂合成数据差异背后的宏观制度模式。

words.enDefinition: the broader cultural, social and institutional patterns that shape the other settings in ecological systems theory

examples.en: The model places prevailing beliefs about schooling in the macrosystem of the fictional community's developmental environment.
examples.zh: 模型把关于学校教育的主流观念放在虚构社区发展环境的「宏系统」中。

examples.en: We compared how two different macrosystem contexts could influence practices in families and schools in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们比较两个不同的「宏系统」背景如何影响练习中家庭与学校的做法。

words.enDefinition: An approach asking observers to assign numbers proportional to perceived intensity.

examples.en: In the magnitude estimation example, participants assigned larger numbers to tones they judged much louder.
examples.zh: 在「数量估计法」示例中，参与者给听起来响得多的音调分配了更大的数值。

examples.en: We plotted classroom magnitude estimation responses against the physical intensity values listed on the slide.
examples.zh: 我们用投影片列出的物理强度值和课堂「数量估计法」的作答绘图。

words.enDefinition: A factor's effect averaged over the levels of other factors.

examples.en: The plot showed a main effect of font size after averaging across both background patterns.
examples.zh: 对两种背景图案取平均后，图中显示了字体大小的「主效应」。

examples.en: We discussed the main effect of display type before looking at how it varied with text size.
examples.zh: 我们先讨论显示类型的「主效应」，再看这个效应如何随字体大小变化。

collocations: the main effect of a factor

words.enDefinition: Simple repetition used to keep information temporarily available in memory

examples.en: The model illustrates maintenance rehearsal with a student quietly repeating a room number.
examples.zh: 模型用学生小声重复教室号码的情形说明「维持性复述」。

examples.en: We separated maintenance rehearsal from making meaningful links among the new vocabulary words.
examples.zh: 我们区分了「维持性复述」与在新词之间建立意义联系。

words.enDefinition: an intended and recognized consequence of a social practice or institution in functional analysis

examples.en: The class identified academic instruction as a manifest function of the fictional school in the example.
examples.zh: 全班将进行学业教学认作示例中虚构学校的一项「显功能」。

examples.en: We checked the stated aims before calling a consequence a manifest function in the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 课堂练习中，我们在把某一后果归为「显功能」前先核对公开的目标。

words.enDefinition: A variable whose levels researchers deliberately set to compare outcomes.

examples.en: Display brightness was the manipulated variable in the example, while all symbols remained the same size.
examples.zh: 亮度是示例中的「操纵变量」，所有符号的大小则保持一致。

examples.en: We identified the manipulated variable by checking which feature changed between the two versions of the task.
examples.zh: 我们核对任务的两个版本之间哪项特征会变，以找出「操纵变量」。

words.enDefinition: A measure testing whether an experimental manipulation changed the intended experience or variable.

examples.en: The manipulation check asked whether students noticed the difference between the two simulated display speeds.
examples.zh: 「操纵检验」询问学生是否注意到两种模拟显示速度的差异。

examples.en: We read the manipulation check separately from the accuracy data to see whether the display change registered.
examples.zh: 我们把「操纵检验」和正确率数据分开看，以确认参与者是否感知到了显示变化。

collocations: a manipulation check for perceived difficulty

words.enDefinition: Practice compressed into one session or repeated with little time between attempts

examples.en: The classroom example uses one uninterrupted session to illustrate massed practice for vocabulary.
examples.zh: 课堂示例用一次不中断的学习说明词汇的「集中练习」。

examples.en: We compared scores after massed practice with scores after the spaced study schedule.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「集中练习」后的分数与分散学习安排后的分数。

collocations: compare massed practice with spaced practice

words.enDefinition: a social status that strongly shapes how a person is seen across many encounters, sometimes overshadowing other positions

examples.en: The reading describes a master status when fictional observers emphasize one position across many different social situations.
examples.zh: 阅读材料用虚构观察者在许多社会情境中强调同一种身份，描述「主导地位」。

examples.en: We discussed why one master status became especially salient in one setting in the classroom vignette.
examples.zh: 我们讨论课堂短情景中，一种「主导地位」在某个环境里为何尤其显眼。

collocations: social effects of a master status
perceive someone through a master status

words.enDefinition: the physical objects and built environments through which a group's practices and meanings are expressed

examples.en: The exhibit's model tools illustrate material culture because their forms reflect how people performed everyday activities.
examples.zh: 展览模型中的工具体现「物质文化」，因为它们的形制反映人们怎样开展日常活动。

examples.en: We examined material culture by comparing the different objects used in two fictional classroom routines in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，我们比较两个虚构课堂惯例使用的不同物品，考察「物质文化」。

words.enDefinition: limited ability to obtain goods or services considered necessary for a specified standard of living

examples.en: The report measures material deprivation with questions about access to essential items in its fictional household survey.
examples.zh: 报告在虚构家庭调查中，用关于必需品可获得性的提问衡量「物质匮乏」。

examples.en: We compared material deprivation with reported income because the two indicators measured different aspects of the example.
examples.zh: 我们将「物质匮乏」与报告收入对照，因为两个指标衡量示例的不同方面。

words.enDefinition: In the sociology of science, the tendency for already eminent researchers to gain disproportionate credit for comparable contributions.

examples.en: The lecture used the Matthew effect to explain why well-known scientists received more credit for comparable work.
examples.zh: 课堂用「马太效应」解释为什么在贡献相当时，知名科学家获得了更多认可。

examples.en: In the example, the Matthew effect favored the famous coauthor when readers remembered who contributed the idea.
examples.zh: 在示例中，当读者回想谁提出了这个想法时，「马太效应」使知名合著者占了优势。

collocations: an example of the Matthew effect

words.enDefinition: developmental change associated with underlying biological growth and organization over time

examples.en: The reading distinguished maturation from practice when discussing gains in physical coordination during the fictional observation period.
examples.zh: 讨论虚构观察期内身体协调性提高时，阅读材料区分了「成熟」和练习。

examples.en: We asked whether age alone could separate maturation from other influences on performance in the example.
examples.zh: 我们讨论在示例中，仅靠年龄能否将「成熟」与影响表现的其他因素区分开来。

words.enDefinition: Model-based reliability coefficient using factor loadings and item error variances

examples.en: The exercise computes McDonald's omega from the factor model fitted to simulated item scores.
examples.zh: 练习根据拟合到模拟题目分数的因子模型计算「麦克唐纳ω系数」。

examples.en: We read the assumptions behind McDonald's omega before interpreting the worksheet's reliability estimate.
examples.zh: 解读习题的信度估计值之前，我们阅读了「麦克唐纳ω系数」所依据的假设。

words.enDefinition: A change in heard speech caused by conflicting visible articulation.

examples.en: The McGurk effect appeared when the same recorded syllable sounded different after students saw another mouth movement.
examples.zh: 学生看见另一种口型后觉得同一录制音节听起来不同，出现了「麦格克效应」。

examples.en: The class compared sound-only and video versions of the clip to discuss the McGurk effect.
examples.zh: 全班比较了同一片段的纯音频和视频版本，以讨论「麦格克效应」。

collocations: a demonstration of the McGurk effect

words.enDefinition: A change over time in the group average of a characteristic, regardless of whether individuals retain their relative order.

examples.en: The chart shows mean-level change as the fictional group's average moves upward between two recorded time points.
examples.zh: 虚构群体的平均值在两个记录时点之间上升，图表用此说明「平均水平变化」。

examples.en: Our exercise illustrates how mean-level change can occur while members of the fictional sample keep their relative positions.
examples.zh: 练习说明，即使虚构样本成员的相对次序不变，也可能发生「平均水平变化」。

words.enDefinition: a strategy comparing the current state with the goal and choosing actions or subgoals to reduce important differences

examples.en: The solver used means-ends analysis to find the largest remaining difference and choose an appropriate intermediate step.
examples.zh: 解题者用「手段—目的分析」找出最重要的剩余差异，并选取合适的中间步骤。

examples.en: We showed how means-ends analysis led the fictional group to create a subgoal before taking the next action.
examples.zh: 我们展示「手段—目的分析」如何引导虚构小组在采取下一步行动前设立子目标。

words.enDefinition: a benefit whose eligibility or amount depends on an assessment of income, assets or other financial resources

examples.en: The policy chart describes a means-tested benefit by showing how eligibility changes with resources in the fictional model.
examples.zh: 政策图展示虚构模型中资格怎样随资源而改变，以描述「经济状况审查型福利」。

examples.en: We checked which resources counted for the means-tested benefit in the synthetic example before comparing the cases.
examples.zh: 对照案例前，我们核查合成示例中哪些资源纳入「经济状况审查型福利」的审查。

words.enDefinition: A variable whose values are observed or recorded rather than assigned.

examples.en: The number of correct answers was a measured variable in the task comparing two symbol displays.
examples.zh: 两组符号显示的对比任务中，答对的数量是一个「测量变量」。

examples.en: In the observational example, each measured variable came from the same fictional activity log.
examples.zh: 观察研究示例中的各个「测量变量」都来自同一份虚构活动日志。

collocations: an association between two measured variables

words.enDefinition: Source of measurement variation represented by conditions such as raters or occasions

examples.en: In the simulated design, raters are one measurement facet and tasks are another.
examples.zh: 在模拟设计中，评分者是一个「测量侧面」，任务是另一个。

examples.en: Our group marked each measurement facet in the practice diagram before reading the results.
examples.zh: 我们组先在练习图中标出每个「测量侧面」，再阅读结果。

words.enDefinition: Equivalence of measurement relationships across specified groups, conditions, or occasions

examples.en: The paper describes measurement invariance across two invented groups with different average scores.
examples.zh: 论文描述了平均分不同的两个虚构组之间的「测量不变性」。

examples.en: We discussed measurement invariance before interpreting the differences in scores between those groups.
examples.zh: 我们先讨论「测量不变性」，再解读这些组的分数差异。

words.enDefinition: Statistical description linking observed measures to the attributes they represent

examples.en: The measurement model connects each of the questionnaire items with its intended factor.
examples.zh: 「测量模型」将每道问卷题与它意在反映的因子连接起来。

examples.en: Our group compared two versions of the measurement model using the same simulated responses.
examples.zh: 我们组用同一批模拟作答比较了两个版本的「测量模型」。

words.enDefinition: in Durkheim's theory, social cohesion based largely on similarities in shared beliefs, activities and ways of life

examples.en: The text illustrates mechanical solidarity by emphasizing the shared occupations and collective practices in its stylized example.
examples.zh: 教材强调简化示例中共同的职业与集体做法，以说明「机械团结」。

examples.en: We compared mechanical solidarity with cohesion based on people relying on one another for different specialized tasks.
examples.zh: 我们把「机械团结」与依靠他人完成不同专业任务而形成的凝聚方式作比较。

words.enDefinition: Grouping separate pieces of information into larger memorable units

examples.en: Our tutor illustrated memory chunking by grouping the digits into familiar year patterns.
examples.zh: 老师把数字按熟悉的年份样式分组，以此说明「记忆组块化」。

examples.en: The worksheet compares memory chunking for familiar letter patterns and for random letters.
examples.zh: 习题比较了熟悉字母组合和随机字母的「记忆组块化」。

words.enDefinition: Processes through which a newly formed memory becomes more stable over time

examples.en: The diagram depicts memory consolidation as a gradual change after the initial learning period.
examples.zh: 示意图将「记忆巩固」描绘为初次学习之后逐步发生的变化。

examples.en: We discussed memory consolidation when comparing memory measured at different times after study.
examples.zh: 我们比较了学习后不同时间测得的记忆表现，并讨论了「记忆巩固」。

words.enDefinition: Process of transforming information into a representation usable by memory

examples.en: The worksheet compares memory encoding for pictures and for the names of pictured objects.
examples.zh: 习题比较了对图片的「记忆编码」和对图中物品名称的编码。

examples.en: Our seminar discussed memory encoding before looking at how the same information is retrieved.
examples.zh: 研讨课先讨论了「记忆编码」，再考察同样的信息如何被提取。

words.enDefinition: Process of accessing information that has been retained in memory

examples.en: The study guide explains memory retrieval with an example about recalling a name.
examples.zh: 学习指南用想起姓名的例子说明「记忆提取」。

examples.en: We observed faster memory retrieval when the practice question included a familiar picture.
examples.zh: 练习题出现熟悉的图片时，我们观察到更快的「记忆提取」。

words.enDefinition: Retention of encoded information over a period of time

examples.en: The diagram places memory storage between the initial processing and the later test.
examples.zh: 示意图把「记忆储存」放在初始加工和后来的测验之间。

examples.en: We compared two models of memory storage using the same classroom memory example.
examples.zh: 我们用同一个课堂记忆示例比较了两种「记忆储存」模型。

words.enDefinition: the experience of mentally representing sensory qualities without the corresponding stimulus currently being present

examples.en: The class discussed mental imagery after students described how they pictured the route while looking away.
examples.zh: 学生描述自己移开视线时如何在脑中想象路线后，全班讨论了「心理意象」。

examples.en: The worksheet contrasts visual mental imagery with imagining the sound of an instrument in the next example.
examples.zh: 练习对照视觉「心理意象」和下一例中在脑中想象乐器声音的体验。

words.enDefinition: a person's stored knowledge of words, including their forms, meanings and syntactic properties

examples.en: The model describes a mental lexicon in which words are connected to related forms and meanings.
examples.zh: 模型描述了一个「心理词库」，其中的词连接到有关的形式和意义。

examples.en: We used the mental lexicon to explain why a meaning can be available before its precise word form.
examples.zh: 我们用「心理词库」解释为什么有时先想到一个意思，之后才想到准确词形。

collocations: store words in the mental lexicon

words.enDefinition: an internal operation such as attending, remembering, interpreting or deciding that contributes to experience or behavior

examples.en: The same visible choice could follow a different mental process in each fictional learner's explanation of the exercise.
examples.zh: 在虚构学习者对练习的解释里，同一个可观察选择可能来自各自不同的「心理过程」。

examples.en: We considered which mental process might explain the delay between the question and the student's response.
examples.zh: 我们讨论哪个「心理过程」可能解释从提问到学生回应之间的延迟。

words.enDefinition: an internal form in which information about an object, event or relation is encoded for use in cognition

examples.en: The mental representation of the room preserved the relative positions of its desks in the example.
examples.zh: 在示例中，对房间的「心理表征」保留了桌子之间的相对位置。

examples.en: In class, we compared a verbal description and diagram as models of a possible mental representation.
examples.zh: 课上，我们比较两种作为「心理表征」模型的形式，即口头描述和示意图。

words.enDefinition: a tendency to approach a new problem using a familiar strategy that succeeded in earlier problems

examples.en: A mental set led the fictional solver to repeat the older method even after an easier option appeared.
examples.zh: 「思维定势」使虚构解题者在更简单的选项出现后仍重复使用旧方法。

examples.en: We changed the next puzzle to see whether the established mental set would interfere with solving it.
examples.zh: 我们改变下一道谜题，观察既有「思维定势」会不会妨碍解题。

collocations: problem solving affected by a mental set

words.enDefinition: A tendency in some conditions for repeated encounters with a stimulus to increase liking or positive evaluation.

examples.en: The classroom example illustrates the mere exposure effect with fictional ratings of otherwise unfamiliar patterns across sessions.
examples.zh: 课堂示例用多次活动中对原本陌生图案的虚构评分说明「单纯暴露效应」。

examples.en: Our seminar asks whether increasing familiarity could account for the mere exposure effect described in the example.
examples.zh: 研讨课讨论，熟悉程度上升能否解释示例所述的「单纯暴露效应」。

collocations: evidence for a mere exposure effect

words.enDefinition: an ideal or claimed system in which positions and rewards depend primarily on effort and ability

examples.en: The seminar discussed meritocracy by comparing the stated selection ideal with observed opportunities in the fictional system.
examples.zh: 研讨课通过对照公开声明的选拔理想和虚构制度中的实测机会，讨论「任人唯才制度」。

examples.en: We distinguished the claim of meritocracy from evidence about how qualifications were acquired across the example's groups.
examples.zh: 我们区分「任人唯才制度」的主张与关于示例各群体如何取得资质的证据。

words.enDefinition: the connections and interactions between two or more settings in which the developing person directly participates

examples.en: The lecture uses communication between home and school to illustrate the mesosystem in the fictional child's environment.
examples.zh: 讲义用家庭与学校之间的沟通来说明虚构儿童环境里的「中间系统」。

examples.en: We drew a line between two immediate settings to represent the mesosystem in the ecological model.
examples.zh: 我们在两个直接参与的环境之间画线，表示生态模型中的「中间系统」。

words.enDefinition: knowledge and regulation of one's own thinking, understanding and learning processes

examples.en: The teacher discussed metacognition when learners explained how they knew which part of the passage remained unclear.
examples.zh: 学习者解释自己怎样知道文章哪段还没弄明白时，老师讨论了「元认知」。

examples.en: We used a reflection activity to observe metacognition while students compared their predictions with their actual performance.
examples.zh: 学生对照预测与实际表现时，我们用反思活动观察其「元认知」。

words.enDefinition: changing one's strategies or allocation of mental effort based on evaluation of one's current cognitive state

examples.en: The student showed metacognitive control by spending more review time on the section judged least clear.
examples.zh: 学生把更多复习时间用在自己判断最不清楚的部分，表现出「元认知调节」。

examples.en: We compared metacognitive control in two cases where students knew equally well which material needed review.
examples.zh: 我们比较两种情形的「元认知调节」，两种情形中学生都同样清楚要复习哪些材料。

words.enDefinition: assessing one's current understanding, performance or progress during a cognitive task

examples.en: The worksheet illustrates metacognitive monitoring when students rate their understanding before seeing whether their answers are correct.
examples.zh: 练习中，学生在知道答案是否正确前评估自己的理解程度，说明了「元认知监控」。

examples.en: We discussed which confidence ratings provided evidence of metacognitive monitoring in the classroom reading activity.
examples.zh: 我们讨论课堂阅读活动中的哪些信心评分可作为「元认知监控」的证据。

words.enDefinition: An approach in which observers directly vary a stimulus to meet a perceptual criterion.

examples.en: In the method of adjustment, the classroom observer changed a patch until its brightness matched the reference.
examples.zh: 课堂展示「调整法」时，观察者调整色块，直到它跟参照色块看起来一样亮。

examples.en: The method of adjustment let observers control the comparison stimulus in the example on the slide.
examples.zh: 投影片的示例中，「调整法」让观察者自行控制比较刺激。

collocations: a threshold from the method of adjustment
a brightness match using the method of adjustment

words.enDefinition: An approach presenting fixed stimulus levels repeatedly, typically in randomized order.

examples.en: In the method of constant stimuli, the worksheet listed the same intensity levels in a shuffled sequence.
examples.zh: 习题将相同的几个强度水平打乱呈现，展示了「恒定刺激法」。

examples.en: We plotted the response proportions for the method of constant stimuli using the simulated class data.
examples.zh: 我们用课堂模拟数据画出了「恒定刺激法」下各作答的比例。

collocations: a threshold from the method of constant stimuli
fixed levels in the method of constant stimuli
use the method of constant stimuli

words.enDefinition: An approach estimating a threshold from ordered increasing and decreasing stimulus series.

examples.en: For the method of limits, the handout graphed trials in both increasing and decreasing intensity order.
examples.zh: 讲义把「极限法」中按强度递增和递减呈现的试次分别画了出来。

examples.en: The example marked where responses changed during each series in the method of limits.
examples.zh: 示例在「极限法」的每个序列中标出了作答发生变化的位置。

collocations: estimate a threshold using the method of limits
an ascending sequence in the method of limits
compare the method of limits with constant stimuli

words.enDefinition: Measurement of retention from reduced effort needed to relearn previously studied material

examples.en: The instructor illustrates the method of savings by comparing initial study time with relearning time.
examples.zh: 老师用首次学习时间与重新学习时间的对比来说明「节省法」。

examples.en: We used the method of savings to interpret the shorter relearning time in the sample data.
examples.zh: 我们用「节省法」解释样本数据中较短的重新学习时间。

collocations: measure retention with the method of savings

words.enDefinition: Equality of corresponding factor loadings across groups with a shared factor structure

examples.en: The metric invariance model constrains loadings to be equal in both simulated groups.
examples.zh: 「载荷不变性」模型将两个模拟组的载荷约束为相等。

examples.en: We compared the model with metric invariance against one allowing loadings to differ.
examples.zh: 我们将设有「载荷不变性」约束的模型与允许载荷不同的模型作了比较。

words.enDefinition: the study of relatively small-scale social processes, including encounters and interactions among individuals

examples.en: The microsociology example analyzes how two fictional participants handled a brief misunderstanding during their conversation.
examples.zh: 「微观社会学」示例分析两位虚构参与者在谈话中如何处理短暂误会。

examples.en: We used microsociology to examine the meaning of pauses and gestures in the classroom interaction transcript.
examples.zh: 我们用「微观社会学」考察课堂互动文字稿中停顿和手势的含义。

words.enDefinition: a setting in which the developing person directly takes part in activities and relationships, in ecological systems theory

examples.en: The diagram places the child's classroom in a microsystem because the child interacts directly with people there.
examples.zh: 图将儿童的课堂归为一个「微系统」，因为儿童在此与他人直接互动。

examples.en: We identified a second microsystem by looking for another setting the fictional child regularly took part in.
examples.zh: 我们找出虚构儿童经常直接参与的另一个环境，从而辨认第二个「微系统」。

words.enDefinition: Selectable category positioned at the center of an ordered response scale

examples.en: The mock questionnaire includes a midpoint option labeled neither agree nor disagree.
examples.zh: 模拟问卷有一个标为既不赞同也不反对的「中点选项」。

examples.en: We discussed whether the midpoint option meant neutrality on this particular scale.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了在这个量表中「中点选项」是否表示中立。

words.enDefinition: the philosophical problem of explaining how mental experience relates to physical processes and the body

examples.en: The introduction raised the mind-body problem when comparing descriptions of pain with accounts of neural activity.
examples.zh: 导论在对照疼痛的主观描述与神经活动的解释时，提出了「心身问题」。

examples.en: We discussed why several competing positions address the mind-body problem in different ways in our reading.
examples.zh: 我们讨论指定阅读中几种相互竞争的立场为何以不同方式回答「心身问题」。

words.enDefinition: A research framework using group memberships with little prior meaning to study the effects of categorisation itself.

examples.en: The reading explains how the minimal group paradigm separates group labels from long-standing relationships in a classroom example.
examples.zh: 读物以课堂示例说明，「最简群体范式」如何将群体标签与长期关系区分开来。

examples.en: Our seminar discusses findings reported under the minimal group paradigm without making claims about any existing communities.
examples.zh: 研讨课讨论「最简群体范式」下报告的发现，所用材料未对实际存在的社群下结论。

collocations: research using the minimal group paradigm
findings from a minimal group paradigm

words.enDefinition: In U.S. research regulations, a level of harm or discomfort whose probability and magnitude do not exceed those ordinarily encountered in daily life or routine examinations.

examples.en: The class used a fictional task to discuss minimal risk in the United States research regulations.
examples.zh: 全班用一项虚构任务讨论美国研究法规中的「最小风险」。

examples.en: We read the minimal risk definition before considering the fictional activity described in the review notes.
examples.zh: 我们先阅读「最小风险」的定义，再考察审查笔记中描述的虚构活动。

collocations: assess whether a study involves minimal risk

words.enDefinition: A change in how a group or its members think or act associated with a position held by a minority.

examples.en: The seminar considers minority influence when a few fictional committee members offer an alternative interpretation for discussion.
examples.zh: 少数虚构委员提出另一种解读供讨论，研讨课借此考虑「少数派影响」。

examples.en: Our reading compares minority influence across fictional meetings while tracking whether the team's assessments change over time.
examples.zh: 读物对比了虚构会议中的「少数派影响」，同时追踪团队评价是否随时间发生变化。

words.enDefinition: an observation task using a mirror to look for evidence that an individual recognizes their own reflected image

examples.en: The class discussed the mirror self-recognition test while interpreting possible meanings of the behavior in a recorded example.
examples.zh: 全班解读录像示例中某种行为可能的含义时，讨论了「镜像自我识别测验」。

examples.en: We compared the observation from the mirror self-recognition test with another indicator of self-awareness in the reading.
examples.zh: 我们将「镜像自我识别测验」中的观察与阅读材料中的另一个自我觉察指标比较。

collocations: read about the mirror self-recognition test

words.enDefinition: Distortion of memory by misleading information encountered after an event

examples.en: The lecture illustrates the misinformation effect with an inaccurate account in a fictional study.
examples.zh: 讲座用一项虚构研究中的不准确描述来说明「错误信息效应」。

examples.en: We compared remembered details from two fictional groups to discuss the misinformation effect.
examples.zh: 我们对照了两个虚构小组记得的细节，以讨论「错误信息效应」。

words.enDefinition: The proportion of signal-present trials answered as though no signal was present.

examples.en: The simulated listener had a lower miss rate when the target tone stood out more clearly.
examples.zh: 目标音调更突出时，模拟听者的「漏报率」较低。

examples.en: Our worksheet calculated the miss rate from negative responses on trials that contained the signal.
examples.zh: 习题根据实际有信号时回答未检出的次数计算「漏报率」。

words.enDefinition: A factorial design combining between-participants factors with within-participants factors.

examples.en: The mixed factorial design varied display type between groups, but every participant saw both symbol sizes.
examples.zh: 在「混合析因设计」中，不同组采用不同的显示方式，而每位参与者都会看到两种大小的符号。

examples.en: In the mixed factorial design, the same fictional student contributed results for two levels of one factor.
examples.zh: 在「混合析因设计」中，同一名虚构学生为同一个因素的两个水平都提供了结果。

collocations: a study using a mixed factorial design
analyze data from a mixed factorial design

words.enDefinition: Information available to one eye that contributes to depth perception.

examples.en: The lecture treated overlap as a monocular depth cue because it remained visible in a single image.
examples.zh: 课堂把遮挡视为「单眼深度线索」，因为它在单张图像中也看得见。

examples.en: We found a monocular depth cue in the painted street before discussing the paired camera views.
examples.zh: 我们先在画中的街道上找出一种「单眼深度线索」，再讨论成对的相机视图。

words.enDefinition: changes in moral reasoning, feelings and actions across development

examples.en: The text uses moral development to connect changing judgments of fairness with observations of behavior in peer groups.
examples.zh: 教材用「道德发展」联系公平判断的变化和同伴群体中观察到的行为。

examples.en: We compared moral development examples that involved different kinds of disagreement in the fictional classroom stories.
examples.zh: 我们比较虚构课堂故事中涉及不同类型分歧的「道德发展」示例。

words.enDefinition: a situation in which competing moral considerations support incompatible choices

examples.en: The moral dilemma asks whether preserving a confidence or warning a friend should take priority in the story.
examples.zh: 故事的「道德两难」问，保守秘密和提醒朋友哪一项应该优先。

examples.en: We compared how two groups explained their choices in the same fictional moral dilemma during the seminar.
examples.zh: 研讨课上，我们比较两个小组如何解释自己在同一虚构「道德两难」中的选择。

words.enDefinition: thinking about why an action is right, wrong, fair or unfair under relevant principles or expectations

examples.en: The class analyzed moral reasoning by comparing explanations that led to the same decision in the fictional situation.
examples.zh: 全班对照在虚构情形中导向同一决定的不同解释，以分析「道德推理」。

examples.en: We discussed moral reasoning about sharing after reading contrasting justifications for similar choices in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们读完习题中对相似选择的不同论证后，讨论了关于分享的「道德推理」。

words.enDefinition: social norms carrying strong moral importance for a group and often attracting serious disapproval when violated

examples.en: The worksheet distinguishes mores from ordinary customs by comparing how strongly fictional group members reacted to violations.
examples.zh: 习题比较虚构群体成员对不同违规行为反应的强烈程度，以区分「道德习俗」和普通习惯。

examples.en: We identified which expectations the textbook treated as mores in its example of a community's rules.
examples.zh: 我们辨认教材在社区规则示例中把哪些预期视为「道德习俗」。

words.enDefinition: the smallest part of a language form that carries meaning or a grammatical function

examples.en: The class identified a morpheme that changed the example noun from a singular to a plural form.
examples.zh: 全班辨认出一个使例词名词由单数变成复数的「语素」。

examples.en: We compared a morpheme that can stand alone with one that requires attachment to another form.
examples.zh: 我们把一个可以独立使用的「语素」与一个必须附着在其他形式上的语素比较。

words.enDefinition: Relative image motion of objects at different depths as the viewpoint changes.

examples.en: The animation demonstrated motion parallax when the near trees crossed the picture faster than the distant hills.
examples.zh: 动画展示了「运动视差」，近处树木掠过画面的速度比远处山丘快。

examples.en: The instructor used motion parallax to explain why nearby and distant objects shifted differently during the simulated movement.
examples.zh: 老师用「运动视差」解释为何在模拟移动时，近处和远处物体在视野中移动的方式不同。

words.enDefinition: A single-case design introducing a condition at different times across cases, behaviors, or settings.

examples.en: The multiple-baseline design introduced the new classroom display at different points in each fictional response series.
examples.zh: 「多基线设计」在各条虚构作答序列的不同时间点引入了新的课堂显示方式。

examples.en: We compared when the simulated scores changed with when each condition started in the multiple-baseline design.
examples.zh: 我们比较「多基线设计」中各条件的起始时间与模拟得分发生变化的时间。

collocations: stagger changes in a multiple-baseline design

words.enDefinition: Gardner's proposal that human abilities include several distinct forms of intelligence across different domains

examples.en: The lecture contrasted multiple intelligences theory, which proposes several ability domains, with a single-factor model of intelligence.
examples.zh: 课程将提出多个能力领域的「多元智能理论」与智力单因素模型作比较。

examples.en: We examined how multiple intelligences theory classifies abilities in the textbook before discussing evidence for its distinctions.
examples.zh: 我们先考察教材上的「多元智能理论」如何划分能力，再讨论支持这种划分的证据。

words.enDefinition: Keeping track of several designated moving objects among other objects.

examples.en: The multiple object tracking demonstration asked students to follow three marked dots after their labels disappeared.
examples.zh: 「多目标追踪」演示要求学生在标记消失后继续追踪原先标过的三个圆点。

examples.en: The instructor changed the number of targets to compare multiple object tracking accuracy in the simulation.
examples.zh: 老师改变了目标数量，以比较模拟「多目标追踪」的正确率。

words.enDefinition: Combining information from different senses to produce a coherent percept.

examples.en: The lecture used multisensory integration to explain how listeners combined visible mouth movements with the recorded sounds.
examples.zh: 老师用「多感觉整合」解释听者如何把看到的口型与录音中的声音结合起来。

examples.en: We discussed multisensory integration after comparing how the same clip appeared with and without its soundtrack.
examples.zh: 我们比较同一片段在有无声轨时给人的印象，随后讨论了「多感觉整合」。

words.enDefinition: Repeating a study across multiple locations or research teams under a shared plan.

examples.en: The fictional multisite replication used a common task across several universities and compared the resulting patterns.
examples.zh: 虚构「多地点重复研究」在多所大学采用相同任务，再比较得到的数据模式。

examples.en: We checked which parts of the classroom protocol remained consistent across sites in the multisite replication.
examples.zh: 我们核对了课堂方案中的哪些部分在「多地点重复研究」开展的各地点保持一致。

words.enDefinition: The lightest non-REM stage, marking the transition from wakefulness into sleep.

examples.en: The classroom chart marked N1 sleep where the simulated record first shifted from wakefulness into sleep.
examples.zh: 课堂图表在模拟记录第一次从清醒转入睡眠的位置标出了「非快速眼动一期睡眠」。

examples.en: We distinguished N1 sleep from the later stage marked by spindles in the fictional overnight record.
examples.zh: 我们在虚构的整夜记录中区分了「非快速眼动一期睡眠」与有纺锤波的后续阶段。

words.enDefinition: The non-REM stage marked by sleep spindles or K-complexes under standard scoring.

examples.en: The example marked N2 sleep where the simulated record showed a spindle after the earlier stage.
examples.zh: 示例在前一阶段结束后出现纺锤波的模拟记录部分标出了「非快速眼动二期睡眠」。

examples.en: We checked which characteristic waveform supported the classroom label for N2 sleep in the sample.
examples.zh: 我们核对样本中的哪种特征波形为课堂标注「非快速眼动二期睡眠」提供了依据。

words.enDefinition: The deepest non-REM stage, characterized by prominent slow brain waves.

examples.en: The synthetic trace showed the slow waves used to identify N3 sleep in the class exercise.
examples.zh: 合成波形展示了课上用于辨认「非快速眼动三期睡眠」的慢波。

examples.en: We marked the periods of N3 sleep on the chart before looking at the stage distribution.
examples.zh: 我们先在图表上标出「非快速眼动三期睡眠」的各个时段，再查看睡眠阶段的分布。

words.enDefinition: the evolving life story that ties together who you understand yourself to be

examples.en: The fictional interview illustrates narrative identity through the way a character connects past experiences with future goals.
examples.zh: 虚构访谈通过一名角色把过往经历和未来目标相联的方式，说明「叙事认同」。

examples.en: Our personality seminar considers how narrative identity changes when fictional characters reinterpret important events in their lives.
examples.zh: 人格研讨课讨论，虚构角色重新解读人生中的重要事件时，「叙事认同」会如何变化。

words.enDefinition: a category typically learned from everyday encounters, often without a single precise definition

examples.en: The worksheet uses the category of fruit to illustrate a natural concept containing typical and atypical members.
examples.zh: 练习用水果这一类别，说明「自然概念」可包含典型及非典型成员。

examples.en: We discussed why a natural concept could be used consistently without listing a strict defining rule.
examples.zh: 我们讨论为什么即使不列严格定义规则，人们仍能一致地使用一个「自然概念」。

words.enDefinition: Watching and recording behavior in its usual setting without manipulating conditions.

examples.en: The class discussed naturalistic observation using a fictional account of how students chose seats during ordinary breaks.
examples.zh: 全班用一段学生平常休息时如何选座的虚构描述，讨论了「自然观察」。

examples.en: The naturalistic observation example recorded ordinary classroom activity without changing the room or giving a special task.
examples.zh: 「自然观察」示例记录普通课堂活动，没有改变教室环境，也没有布置专门任务。

words.enDefinition: discussion of how inherited influences and experience contribute to psychological characteristics and interact in development

examples.en: The tutor introduced the nature-nurture debate with a fictional example of children acquiring a classroom skill.
examples.zh: 老师以儿童学习一项课堂技能的虚构示例引入「先天与后天之争」。

examples.en: We considered how a developmental model could answer questions raised by the nature-nurture debate in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们讨论一种发展模型怎样回答「先天与后天之争」提出的问题。

collocations: evidence relevant to the nature-nurture debate

words.enDefinition: Decrease in behavior because a stimulus is removed after that behavior

examples.en: In the simulation, negative punishment occurs when losing points reduces a particular move.
examples.zh: 在模拟中，扣分使某一动作减少，体现了「负惩罚」。

examples.en: The checklist identifies negative punishment using both the point loss and the declining response.
examples.zh: 核对表根据分数损失和反应减弱这两个现象识别「负惩罚」。

collocations: distinguish negative punishment from negative reinforcement

words.enDefinition: Increase in behavior because that behavior removes or prevents a stimulus

examples.en: The worksheet depicts negative reinforcement when silencing an alert makes a button press more frequent.
examples.zh: 习题用按键让提示音停止、此后按键更频繁的情形说明「负强化」。

examples.en: In the lecture, negative reinforcement was identified by an increase in the response rate.
examples.zh: 讲座以反应频率上升来识别「负强化」。

words.enDefinition: an unfavorable social response that discourages conduct considered to violate a group expectation

examples.en: The example presents a mild negative sanction when group members express disapproval of a fictional rule violation.
examples.zh: 示例中，群体成员对虚构违规行为表达不赞同，这是一种轻度「负向制裁」。

examples.en: We compared two forms of negative sanction described in the classroom account of the same routine disruption.
examples.zh: 我们比较关于同一次常规中断的课堂叙述中描述的两种「负向制裁」形式。

words.enDefinition: Worse performance on a new task attributable to prior practice or learning

examples.en: The negative transfer example shows old button habits interfering with a new layout.
examples.zh: 「负迁移」的例子显示，原先的按键习惯妨碍了对新布局的使用。

examples.en: We identified negative transfer when the trained group initially made more selection errors.
examples.zh: 经过练习的小组起初出现更多选择错误，我们由此辨认出「负迁移」。

words.enDefinition: A broad personality dimension reflecting a tendency to experience negative emotions, such as worry or distress, more readily.

examples.en: The fictional personality chart uses neuroticism as a trait dimension within a general model of personality.
examples.zh: 虚构人格图表把「神经质倾向」作为一般人格模型所含的一个特质维度。

examples.en: We discussed why the class example describes neuroticism using typical reactions across a long period of time.
examples.zh: 我们讨论课堂示例为什么用长期的典型反应来描述「神经质倾向」。

words.enDefinition: Stimulus that initially does not elicit the response being studied

examples.en: The square begins as a neutral stimulus in the illustrated conditioning task.
examples.zh: 在图示的条件作用任务中，方块最初是「中性刺激」。

examples.en: We looked for a neutral stimulus before any learned response appeared in the animation.
examples.zh: 我们在动画出现任何习得反应之前寻找「中性刺激」。

words.enDefinition: Sleep outside the REM stage, classified into N1, N2, and N3.

examples.en: The teaching diagram used three separate labels for the stages of non-REM sleep in the example.
examples.zh: 教学示意图为示例中的「非快速眼动睡眠」三个阶段分别设置了标签。

examples.en: We tallied time in non-REM sleep before comparing it with the shorter intervals in the other category.
examples.zh: 我们先统计「非快速眼动睡眠」的时长，再与另一类中较短的时段对照。

words.enDefinition: Experience-dependent change in responsiveness without learning an association between events

examples.en: The textbook uses a repeated sound to introduce nonassociative learning in the first paragraph.
examples.zh: 教材第一段用反复播放的声音来介绍「非联结学习」。

examples.en: We classified the declining response to a single tone as nonassociative learning.
examples.zh: 我们把对同一音调逐渐减弱的反应归为「非联结学习」。

words.enDefinition: A hypothesis predicting a difference or relationship without specifying its direction.

examples.en: The nondirectional hypothesis predicted different scores for the two layouts without specifying which would score higher.
examples.zh: 「无方向假设」预测两种布局的得分会不同，但未说明哪种更高。

examples.en: We chose a nondirectional hypothesis because earlier classroom examples supported both possible directions for the difference.
examples.zh: 先前的课堂例子指向不同方向，所以我们选择了「无方向假设」。

words.enDefinition: A quasi-experiment comparing preexisting groups that may differ before the study condition.

examples.en: The nonequivalent groups design compared two existing classes whose fictional starting scores were already different.
examples.zh: 「非等组设计」对比两个已有的班级，它们的虚构起始得分本来就不同。

examples.en: We checked the starting scores because the nonequivalent groups design did not make the groups comparable automatically.
examples.zh: 我们核对了初始得分，因为「非等组设计」本身并不能让各组具有可比性。

collocations: a limitation of a nonequivalent groups design
baseline scores in a nonequivalent groups design

words.enDefinition: A study design that examines variables without deliberately manipulating them.

examples.en: The nonexperimental design relied on existing activity logs instead of changing anyone's classroom routine.
examples.zh: 「非实验设计」使用已有的活动日志，不改变任何人的课堂日常。

examples.en: We identified the nonexperimental design because the fictional researchers recorded activity without changing the existing routine.
examples.zh: 虚构研究者记录活动，但保留既有流程，我们据此判断这是「非实验设计」。

collocations: a study with a nonexperimental design
interpret findings from a nonexperimental design

words.enDefinition: the shared meanings, beliefs, norms and other intangible elements of a group's way of life

examples.en: The text uses a shared idea about politeness to illustrate nonmaterial culture in the fictional community.
examples.zh: 教材用对礼貌的共同看法说明虚构社区的「非物质文化」。

examples.en: We examined nonmaterial culture by comparing the meanings associated with a greeting in two different situations.
examples.zh: 我们比较两个不同情境里与问候相关的含义，以考察「非物质文化」。

words.enDefinition: a life event not commonly experienced at the same age or by most members of a population

examples.en: In the case study, an unexpected relocation was a nonnormative life event for the fictional teenager.
examples.zh: 个案研究中，一次意外迁居是虚构青少年经历的「非规范性生活事件」。

examples.en: We discussed how the same nonnormative life event might affect two fictional people with different resources.
examples.zh: 我们讨论同一个「非规范性生活事件」如何可能影响资源不同的两个虚构人物。

collocations: effect of a nonnormative life event
adapt to a nonnormative life event

words.enDefinition: Observing an activity without taking part in it.

examples.en: In the nonparticipant observation example, the researcher watched the mock group activity without joining the discussion.
examples.zh: 在「非参与式观察」示例中，研究者观看模拟小组活动，没有参加讨论。

examples.en: We discussed how nonparticipant observation shaped what the fictional researcher could learn about the group's decisions.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「非参与式观察」如何影响虚构研究者能从小组决策中了解的内容。

words.zhGloss: 非一致性项目功能差异
words.enDefinition: Group effect on item responses that varies with measured trait level
acceptedZhAnswers: 非一致性项目功能差异
非均一性项目功能差异

examples.en: The exercise illustrates nonuniform differential item functioning because the group difference changes with trait level.
examples.zh: 习题中的组间差异随特质水平变化，体现了「非一致性项目功能差异」。

examples.en: The sample plot illustrates nonuniform differential item functioning even though the group curves never cross.
examples.zh: 尽管两组曲线从未相交，样本图依然展示了「非一致性项目功能差异」。

collocations: test for nonuniform differential item functioning
evidence of nonuniform differential item functioning

words.enDefinition: Reference group whose scores provide a comparison for individual test scores

examples.en: The fictional manual describes the norm group before explaining how to interpret scores.
examples.zh: 虚构手册先描述「常模群体」，再说明如何解读分数。

examples.en: We compared the norm group in the workbook with the intended test population.
examples.zh: 我们把练习册里的「常模群体」与预定的测验对象作了对照。

words.enDefinition: A social expectation that people return benefits or assistance they have received.

examples.en: The fictional study group illustrates the norm of reciprocity when members feel obliged to return each other's favours.
examples.zh: 虚构学习小组成员觉得应当回报彼此的帮助，体现了「互惠规范」。

examples.en: Our tutor distinguishes the norm of reciprocity from a formal exchange agreement in the fictional club's rules.
examples.zh: 老师把「互惠规范」与虚构社团规则中的正式交换协议区分开。

collocations: social expectations under the norm of reciprocity
influence of the norm of reciprocity

words.enDefinition: Interpretation that compares a score with those of a designated reference group

examples.en: In the norm-referenced interpretation example, the score is compared with a reference distribution.
examples.zh: 在「常模参照解释」示例中，该得分和一个参照分布相比较。

examples.en: We discussed how norm-referenced interpretation differs from reporting a student's mastery of specific material.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「常模参照解释」与报告学生对特定内容的掌握程度有何不同。

words.enDefinition: Table giving score comparisons or conversions based on a reference group

examples.en: The workbook includes a norm table for converting example scores into percentile ranks.
examples.zh: 练习册给出一张「常模表」，用于把示例分数换算成百分等级。

examples.en: Our tutor pointed out the reference group described above the norm table.
examples.zh: 老师指出了「常模表」上方说明的参照群体。

collocations: locate a value in the norm table

words.enDefinition: a developmental influence commonly associated with a particular age or stage in a given society

examples.en: The course uses starting school as a normative age-graded influence in the context of the fictional community.
examples.zh: 课程在虚构社区背景下，把入学作为一种「规范性年龄相关影响」。

examples.en: We discussed how the timing of the normative age-graded influence differed across the two example communities.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「规范性年龄相关影响」发生的时间如何在两个示例社区间不同。

collocations: example of a normative age-graded influence
adapt to a normative age-graded influence

words.enDefinition: changes in cognitive abilities commonly associated with aging outside a specified disease process

examples.en: The lecture on normative cognitive aging compared abilities that often stay relatively stable with those that may change.
examples.zh: 关于「典型认知老化」的讲义，对照了通常相对稳定的能力和可能改变的能力。

examples.en: We discussed individual differences in normative cognitive aging after looking at age group averages in the synthetic table.
examples.zh: 我们查看合成表中的各年龄组均值后，讨论「典型认知老化」中的个体差异。

words.enDefinition: an event or broad change that influences many people who live through the same historical period

examples.en: The reading treats the arrival of a new communication medium as a normative history-graded influence for one cohort.
examples.zh: 阅读材料把一种新传播媒介的出现作为对某一世代的「规范性历史时期影响」。

examples.en: We compared a normative history-graded influence with a transition common at a particular age in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们比较「规范性历史时期影响」与在某个年龄常见的一种转折。

collocations: cohort exposed to a normative history-graded influence
example of a normative history-graded influence

words.enDefinition: Social influence motivated by wanting acceptance or avoiding disapproval from other people.

examples.en: The class discusses normative social influence when a fictional character agrees publicly and later reports wanting acceptance.
examples.zh: 虚构角色当众表示赞同，后来坦言希望被接纳，全班以此讨论「规范性社会影响」。

examples.en: Our seminar contrasts normative social influence with a situation in which group input provides useful new information.
examples.zh: 研讨课把「规范性社会影响」与小组意见提供了有用新信息的情形作比较。

words.enDefinition: Following an instruction or order given by a person perceived to hold authority.

examples.en: The classroom vignette illustrates obedience to authority when a fictional student follows the instructor's direction to stop writing.
examples.zh: 课堂材料用虚构学生按老师指示停笔的例子说明「服从权威」。

examples.en: Our seminar separates obedience to authority from group conformity in the examples assigned for the week's reading.
examples.zh: 研讨课将本周读物例子中的「服从权威」与群体从众区分开来。

words.enDefinition: the understanding that an object continues to exist when it is no longer directly perceived

examples.en: The lesson illustrates object permanence when the animated child searches for a toy that has been covered.
examples.zh: 动画里的儿童寻找被遮住的玩具时，课程用这一行为说明「客体永久性」。

examples.en: We discussed how different tasks can provide different kinds of evidence for object permanence in the reading.
examples.zh: 我们讨论指定阅读中，不同任务如何为「客体永久性」提供不同类型的证据。

words.enDefinition: A specified plan for when, where, and how observations are made.

examples.en: The observation protocol listed which visible actions the classroom exercise would record during the short clip.
examples.zh: 「观察方案」列出了课堂练习观看短片时要记录的可见行为。

examples.en: We compared each observation protocol before deciding whether two simulated teams watched the same type of activity.
examples.zh: 在判断两个模拟小组是否观察同一类活动之前，我们对照了各自的「观察方案」。

collocations: the criteria in an observation protocol

words.enDefinition: Acquisition of behavior or knowledge through watching another person's actions

examples.en: The classroom exercise shows observational learning through a silent demonstration of paper folding.
examples.zh: 课堂练习通过无声的折纸演示说明「观察学习」。

examples.en: We used observational learning to explain why participants copied the unfamiliar hand movement.
examples.zh: 我们用「观察学习」解释参与者为何会模仿陌生的手部动作。

words.enDefinition: Measured variable used to represent an attribute in a statistical model

examples.en: The diagram treats each recorded answer as an observed indicator of the proposed construct.
examples.zh: 示意图将每项记录下来的答案视为拟研究构念的一个「观测指标」。

examples.en: We discussed why an observed indicator can reflect influences outside the target construct.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么一个「观测指标」也可能反映目标构念以外的因素。

collocations: link an observed indicator to a factor

words.enDefinition: Score actually obtained from a specified testing occasion and scoring procedure

examples.en: Each simulated row contains an observed score alongside the label for its testing occasion.
examples.zh: 模拟数据每行都有一个「观测分数」与对应的施测场次标签。

examples.en: The worksheet compares an observed score with the average across hypothetical repeated measurements.
examples.zh: 习题把一个「观测分数」与多次假设施测的平均值作了比较。

words.enDefinition: A systematic distortion in records due to what an observer expects or believes.

examples.en: The worksheet discussed observer bias when fictional observers classified unclear gestures in line with what they expected.
examples.zh: 虚构观察者按照预期分类含糊的动作，习题就此讨论了「观察者偏差」。

examples.en: We considered observer bias before interpreting the difference between two teams watching the same classroom clip.
examples.zh: 在解读观看同一课堂短片的两个小组记录有何差异前，我们先考虑了「观察者偏差」。

collocations: a possible source of observer bias

words.enDefinition: A gradual change in how an observer applies the original recording rules.

examples.en: The tutor looked for observer drift after the fictional coders began classifying similar gestures differently over time.
examples.zh: 虚构编码员逐渐以不同方式分类相似动作后，辅导老师检查是否出现了「观察者编码漂移」。

examples.en: We checked early and late sample clips for observer drift using the same set of category definitions.
examples.zh: 我们用同一套类别定义检查早期和后期的样例短片，查看是否有「观察者编码漂移」。

words.enDefinition: Ordered scoring tool used to rate attributes based on observed behavior

examples.en: The fictional observer rating scale records judgments about how consistently a character completes tasks.
examples.zh: 虚构的「观察者评定量表」记录对角色完成任务是否稳定的判断。

examples.en: Our class compared the observer rating scale with reports from the fictional participants themselves.
examples.zh: 课堂把「观察者评定量表」与虚构作答者本人的报告作了比较。

collocations: scores on an observer rating scale

words.enDefinition: the social standing or esteem associated with an occupation in a specified setting

examples.en: The fictional survey asked about occupational prestige separately from how much people in the same occupations earned.
examples.zh: 虚构调查对「职业声望」和相关职业人员获得多少报酬分别提问。

examples.en: We compared occupational prestige rankings across two survey settings before discussing how they might differ by context.
examples.zh: 我们对照两个调查环境的「职业声望」排名，再讨论环境怎样影响两者差异。

words.enDefinition: A failure to respond when the task calls for a response.

examples.en: An omission error occurred when the fictional observer failed to press a key for the target symbol.
examples.zh: 虚构观察者在目标符号出现时没有按键，产生了一次「漏答错误」。

examples.en: We counted an omission error only when the classroom task required a response on that trial.
examples.zh: 只有课堂任务要求在该试次作答时，我们才将未作答记作「漏答错误」。

collocations: a trial with an omission error

words.enDefinition: Research materials made publicly available for others to inspect or reuse under stated terms.

examples.en: The fictional study shared open materials so the class could examine the wording of the task instructions.
examples.zh: 虚构研究共享了「开放研究材料」，全班得以查看任务指导语的措辞。

examples.en: We looked for open materials that included the example stimuli and a description of the response options.
examples.zh: 我们寻找包含示例刺激及作答选项说明的「开放研究材料」。

words.enDefinition: A broad personality dimension involving receptiveness to ideas, imagination, and a range of experiences.

examples.en: In our fictional profiles, curiosity about unfamiliar art provides one example of behaviour associated with openness to experience.
examples.zh: 在虚构人物画像中，对陌生艺术形式感到好奇是与「经验开放性」有关的一种行为示例。

examples.en: The tutor uses openness to experience to explain why the example contains several different kinds of curiosity.
examples.zh: 老师用「经验开放性」来说明，为什么示例包含几种不同类型的好奇心。

words.enDefinition: Learning in which consequences change the future frequency of behavior

examples.en: The course introduces operant conditioning with a simple simulation of choices and points.
examples.zh: 课程用一个选择与得分的简单模拟来介绍「操作性条件作用」。

examples.en: Our group compared operant conditioning with learning that links two events on the screen.
examples.zh: 我们组比较了「操作性条件作用」和对屏幕上两个事件建立联结的学习。

words.enDefinition: Decline in an operant behavior after its prior reinforcement stops

examples.en: In the animation, operant extinction begins when correct clicks stop producing points.
examples.zh: 在动画中，正确点击停止得分后开始出现「操作性消退」。

examples.en: We compared how rapidly operant extinction occurred across the two simulated games.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个模拟游戏中「操作性消退」发生的速度。

words.enDefinition: Behavior whose future occurrence is affected by the consequences it produces

examples.en: The simulation counts each press of the green button as an operant response.
examples.zh: 模拟把每次按绿色按钮都计为一次「操作性反应」。

examples.en: We graphed the operant response frequencies shown for the two levels of the game.
examples.zh: 我们把游戏两个关卡的「操作性反应」次数画成了图。

words.enDefinition: A precise specification of how a variable will be measured or manipulated.

examples.en: Our operational definition counted a response as correct only when it matched the target letter exactly.
examples.zh: 根据我们的「操作性定义」，只有作答与目标字母完全相同才算正确。

examples.en: The class compared each operational definition before deciding whether the two studies measured the same behavior.
examples.zh: 判断两项研究是否测量同一种行为之前，全班先对照了各自的「操作性定义」。

collocations: give an operational definition of a variable

words.enDefinition: Turning a theoretical concept into a specific measurement or experimental procedure.

examples.en: The operationalization of persistence involved deciding which observable attempts would count in the classroom task.
examples.zh: 在对坚持性进行「操作化」时，我们决定课堂任务中哪些可观察的尝试应计入统计。

examples.en: We compared two approaches to operationalization by asking what each task outcome could actually capture.
examples.zh: 我们通过询问每种任务结果实际能反映什么，比较了两种「操作化」方法。

words.enDefinition: A change in performance attributable to when a condition is experienced in a sequence.

examples.en: The simulated results suggested an order effect because both groups responded faster in their second block.
examples.zh: 模拟结果提示存在「顺序效应」，因为两组在第二个任务区段都作答得更快。

examples.en: We separated the order effect from the display effect by checking which task each group completed first.
examples.zh: 我们核对各组先做哪项任务，以区分「顺序效应」和显示方式的影响。

collocations: an order effect in repeated testing

words.enDefinition: Response options with a meaningful order but no assumed equal spacing

examples.en: The example lists ordinal response categories from rarely to often without assuming equal gaps.
examples.zh: 例子将「有序作答类别」从很少到经常排列，并未假定各级间距相等。

examples.en: Our tutor explained why numbers assigned to ordinal response categories need not represent equal distances.
examples.zh: 老师解释了为什么给「有序作答类别」分配的数值并不一定表示相等的间距。

words.enDefinition: in Durkheim's theory, cohesion based largely on interdependence among people and roles performing different specialized tasks

examples.en: The classroom diagram shows organic solidarity by linking specialized roles that rely on other people for different services.
examples.zh: 课堂图将依赖他人提供不同服务的专业化角色连接起来，展示「有机团结」。

examples.en: We identified organic solidarity as the form of cohesion highlighted by the example of an interdependent society.
examples.zh: 我们将相互依赖社会的示例所突出的凝聚方式辨认为「有机团结」。

words.enDefinition: A tendency to perceive members of other groups as more alike than members of one's own group.

examples.en: The worksheet illustrates the out-group homogeneity effect with fictional students' ratings of similarity within two campus clubs.
examples.zh: 练习单以虚构学生对两个校园社团内成员相似程度的评分说明「外群体同质性效应」。

examples.en: Our class counted the varied opinions in each group before discussing the out-group homogeneity effect in the example.
examples.zh: 全班先清点各组的不同意见，再讨论示例中的「外群体同质性效应」。

collocations: evidence for an out-group homogeneity effect

words.enDefinition: a tendency for confidence in judgments or performance to exceed the accuracy justified by the evidence

examples.en: The classroom quiz suggested overconfidence bias because mean confidence ratings exceeded accuracy on the same questions.
examples.zh: 在课堂测验中，相同题目的平均信心百分比高于正确率，提示出现了「过度自信偏差」。

examples.en: We plotted overconfidence bias by comparing the predicted and observed accuracy across the practice questions in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们对照练习题的预测准确率与观测准确率，将「过度自信偏差」画成图。

words.enDefinition: Reduced learning about one cue presented alongside a more salient cue

examples.en: The simulation illustrates overshadowing when a bright color dominates a faint pattern.
examples.zh: 模拟用鲜亮的颜色比淡淡的图案更显眼的情形说明「遮蔽效应」。

examples.en: We compared overshadowing across cue pairs with very different levels of visibility.
examples.zh: 我们比较了明显程度相差很大的不同线索对之间的「遮蔽效应」。

words.enDefinition: Directing attention while visibly orienting the eyes or other sensory organs.

examples.en: The example labeled overt attention when the observer moved their eyes toward the highlighted shape.
examples.zh: 例子把观察者将目光移向高亮形状的情形标为「外显注意」。

examples.en: We watched for overt attention in the recording by noting whether gaze moved with the target.
examples.zh: 我们记录目光是否随目标而移动，据此观察录像中的「外显注意」。

words.enDefinition: play in which children carry out similar or separate activities near one another with little direct coordination

examples.en: The recording shows parallel play as two children build separately with similar blocks at the same table.
examples.zh: 录像中，两名儿童在同一桌旁用类似积木分别搭建，展示了「平行游戏」。

examples.en: We compared parallel play with the next classroom clip, in which the children shared a goal.
examples.zh: 我们将「平行游戏」和下一段课堂视频比较，后者中儿童有共同目标。

words.enDefinition: the degree to which a parent sets expectations, monitors conduct or requires maturity in the stated parenting framework

examples.en: The reading uses parental demandingness to describe expectations and monitoring across several fictional household examples.
examples.zh: 阅读材料用「家长要求性」描述数个虚构家庭示例中的要求和监督。

examples.en: We mapped parental demandingness to one axis of the chart categorizing approaches to parenting in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们将「家长要求性」放在养育取向分类图的一条轴上。

words.enDefinition: the extent to which a parent responds warmly and appropriately to a child's needs, cues or perspective

examples.en: The class coded parental responsiveness by observing whether the adult in the fictional clip acknowledged the child's request.
examples.zh: 全班通过观察虚构片段中的成人是否回应儿童的请求，对「家长回应性」进行编码。

examples.en: We discussed parental responsiveness separately from the number of household rules in the example table.
examples.zh: 我们分别讨论示例表里的「家长回应性」和家庭规则的数量。

words.enDefinition: Rasch-family model relating probabilities of adjacent ordered score categories to ability

examples.en: The exercise uses a partial credit model for items scored zero, one, or two.
examples.zh: 练习对计零、一或二分的题目使用了「部分计分模型」。

examples.en: We identified which steps the partial credit model associated with moving between adjacent scores.
examples.zh: 我们辨认出了「部分计分模型」中对应于相邻分值转换的步骤参数。

collocations: thresholds in a partial credit model

words.enDefinition: Scoring an interval positive when a target behavior occurs at any point within it.

examples.en: Partial-interval recording marked the segment even when the fictional student looked away only once very briefly.
examples.zh: 即使虚构学生只短暂移开目光一次，「部分区间记录」也为该时段作标记。

examples.en: We used partial-interval recording to score the sample without measuring how long each movement lasted.
examples.zh: 我们用「部分区间记录」给样本评分，没有测量每个动作持续了多长时间。

words.enDefinition: Measurement equivalence after allowing some parameters to vary across comparison groups

examples.en: The fictional example illustrates partial measurement invariance by allowing one item intercept to differ.
examples.zh: 虚构示例允许一道题的截距不同，从而说明「部分测量不变性」。

examples.en: We discussed partial measurement invariance after noticing that most constraints fit the synthetic data.
examples.zh: 我们发现大部分约束与合成数据吻合，随后讨论了「部分测量不变性」。

words.enDefinition: Greater response persistence during extinction after intermittent than continuous reinforcement

examples.en: The hypothetical chart illustrates the partial reinforcement extinction effect after points stop appearing.
examples.zh: 假设图表说明了积分停止出现后的「部分强化消退效应」。

examples.en: We discussed the partial reinforcement extinction effect by comparing responding during two simulated extinction phases.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个模拟消退阶段的反应情况，由此讨论「部分强化消退效应」。

collocations: test the partial reinforcement extinction effect
demonstrate a partial reinforcement extinction effect
account for the partial reinforcement extinction effect

words.enDefinition: Payment or another benefit offered for taking part in a study.

examples.en: The mock study notice stated the participant compensation before describing how long the classroom activity would take.
examples.zh: 模拟研究公告先列出「参与者报酬」，再说明课堂活动需要多长时间。

examples.en: We read the participant compensation clause and noted whether it covered a partially completed session in the example.
examples.zh: 我们阅读「参与者报酬」条款，留意例题是否规定了活动只完成一部分时的报酬。

words.enDefinition: A participant's belief about a study that may influence their response.

examples.en: The example discussed participant expectancy when fictional students predicted that one layout would make reading easier.
examples.zh: 虚构学生预期一种布局更易读，例题借此讨论了「参与者期望」。

examples.en: We compared participant expectancy with actual performance to see whether the two followed the same pattern.
examples.zh: 我们将「参与者期望」与实际表现作比较，看看两者是否呈现相同模式。

words.enDefinition: A separate record linking participant codes to identifying information.

examples.en: The case description said the participant identification key was held separately from the fictional response file.
examples.zh: 案例说明中，「参与者身份对应表」与虚构作答文件分开保存。

examples.en: The ethics exercise contrasted the participant identification key with the code labels visible in the analysis table.
examples.zh: 伦理练习对比了「参与者身份对应表」与分析表中可见的编号标签。

collocations: store the participant identification key separately

words.enDefinition: Observing a group while taking part in its activities.

examples.en: The fictional researcher used participant observation by joining the club's scheduled activities and then writing notes.
examples.zh: 虚构研究者参加社团定期活动，再写下笔记，以此进行「参与式观察」。

examples.en: We discussed participant observation after reading how the classroom example combined taking part with keeping field notes.
examples.zh: 读完课堂示例如何结合参与活动与记录田野笔记之后，我们讨论了「参与式观察」。
