words.enDefinition: A group of people available to be invited to research studies.

examples.en: The fictional department used its participant pool to advertise a voluntary classroom study about reading tasks.
examples.zh: 虚构院系通过「研究参与者库」发布一项关于阅读任务的自愿课堂研究。

examples.en: We read the participant pool notice to see who could browse the available studies in the example.
examples.zh: 我们阅读「研究参与者库」通知，看看例子中哪些人可以浏览开放报名的研究。

words.enDefinition: Behavioral changes resulting from awareness of being observed or measured.

examples.en: The exercise considered participant reactivity after fictional students changed how they discussed the task once observation began.
examples.zh: 虚构学生在观察开始后改变了讨论任务的方式，练习就此考察了「参与者反应性」。

examples.en: We compared two reports to see whether the behavior change might reflect participant reactivity in the simulation.
examples.zh: 我们比较两份报告，看看模拟中的行为变化是否可能反映了「参与者反应性」。

collocations: a possible source of participant reactivity

words.enDefinition: An announcement describing a study and inviting eligible people to consider joining.

examples.en: The participant recruitment notice in the exercise stated the expected time and what the task involved.
examples.zh: 练习中的「参与者招募公告」写明了预计用时和任务内容。

examples.en: We read the participant recruitment notice to see whether it clearly described who could take part.
examples.zh: 我们阅读「参与者招募公告」，查看它是否明确说明了哪些人可以参加。

words.enDefinition: Repayment of eligible costs someone incurs by participating in a study.

examples.en: The fictional notice described participant reimbursement for travel separately from payment for time spent in the study.
examples.zh: 虚构公告分开说明了交通方面的「参与者费用报销」和对研究参与时间的补偿。

examples.en: We checked which travel costs the participant reimbursement section listed in the example information sheet.
examples.zh: 我们核对示例信息表的「参与者费用报销」部分列出了哪些交通费用。

words.enDefinition: the degree to which someone is liked, included or accepted by members of a peer group

examples.en: The fictional class scenario illustrates peer acceptance by showing who is invited to join ordinary shared activities.
examples.zh: 虚构班级情景通过展示谁会被邀请参加普通集体活动，说明「同伴接纳」。

examples.en: We compared peer acceptance across different settings rather than treating a single invitation as conclusive in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们对照不同情境中的「同伴接纳」，一次邀请可作为多个观察依据之一。

words.enDefinition: a pattern of disliking, excluding or refusing someone within a peer group, as assessed in a stated context

examples.en: The study notes distinguish peer rejection from a fictional student simply spending some time alone during lunch.
examples.zh: 研究笔记区分「同伴排斥」与虚构学生在午餐时单独度过一段时间。

examples.en: We read an example of peer rejection in which repeated exclusion was recorded across several activities.
examples.zh: 我们阅读「同伴排斥」示例，其中记录了多个活动里一再发生的排斥。

words.enDefinition: In the theory of planned behaviour, a person's perception of how possible or difficult performing an action will be.

examples.en: Our worksheet uses perceived behavioural control to discuss how manageable the fictional volunteer task seems to each character.
examples.zh: 练习单用「感知行为控制」讨论每个虚构角色认为志愿任务有多容易做到。

examples.en: The seminar separates perceived behavioural control from the resources actually recorded for the same fictional activity.
examples.zh: 研讨课将「感知行为控制」与同一虚构活动中实际记录的资源分开。

collocations: perceived behavioural control over an action

words.enDefinition: Percentage of reference scores below a value, with ties treated by convention

examples.en: The fictional report gives a percentile rank alongside the number of questions answered correctly.
examples.zh: 虚构报告在答对题数旁边给出了一个「百分等级」。

examples.en: We checked which reference distribution the percentile rank came from in the sample table.
examples.zh: 我们核对了样表里的「百分等级」来自哪个参照分布。

words.enDefinition: Perceiving stable properties despite changes in the sensory information reaching the observer.

examples.en: The lecture introduced perceptual constancy by showing the same objects under changes in viewpoint and illumination.
examples.zh: 课堂通过展示视角和光照改变时的同一批物体，引入了「知觉恒常性」。

examples.en: Perceptual constancy explained why the classroom display still looked stable as the simulated observer moved around it.
examples.zh: 「知觉恒常性」解释了为什么模拟观察者走动时，课堂展示中的物体看起来仍然稳定。

words.enDefinition: The experience of distinct elements as members of a common perceptual unit.

examples.en: The Gestalt demonstration showed perceptual grouping when students saw rows instead of a collection of individual dots.
examples.zh: 格式塔演示中，学生看到一排排的圆点，这个例子展示了「知觉分组」。

examples.en: The handout used changes in spacing and shape to illustrate two cues for perceptual grouping.
examples.zh: 讲义用间距和形状的变化说明两种「知觉分组」线索。

words.enDefinition: The arrangement of sensory information into coherent objects and patterns.

examples.en: The slides illustrated perceptual organization by rearranging the same dots into several apparently different patterns.
examples.zh: 投影片把同样的圆点重新排列，使人看出几种不同的图案，借此说明「知觉组织」。

examples.en: Our discussion of perceptual organization began with a drawing whose foreground and background looked equally plausible.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「知觉组织」时，先看了一幅前景与背景都同样说得通的图。

words.enDefinition: The ability to distinguish a stimulus or signal from alternatives or background noise.

examples.en: The simulated listeners had similar perceptual sensitivity despite using different criteria for reporting the faint tone.
examples.zh: 两位模拟听者报告微弱音调的标准不同，「知觉敏感性」却相近。

examples.en: We compared perceptual sensitivity across the two noise conditions instead of counting only positive responses.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两种噪声条件下的「知觉敏感性」，没有只统计回答检出的次数。

words.enDefinition: A readiness to interpret ambiguous sensory input in a particular way.

examples.en: The preceding picture created a perceptual set that influenced how students interpreted the ambiguous drawing.
examples.zh: 前一幅图形成了「知觉定势」，影响学生解读含义不明确的图画。

examples.en: The class compared how a perceptual set changed after seeing different titles for the same image.
examples.zh: 全班比较了同一图像配上不同标题后，「知觉定势」发生的变化。

collocations: a perceptual set induced by context
the effects of a perceptual set

words.enDefinition: a pattern of parenting described as relatively responsive while setting or enforcing fewer demands or limits

examples.en: The classroom vignette illustrates a permissive parenting style with warm responses and few consistently enforced expectations at home.
examples.zh: 课堂短情景用温暖回应和很少持续执行的家庭要求来展示「宽容型养育方式」。

examples.en: We identified the permissive parenting style from the pattern of responsiveness and demands in the textbook table.
examples.zh: 我们根据教材表格中回应与要求构成的模式，辨认出「宽容型养育方式」。

collocations: example of a permissive parenting style
compare a permissive parenting style with other styles

words.enDefinition: The process of noticing and interpreting information about other people.

examples.en: The social psychology class introduces person perception using two fictional accounts of the same group discussion.
examples.zh: 社会心理学课用对同一场小组讨论的两份虚构记述介绍「人际知觉」。

examples.en: Our person perception exercise asks how students interpreted a character's brief response in the fictional scene.
examples.zh: 「人际知觉」练习询问，学生怎样理解虚构场景中某个角色的简短回应。

words.enDefinition: The debate about how much stable personality characteristics and features of the situation explain behaviour.

examples.en: The person-situation debate gives the class two perspectives on a fictional student changing behaviour between settings.
examples.zh: 「人格与情境之争」为全班提供了两种视角，以解释虚构学生在不同场合中的行为变化。

examples.en: Our tutor begins the person-situation debate with examples of both stable tendencies and changing classroom expectations.
examples.zh: 老师以稳定倾向和不断变化的课堂期望为例，引入「人格与情境之争」。

words.zhGloss: 个体与情境的交互作用
words.enDefinition: The joint influence of personal characteristics and situational features on behaviour, when the effect of one depends on the other.
acceptedZhAnswers: 个体与情境的交互作用

examples.en: The hypothetical table illustrates person-situation interaction because the same setting affects two fictional participants in different ways.
examples.zh: 假设表格用同一场景对两名虚构参与者产生的不同影响，说明「个体与情境的交互作用」。

examples.en: Our seminar uses person-situation interaction to explain why a trait may predict behaviour better in certain settings.
examples.zh: 研讨课用「个体与情境的交互作用」说明，某种特质为何在某些场景中更能预测行为。

words.zhGloss: 共情情境中的个人不适
words.enDefinition: In empathy research, self-focused discomfort that can arise when witnessing another person's difficulty.
acceptedZhAnswers: 共情情境中的个人不适

examples.en: The seminar uses a fictional response to distinguish personal distress from concern directed towards another person's welfare.
examples.zh: 研讨课用一种虚构反应来区分「共情情境中的个人不适」和针对他人福祉的关怀。

examples.en: Our worksheet describes personal distress through the fictional observer's own discomfort during an awkward group discussion.
examples.zh: 练习单通过虚构观察者在尴尬的小组讨论中自身的不适说明「共情情境中的个人不适」。

collocations: distinguish personal distress from empathic concern

words.enDefinition: in accounts of adolescent egocentrism, the perception that one's experiences are uniquely special or unlike others' experiences

examples.en: The personal fable example shows a fictional teenager describing their reaction as impossible for anyone else to understand.
examples.zh: 「个人神话」的示例中，虚构青少年认为自己的反应不可能被任何其他人理解。

examples.en: We discussed personal fable and the imaginary audience as separate ideas in the classroom reading on adolescence.
examples.zh: 我们在青少年课堂阅读中，把「个人神话」和假想观众作为两个概念讨论。

words.enDefinition: the study of relatively enduring patterns of thought, feeling and behavior and of differences among people

examples.en: The personality psychology class discussed how a person can show similar tendencies across different situations.
examples.zh: 「人格心理学」课讨论一个人如何在不同情境中表现出相似的倾向。

examples.en: We compared personality psychology explanations of recurring patterns in several fictional students' answers to the same prompts.
examples.zh: 我们比较「人格心理学」对数名虚构学生回答相同题目时所呈现重复模式的不同解释。

words.enDefinition: A relatively enduring tendency in how a person thinks, feels, or behaves across relevant situations.

examples.en: The seminar uses several fictional observations to illustrate why a personality trait cannot be inferred from one afternoon.
examples.zh: 研讨课用几项虚构观察说明，为什么不能根据一个下午的表现推断某种「人格特质」。

examples.en: A personality trait describes a recurring tendency in the case study across several weeks of observations.
examples.zh: 在这个涵盖数周观察的案例中，「人格特质」用来描述反复出现的倾向。

words.enDefinition: a sound category in a spoken language that can distinguish one word from another

examples.en: Changing one phoneme produced a different word in the pair of spoken examples used by the instructor.
examples.zh: 老师使用的一对口语例子中，改变一个「音位」就产生了另一个词。

examples.en: We marked the phoneme contrast in the transcript before listening to the two example words again.
examples.zh: 我们在文字稿上标出「音位」对立，再听一遍那两个例词。

words.enDefinition: Working memory component that temporarily maintains speech-based information through storage and rehearsal

examples.en: The diagram connects the phonological loop with holding a short list of spoken letters.
examples.zh: 示意图把「语音环路」与记住一小列口头报出的字母联系起来。

examples.en: We used the phonological loop model to discuss silently repeating a new word.
examples.zh: 我们用「语音环路」模型讨论在心里重复新单词的现象。

words.enDefinition: Component of the phonological loop that briefly holds speech-based representations

examples.en: The phonological store holds a brief record of sounds in the working memory model.
examples.zh: 在工作记忆模型里，「语音存储器」能短暂保留声音的记录。

examples.en: We labeled the phonological store separately from the mechanism for silently repeating speech.
examples.zh: 我们将「语音存储器」与在心里重复话语的机制分开标注。

words.enDefinition: changes in the body and physical capacities over time, including growth and motor abilities

examples.en: The classroom chart tracks physical development by showing changes in reach and coordination across the fictional observations.
examples.zh: 课堂图表展示虚构观察中伸手能力和协调性如何变化，用以追踪「身体发展」。

examples.en: We discussed how physical development can affect which objects a child explores in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 我们讨论在课堂示例中，「身体发展」如何影响儿童会探索哪些物品。

words.enDefinition: A group pattern in which members misread one another's private attitudes, often because their public behaviour gives a different impression.

examples.en: The fictional seminar illustrates pluralistic ignorance when several confused students each assume everyone else understands the instructions.
examples.zh: 虚构研讨课上，几名不明白要求的学生都以为别人听懂了，用以说明「多元无知」。

examples.en: Our class discusses pluralistic ignorance after comparing what fictional members privately believed with what they said aloud.
examples.zh: 全班比较虚构成员私下的想法与公开说出的内容后，讨论了「多元无知」。

words.enDefinition: The comparison stimulus value perceived as equal to a reference on average.

examples.en: We marked the point of subjective equality where the two patches were judged equally bright overall.
examples.zh: 我们标出「主观等同点」，即总体上两块色块被判断为一样亮的位置。

examples.en: The point of subjective equality shifted when the simulated brightness comparison included a darker surround.
examples.zh: 模拟亮度比较采用较暗背景时，「主观等同点」发生了偏移。

collocations: estimate the point of subjective equality
a shift in the point of subjective equality
plot the point of subjective equality

words.enDefinition: effects of existing policies that shape later political behavior, expectations or decisions about policy

examples.en: The reading describes policy feedback when a fictional program changes which groups participate in later public discussions.
examples.zh: 阅读材料描述一项虚构计划改变了参与后续公共讨论的群体，产生「政策反馈效应」。

examples.en: We explored policy feedback by tracing how an earlier rule influenced preferences after implementation in the model.
examples.zh: 我们追踪模型中一条早期规则实施后如何影响偏好，以探讨「政策反馈效应」。

words.enDefinition: Assessment item scored in more than two distinct response categories

examples.en: The rubric gives a polytomous item scores of zero, one, or two.
examples.zh: 评分标准给一道「多分题项」设定了零、一、二分。

examples.en: The tutorial explains how a polytomous item can award different levels of partial credit.
examples.zh: 辅导课说明了「多分题项」如何给不同等级的部分分。

words.enDefinition: The immediate salience of an item differing visibly from its surroundings.

examples.en: The pop-out effect was clear when the one yellow item stood out among identical blue items.
examples.zh: 唯一的黄色项目在相同的蓝色项目中十分醒目，「突显效应」很明显。

examples.en: We compared the pop-out effect across two displays that used different background colors in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们比较了使用不同背景颜色的两组图中的「突显效应」。

words.enDefinition: the scientific study of strengths, well-being and conditions that help individuals and communities flourish

examples.en: The positive psychology lecture distinguished reported satisfaction from performance on the classroom task being discussed.
examples.zh: 「积极心理学」讲义将自报满意度与课堂所讨论任务的表现区分开来。

examples.en: We read a positive psychology study comparing different measures of engagement in ordinary university activities.
examples.zh: 我们阅读一项「积极心理学」研究，对照普通大学活动中的不同投入度指标。

words.enDefinition: Decrease in behavior because a stimulus is presented after that behavior

examples.en: The simulated game illustrates positive punishment when an added warning reduces invalid moves.
examples.zh: 模拟游戏用增加提示后无效操作减少来说明「正惩罚」。

examples.en: We classified the added error signal as positive punishment only because the response decreased.
examples.zh: 我们之所以把新增错误提示归为「正惩罚」，是因为相关反应减少了。

words.enDefinition: Increase in behavior because a stimulus is presented after that behavior

examples.en: The worksheet illustrates positive reinforcement with extra points and more frequent correct selections.
examples.zh: 习题用获得额外积分后正确选择增多的情形说明「正强化」。

examples.en: We discussed positive reinforcement after the simulated players repeated the rewarded move more often.
examples.zh: 模拟玩家更频繁地重复能得分的动作之后，我们讨论了「正强化」。

words.enDefinition: a favorable social response to conduct regarded by the group as appropriate or desirable

examples.en: The group offered a positive sanction by recognizing the fictional member's consistent contribution during the classroom scenario.
examples.zh: 在课堂情景中，小组肯定虚构成员持续作出贡献，给出一种「正向制裁」。

examples.en: We discussed the difference between a formal award and a spoken compliment as forms of positive sanction.
examples.zh: 我们讨论正式奖励与口头称赞作为两种「正向制裁」形式的区别。

words.enDefinition: Improvement on a new task attributable to prior practice or learning

examples.en: In the simulation, positive transfer occurs when earlier practice improves the new matching task.
examples.zh: 在模拟中，先前练习使新的配对任务表现更好，体现了「正迁移」。

examples.en: We looked for positive transfer by comparing scores with those of the untrained group.
examples.zh: 我们通过对照未接受练习的小组的分数，寻找「正迁移」的迹象。

words.enDefinition: mental images of what one might become, hopes to become or fears becoming in the future

examples.en: The diary exercise identifies possible selves in a fictional student's description of several alternative futures after university.
examples.zh: 日记练习在虚构学生对大学毕业后若干可能人生的描述中，辨认出若干「可能自我」。

examples.en: We compared hoped-for and feared possible selves in the discussion of imagined adult roles from the reading.
examples.zh: 在讨论阅读材料中想象的成人角色时，我们比较了期待的与害怕的「可能自我」。

words.enDefinition: Kohlberg's proposed level at which moral reasoning evaluates rules in light of rights or broader principles

examples.en: The fictional explanation illustrates postconventional morality by evaluating the local rule against a wider principle of fairness.
examples.zh: 虚构解释用更广的公平原则衡量本地规则，以说明「后习俗道德水平」。

examples.en: We discussed postconventional morality as part of the theoretical classification used in the assigned classroom reading.
examples.zh: 我们根据课堂指定阅读所用的理论分类，讨论了其中的「后习俗道德水平」。

words.enDefinition: Dissonance experienced after a choice when the chosen option has drawbacks and rejected options retain attractive features.

examples.en: Our class discusses postdecisional dissonance after the fictional student chooses between two similarly attractive elective courses.
examples.zh: 在虚构学生从两门吸引力相近的选修课中选出一门后，全班讨论了「决策后认知失调」。

examples.en: The diary excerpt illustrates postdecisional dissonance by describing the character's continued discomfort after selecting one activity.
examples.zh: 日记摘录描述角色选定一项活动后仍感不安，用以说明「决策后认知失调」。

words.enDefinition: Brief period of little or no responding immediately following a reinforcer

examples.en: The graph shows a postreinforcement pause right after the point appears onscreen.
examples.zh: 图表显示，积分一出现在屏幕上就发生了「强化后停顿」。

examples.en: We located a postreinforcement pause before the simulated response rate picked up again.
examples.zh: 模拟反应率再次上升前，我们在图上找到了「强化后停顿」。

words.enDefinition: Improved performance resulting from prior experience with the task.

examples.en: The practice effect appeared when both fictional groups made fewer errors after completing the first block.
examples.zh: 两个虚构小组完成第一个任务区段后都犯错更少，出现了「练习效应」。

examples.en: We noted a possible practice effect because scores improved even when task difficulty remained unchanged.
examples.zh: 尽管任务难度没有变化，分数仍有所提高，因此我们注意到可能存在「练习效应」。

words.enDefinition: A trial used to familiarize participants with a task before formal measurement.

examples.en: The practice trial showed an example response so students could learn the two keys before testing.
examples.zh: 「练习试次」展示了一次示范作答，让学生在测试前熟悉两个按键。

examples.en: We excluded each practice trial from the main score because those responses followed an example with feedback.
examples.zh: 「练习试次」的作答紧接在带反馈的示例之后，所以我们没有把它们计入正式得分。

words.enDefinition: using a speaker's words together with context and assumptions to infer meaning beyond what was explicitly said

examples.en: The listener used a pragmatic inference to understand the brief question as a request in the dialogue.
examples.zh: 对话中，听者通过「语用推理」听出简短提问实际提出了一项请求。

examples.en: We compared pragmatic inference in two situations where people heard the same statement from different speakers.
examples.zh: 我们比较两种情境中的「语用推理」，人们从不同说话者那里听到了同一句话。

words.enDefinition: Kohlberg's proposed level at which moral reasoning emphasizes punishment, reward or direct personal exchange

examples.en: The textbook illustrates preconventional morality with a fictional argument focused on avoiding a penalty for breaking a rule.
examples.zh: 教材用一段关注如何避免因违反规则而受处罚的虚构论证，说明「前习俗道德水平」。

examples.en: We coded the explanation as preconventional morality because its main justification depended on a direct reward.
examples.zh: 由于解释的主要依据是直接回报，我们将它编码为「前习俗道德水平」。

words.enDefinition: Relationship indicating how much a cue predicts a particular outcome

examples.en: The worksheet compares predictive contingency for two symbols that appear before the same sound.
examples.zh: 习题比较了在同一声音之前出现的两个符号各自的「预测依存关系」。

examples.en: A short timeline alone does not tell us how strong predictive contingency is.
examples.zh: 一条简短时间线本身无法告诉我们「预测依存关系」有多强。

words.enDefinition: Support from the ability of test scores to predict a later criterion

examples.en: The workbook uses later simulated performance to illustrate evidence of predictive validity.
examples.zh: 练习册用后续的模拟表现来举例说明「预测效度」证据。

examples.en: We discussed predictive validity when the outcome was recorded several weeks after testing.
examples.zh: 当结果在测验几周后才记录时，我们讨论了「预测效度」。

words.enDefinition: an observation method comparing how long an infant looks at different simultaneously presented stimuli

examples.en: The example of preferential looking compares how long the infant in the fictional record viewed two images.
examples.zh: 「偏好注视法」示例对照虚构记录中的婴儿观察两幅图像分别用了多长时间。

examples.en: We used preferential looking data to discuss discrimination while considering why preferences might differ across conditions.
examples.zh: 我们用「偏好注视法」的数据讨论辨别能力，并考虑不同情境下偏好为何可能不同。

collocations: measure looking time in a preferential looking task

words.enDefinition: Piaget's stage in which symbolic thought develops and some forms of logical operation are still limited

examples.en: The reading uses pretend objects to illustrate symbolic abilities developing during the preoperational stage of Piaget's model.
examples.zh: 阅读材料用假扮物件说明在皮亚杰模型「前运算阶段」发展的符号能力。

examples.en: We compared conservation answers attributed to the preoperational stage with examples from a later stage in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们将归于「前运算阶段」的守恒作答与后来阶段的示例比较。

words.enDefinition: A hypothesis documented in a dated research plan before the specified analysis or data collection.

examples.en: The preregistered hypothesis predicted higher accuracy for large symbols before the simulated responses were shown.
examples.zh: 在展示模拟作答之前，「预注册假设」便预测较大符号的正确率更高。

examples.en: We compared the preregistered hypothesis with the additional prediction proposed after reading the fictional data.
examples.zh: 我们将「预注册假设」与查看虚构数据后提出的另一项预测作比较。

words.enDefinition: the ways people manage how others perceive them during social interaction

examples.en: The reading examines presentation of self through two greetings used by the same fictional person in different settings.
examples.zh: 阅读材料通过同一个虚构人物在不同情境的两种问候方式，考察「自我呈现」。

examples.en: We discussed presentation of self when the participant selected different details to share with two audiences in class.
examples.zh: 课堂示例中，参与者选择向两批听众分享不同细节，我们由此讨论「自我呈现」。

words.enDefinition: Better recall for early list items than for items in the middle

examples.en: The class graph shows a primacy effect for the first words on the list.
examples.zh: 课堂图表显示，列表开头的单词出现了「首因效应」。

examples.en: We examined the primacy effect separately from the improvement for items near the end.
examples.zh: 我们将「首因效应」与靠近末尾项目的表现改善分开考察。

words.enDefinition: Consequence with reinforcing value that does not require prior learning

examples.en: The textbook lists water as a primary reinforcer when the example describes thirst.
examples.zh: 教材在描述口渴的例子中把水列为「初级强化物」。

examples.en: We compared learned symbols with a primary reinforcer on the review chart.
examples.zh: 我们用复习图表比较了通过学习获得意义的符号与「初级强化物」。

collocations: biological basis of a primary reinforcer
distinguish a primary reinforcer from a conditioned reinforcer

words.enDefinition: early learning of language, expectations and basic ways of participating, often through close relationships

examples.en: The reading uses early family routines to illustrate primary socialization in the fictional child's environment.
examples.zh: 阅读材料用早期家庭惯例说明虚构儿童环境中的「初级社会化」。

examples.en: We discussed primary socialization while reviewing the early learning examples in the chapter on social development.
examples.zh: 我们复习社会发展章的早期学习示例时，讨论了「初级社会化」。

words.enDefinition: A genuine change in a person's own judgment or belief to align with information or expectations from others.

examples.en: Our worksheet illustrates private acceptance when a fictional student genuinely changes their view after a group conversation.
examples.zh: 练习单用虚构学生在团体谈话后切实改变观点的一幕说明「内心认同」。

examples.en: Does the character's later private response support a conclusion of private acceptance in the fictional example?
examples.zh: 在虚构示例中，角色后来的私下回应是否支持发生了「内心认同」这一判断？

words.enDefinition: speech directed to oneself, often used by children to guide attention or actions during a task

examples.en: The example shows private speech when the child quietly talks through the next steps of the puzzle.
examples.zh: 示例中，儿童低声说出谜题接下来的几步，表现出「自我言语」。

examples.en: We discussed whether private speech helped the fictional learner remember the classroom task's instructions in sequence.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「自我言语」是否帮助虚构学习者按顺序记住课堂任务的指示。

words.enDefinition: Disruption of new learning or remembering by information acquired earlier

examples.en: The model illustrates proactive interference when yesterday's list disrupts recall of today's list.
examples.zh: 模型用昨天的列表妨碍回忆今天的列表来说明「前摄干扰」。

examples.en: We tested for proactive interference by comparing recall after studying similar or unrelated words.
examples.zh: 我们比较了学过相似词或无关词之后的回忆表现，以检验「前摄干扰」。

words.enDefinition: the way a solver mentally organizes the starting conditions, goals and relations of a problem

examples.en: The new diagram changed their problem representation by making an overlooked relationship visible to the fictional group.
examples.zh: 新图使被忽略的关系变得可见，从而改变虚构小组的「问题表征」。

examples.en: We compared a verbal problem representation with one using a diagram of the available moves in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们把口头「问题表征」与用图示表示可采取步骤的表征作对照。

words.enDefinition: reorganizing one's representation of a problem so that different relationships or potential steps become apparent

examples.en: Problem restructuring changed how the learner grouped the shapes and revealed a shorter sequence of moves.
examples.zh: 「问题重构」改变了学习者给图形分组的方式，并揭示一套步骤更少的操作顺序。

examples.en: We compared problem restructuring with trying another move within the original interpretation of the puzzle.
examples.zh: 我们将「问题重构」与沿用谜题的原有理解再尝试另一步操作相对照。

words.enDefinition: the set of possible states and moves that a solver represents for a particular problem

examples.en: The worksheet draws the problem space as a network of states connected by the puzzle's permitted moves.
examples.zh: 习题将「问题空间」画成一个状态网络，其中各状态由谜题允许的步骤连接。

examples.en: We reduced the problem space by ignoring states that were impossible under the rules in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中，我们忽略规则下不可能的状态，以缩小「问题空间」。

words.enDefinition: Long-term memory expressed through the performance of learned skills or procedures

examples.en: The chapter illustrates procedural memory with fluent typing after extensive practice on a keyboard.
examples.zh: 本章用在键盘上大量练习后能流畅打字的情形说明「程序性记忆」。

examples.en: Our tutor discusses procedural memory by contrasting descriptions of a skill with its performance.
examples.zh: 老师通过对照描述一项技能和实际施展该技能来讲解「程序性记忆」。

words.enDefinition: Memory advantage for words spoken aloud during study over silently read words

examples.en: The demo contrasts reading words aloud and silently to illustrate the production effect.
examples.zh: 演示对比朗读和默读单词，以说明「产出效应」。

examples.en: In the simulated study, the production effect appeared on the later recognition test.
examples.zh: 在模拟研究中，「产出效应」体现在后来的再认测验中。

words.enDefinition: a representation encoding the abstract meaning or relations expressed by a statement rather than its particular wording

examples.en: The model gives the two different sentences one propositional representation because they express the same relation.
examples.zh: 模型为两个措辞不同的句子赋予相同「命题表征」，因为它们表达同一关系。

examples.en: We drew the propositional representation for the classroom example using a predicate and two argument positions.
examples.zh: 我们用一个谓词和两个论元位置，画出课堂示例的「命题表征」。

words.enDefinition: Voluntary behaviour intended to benefit another person or group, regardless of whether the actor also benefits.

examples.en: The handout illustrates prosocial behaviour with a fictional student voluntarily sharing useful class notes with a peer.
examples.zh: 讲义用一名虚构学生主动与同伴分享有用课堂笔记的例子来说明「亲社会行为」。

examples.en: Our class discusses how prosocial behaviour might benefit both the recipient and the helper in some cases.
examples.zh: 全班讨论，在某些情况下，「亲社会行为」可能如何使接受者和帮助者都受益。

words.enDefinition: the tendency for central or typical category examples to be recognized or judged more readily than less typical examples

examples.en: The prototype effect appeared when fictional participants classified typical examples faster than equally familiar atypical members.
examples.zh: 虚构参与者对典型成员的分类快于同样熟悉的非典型成员，呈现了「原型效应」。

examples.en: We drew the prototype effect on the graph as a difference between response times for two example types.
examples.zh: 我们在图上将「原型效应」画成两种示例类型对应反应时的差异。

words.enDefinition: a theory of categorization in which objects are compared with a central or typical representation of a category

examples.en: The lecture uses prototype theory to explain why some examples seem more typical of a category than others.
examples.zh: 讲义用「原型理论」解释为什么一些例子看起来比另一些更能代表某个类别。

examples.en: We compared prototype theory with a theory based on comparison to particular remembered examples in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中，我们把「原型理论」与根据特定记忆实例作比较的理论对照。

words.enDefinition: a recurring interaction between the developing person and people, objects or symbols in their immediate environment

examples.en: The example treats repeated shared reading as a proximal process involving both the child and the caregiver.
examples.zh: 示例把反复进行的共同阅读视为儿童与照护者共同参与的一种「近端过程」。

examples.en: We identified a proximal process when the fictional classroom interaction occurred regularly and became more complex over time.
examples.zh: 当虚构课堂互动经常发生并随时间变得更复杂时，我们识别出一种「近端过程」。

words.enDefinition: an explanation in terms of the immediate mechanisms or developmental processes that produce an observed trait or behavior

examples.en: The proximate explanation described which immediate sensory input triggered the response in the classroom model of behavior.
examples.zh: 「近因解释」描述在课堂行为模型中，哪种直接感觉输入触发了这一反应。

examples.en: We discussed a proximate explanation of learning that focused on the learner's changing expectations across trials.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了学习的「近因解释」，着重考察学习者的预期如何在各次试验间改变。

words.enDefinition: a general developmental pattern extending from central or nearby body regions toward more distant parts

examples.en: The example of proximodistal development places control of the arm before the most precise finger movements.
examples.zh: 「近远方向发展」的示例把手臂控制放在最精细的手指活动之前。

examples.en: We used the proximodistal development diagram to compare the order of control within the upper limb.
examples.zh: 我们用「近远方向发展」示意图比较上肢各部分获得控制的顺序。

words.enDefinition: theories originating with Freud that emphasize unconscious processes, conflicts and early experience in explaining behavior

examples.en: The history lecture presents psychoanalytic theory as one influential attempt to explain actions through unconscious processes.
examples.zh: 心理学史讲义把「精神分析理论」作为一种用无意识过程解释行为的有影响力的尝试。

examples.en: We studied psychoanalytic theory in its historical context while comparing its claims with those of other approaches.
examples.zh: 我们在历史背景中学习「精神分析理论」，并将它的主张与其他取向的主张比较。

words.enDefinition: an approach examining how internal conflicts, unconscious processes and patterns of relationships may influence thoughts and behavior

examples.en: The reading discusses repeated relationship patterns from a psychodynamic perspective in the context of a fictional character.
examples.zh: 阅读材料在虚构人物的情境中，从「心理动力学观点」讨论其重复出现的关系模式。

examples.en: We compared the psychodynamic perspective with explanations that placed greater emphasis on deliberate reasoning in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们把「心理动力学观点」和更重视有意识推理的解释作比较。

words.enDefinition: the study of mental processes involved in learning, understanding and producing language

examples.en: The psycholinguistics seminar examined why a listener might initially interpret an ambiguous sentence in one particular way.
examples.zh: 「心理语言学」研讨课考察听者为什么起初可能以某种特定方式理解歧义句。

examples.en: We read a psycholinguistics study that compared response timing for common words and less familiar ones.
examples.zh: 我们阅读一项「心理语言学」研究，对照常见词与不太熟悉的词所对应的反应时。

words.enDefinition: Systematic evaluation combining information about a person's psychological functioning or attributes

examples.en: The class uses a fictional case to examine the sources of information in psychological assessment.
examples.zh: 课堂用虚构个案分析「心理评估」中的信息来源。

examples.en: We discussed how psychological assessment can draw on interviews as well as test results.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「心理评估」如何同时参考访谈和测验结果。

words.enDefinition: A theoretical attribute inferred from observations rather than measured directly.

examples.en: Our class treated persistence as a psychological construct and counted repeated attempts as one observable indicator.
examples.zh: 课堂把坚持性视为一种「心理构念」，并以重复尝试次数作为一个可观察指标。

examples.en: The article defined its psychological construct before explaining how the researchers scored the task responses.
examples.zh: 文章先界定它研究的「心理构念」，再说明研究者如何给任务作答评分。

words.enDefinition: an observable or measurable pattern involving thought, feeling, perception or behavior

examples.en: The class described the psychological phenomenon before discussing competing explanations for the pattern in the results.
examples.zh: 全班先描述结果里呈现的「心理现象」，再讨论对这种模式的不同解释。

examples.en: We looked for a second example of the psychological phenomenon in an unfamiliar classroom task.
examples.zh: 我们在一个不熟悉的课堂任务中寻找该「心理现象」的第二个例子。

words.enDefinition: Delayed response to the second of two tasks when their stimuli occur in close succession.

examples.en: The psychological refractory period appeared when the second response slowed as the two task signals moved closer together.
examples.zh: 两个任务信号靠得更近时，第二次反应变慢，出现了「心理不应期」效应。

examples.en: We discussed the psychological refractory period after comparing closer and wider spacing between the two signals.
examples.zh: 比较两个信号之间较短和较长的间隔后，我们讨论了「心理不应期」。

words.enDefinition: the scientific study of behavior and mental processes through systematic observation and testing

examples.en: The psychological science course compared explanations of behavior using observations from several different classroom studies.
examples.zh: 「心理科学」课用多项课堂研究的观察结果比较对行为的不同解释。

examples.en: We discussed how psychological science can revise an explanation when new observations contradict its predictions.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了新观察与预测相矛盾时，「心理科学」如何修正一种解释。

words.enDefinition: Structured procedure designed to sample behavior and measure a psychological attribute

examples.en: The workbook shows how a fictional psychological test samples performance on pattern problems.
examples.zh: 练习册展示了一个虚构的「心理测验」如何抽取图形规律题的作答表现。

examples.en: We discussed what a psychological test can tell us from a brief set of responses.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「心理测验」能从少量作答中反映什么。

words.enDefinition: A curve linking stimulus magnitude to the probability of a particular perceptual response.

examples.en: We fitted a psychometric function to show how detection responses changed as the tones grew louder.
examples.zh: 我们拟合了「心理测量函数」，展示音调变响时检测作答如何变化。

examples.en: The psychometric function was shallower for the simulated listener whose judgments varied more across trials.
examples.zh: 在各次试验中判断波动较大的模拟听者，对应的「心理测量函数」曲线更平缓。

collocations: the slope of a psychometric function

words.enDefinition: Field concerned with measuring psychological attributes and evaluating those measurements

examples.en: Our psychometrics seminar starts by asking what a questionnaire score actually represents.
examples.zh: 我们的「心理测量学」研讨课从问卷分数究竟代表什么讲起。

examples.en: The textbook introduces psychometrics through several examples using invented scores and responses.
examples.zh: 教材用虚构分数和作答数据的几个例子介绍「心理测量学」。

words.enDefinition: The study of relationships between physical stimuli and sensory experience.

examples.en: In psychophysics, we can ask how changes in light intensity affect the brightness people report.
examples.zh: 在「心理物理学」中，我们可以研究光强变化如何影响人们报告的亮度。

examples.en: The opening psychophysics lecture compared physical sound level with the loudness listeners reported in class.
examples.zh: 「心理物理学」的第一堂课对比了声音的物理声级与听者报告的响度。

words.enDefinition: Erikson's framework describing developmental challenges involving the person and social context across the lifespan

examples.en: The course organized Erikson's psychosocial theory of development around challenges in relationships and roles at different life periods.
examples.zh: 课程围绕人生不同时期的关系和角色挑战，梳理埃里克森的「心理社会发展理论」。

examples.en: We used the psychosocial theory of development timeline to compare two fictional transitions discussed in the reading.
examples.zh: 我们利用「心理社会发展理论」时间线，对照阅读材料中讨论的两个虚构转折。

collocations: stages in the psychosocial theory of development
discuss the psychosocial theory of development

words.enDefinition: Outward alignment with a group response without necessarily changing one's privately held view.

examples.en: The fictional vignette illustrates public conformity because the character's spoken answer changes while their private view remains stable.
examples.zh: 虚构材料所述角色的口头答案变了，但私下观点未变，说明了「公开从众」。

examples.en: Our seminar compares public conformity in the first scene with a genuine change of view in the second.
examples.zh: 研讨课比较第一场景中的「公开从众」和第二场景中观点确实发生的变化。

collocations: distinction between public conformity and private acceptance

words.enDefinition: A design estimating the effect of a change without random assignment to conditions.

examples.en: The quasi-experimental design compared two existing sections after one adopted a different reading format in the simulation.
examples.zh: 模拟中一个班改用不同的阅读材料格式后，「准实验设计」对比了两个已有的班级。

examples.en: We used the classroom checklist to explain why the lack of random assignment indicated a quasi-experimental design.
examples.zh: 我们用课堂清单解释，在这个例子里，为什么未随机分派表明采用的是「准实验设计」。

collocations: an example of a quasi-experimental design

words.enDefinition: Skinner's philosophical approach treating publicly observable actions and private events as behavior shaped by their contexts and history

examples.en: The passage on radical behaviorism treats private events as part of the subject matter of behavioral inquiry.
examples.zh: 有关「激进行为主义」的段落把个体内在事件纳入行为研究的对象。

examples.en: We read the example of radical behaviorism to see how it interpreted what a person silently said.
examples.zh: 我们阅读「激进行为主义」示例，了解它如何解释一个人在心里说的话。

words.enDefinition: Using chance to determine which condition participants enter.

examples.en: The classroom simulation used random assignment to place fictional participants in the two display conditions.
examples.zh: 课堂模拟通过「随机分派」将虚构参与者分到两种不同的呈现条件中。

examples.en: Our diagram separated random assignment from the earlier process of choosing who would join the study.
examples.zh: 我们在示意图中区分了「随机分派」和之前选择哪些人参加研究的过程。

words.enDefinition: The degree to which people retain their relative standing on a characteristic compared with others over time.

examples.en: The class chart illustrates rank-order stability even though the average level changes in the fictional group.
examples.zh: 课堂图表说明，即使虚构群体的平均水平变化，也可能存在「相对排序稳定性」。

examples.en: Students compare the order of the fictional profiles across years to understand rank-order stability in personality.
examples.zh: 学生比较虚构人物画像在不同年份的次序，以理解人格的「相对排序稳定性」。

words.enDefinition: Displaying items one after another in rapid succession, typically at one location.

examples.en: The lecturer used rapid serial visual presentation to show letters and numbers at one central location.
examples.zh: 老师用「快速序列视觉呈现」在同一个中央位置快速依次显示字母和数字。

examples.en: In rapid serial visual presentation, the entire group of symbols appeared one at a time.
examples.zh: 采用「快速序列视觉呈现」时，整组符号依次逐一出现。

collocations: a rapid serial visual presentation task
targets in rapid serial visual presentation

words.enDefinition: Item response model with item difficulty and common discrimination across binary items

examples.en: The tutorial fits a Rasch model to invented answers from a short assessment.
examples.zh: 辅导课把「拉施模型」拟合到一份简短测验的虚构作答数据。

examples.en: We compared the Rasch model curves while keeping their slopes the same.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「拉施模型」曲线，各条曲线的斜率保持相同。

words.enDefinition: in Weberian sociology, a process in which calculation, formal rules and predictability increasingly organize social practices

examples.en: The class examined rationalization when the fictional organization replaced personal judgment with uniform rules and measurable targets.
examples.zh: 虚构组织将个人判断改为统一规则及可测量目标时，全班考察了「理性化」。

examples.en: We discussed rationalization as a change in how decisions were organized across the two historical examples.
examples.zh: 我们把「理性化」作为两个历史示例安排决策方式的变化来讨论。

words.enDefinition: The amount by which response times vary across a specified set of observations.

examples.en: The plots showed different reaction time variability even though the two simulated observers had the same average.
examples.zh: 两位模拟观察者的平均反应时相同，但图上显示的「反应时变异性」不同。

examples.en: We used the spread of responses to discuss reaction time variability before comparing the mean times.
examples.zh: 我们先根据作答的分散程度讨论「反应时变异性」，再比较平均反应时。

collocations: compare reaction time variability across trials

words.enDefinition: Better recall for late list items than for items in the middle

examples.en: The demonstration shows a recency effect when students recall the last items particularly well.
examples.zh: 演示中，学生对最后几个项目回忆得特别好，体现了「近因效应」。

examples.en: We compared the recency effect for immediate recall with recall after a distraction.
examples.zh: 我们比较了即时回忆和经历干扰后回忆中的「近因效应」。

words.enDefinition: Ability to identify an item as previously encountered or studied

examples.en: The class exercise tests recognition memory by mixing familiar pictures with new ones.
examples.zh: 课堂练习把熟悉图片和新图片混在一起，以测量「再认记忆」。

examples.en: We compared recognition memory with the ability to list the pictures from memory.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「再认记忆」与凭记忆列出图片的能力。

words.enDefinition: A person's view of themselves based on how they believe other people see them.

examples.en: The fictional diary uses reflected appraisal to describe a student's beliefs about how their classmates see them.
examples.zh: 虚构日记用「反映性自我评价」描述一名学生认为同学怎样看待自己。

examples.en: Our seminar contrasts reflected appraisal with the actual views separately reported by the fictional group members.
examples.zh: 研讨课把「反映性自我评价」与虚构小组成员分别报告的真实看法作比较。

words.enDefinition: A publication format reviewing the research plan before results are known and reviewing the completed study later.

examples.en: The sample Registered Report presented the approved research plan before describing the results of the classroom simulation.
examples.zh: 「注册报告」样例先陈述通过审查的研究计划，再描述课堂模拟的结果。

examples.en: We compared a Registered Report with a paper first considered after its fictional results were available.
examples.zh: 我们把「注册报告」与一篇在虚构结果出现之后才送审的论文比较。

words.enDefinition: treating an abstract concept or human creation as an independent concrete thing

examples.en: The tutor identified reification when the report described an abstract ranking as though it were a physical object.
examples.zh: 报告把一种抽象排序当作实物描述时，老师指出这是「抽象概念实体化」。

examples.en: We discussed how reification can obscure the human decisions that produce the categories in the classroom chart.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「抽象概念实体化」如何使人忽视课堂图表里各类别背后的人为决定。

collocations: criticize reification of an abstract category

words.enDefinition: Relationship specifying when a reinforcer depends on an observed behavior

examples.en: The reinforcement contingency in the demo links points to selections of the matching shape.
examples.zh: 演示中的「强化依存关系」将得分与选中匹配图形联系起来。

examples.en: We described the reinforcement contingency separately from how much each game point was worth.
examples.zh: 我们将「强化依存关系」与每个游戏积分的价值分开描述。

words.enDefinition: Rule specifying which responses or occasions are followed by reinforcement

examples.en: The two simulated games use the same points but a different reinforcement schedule.
examples.zh: 两个模拟游戏使用同样的积分，但「强化时程」不同。

examples.en: We labeled each reinforcement schedule according to whether it depended on responses or time.
examples.zh: 我们根据各个「强化时程」取决于反应次数还是时间来分类标注。

words.enDefinition: Consequence that increases future occurrence of the behavior it follows

examples.en: A game point counted as a reinforcer only when the response became more frequent.
examples.zh: 游戏积分只有在相关反应变得更频繁时才算「强化物」。

examples.en: The simulation compares how often a particular symbol serves as a reinforcer.
examples.zh: 模拟比较了一个特定符号作为「强化物」发挥作用的频率。

words.enDefinition: feeling disadvantaged when you compare yourself with a relevant group or expectation

examples.en: The classroom example illustrates relative deprivation when evaluations change after the fictional participants learn how peers were treated.
examples.zh: 虚构参与者得知同伴受到怎样的待遇后改变评价，课堂示例由此呈现「相对剥夺感」。

examples.en: We discussed which comparison group mattered for relative deprivation in the two fictional survey scenarios used in class.
examples.zh: 我们讨论课堂所用的两个虚构调查情景中，哪个比较群体会影响「相对剥夺感」。

words.enDefinition: the relationship between origins and destinations expressed through relative chances of reaching social positions across origin groups

examples.en: The exercise compares relative mobility by checking whether the chances of reaching an occupation differ by origin group.
examples.zh: 习题核对进入某职业的机会是否因出身群体不同而变化，以比较「相对流动」。

examples.en: We compared relative mobility using the odds of entering each occupational group for children from different origins.
examples.zh: 我们根据不同家庭出身的子女进入各职业群体的相对机会，比较「相对流动」。

words.enDefinition: Depth information from differences in apparent size among objects expected to be similar in size.

examples.en: The two identical benches illustrated a relative size cue when one occupied much less of the picture.
examples.zh: 两张相同的长椅中，有一张在画面上占的面积小得多，展示了「相对大小线索」。

examples.en: We explained the distance judgment using a relative size cue rather than assuming one object was smaller.
examples.zh: 我们用「相对大小线索」来解释距离判断，没有假定其中一件物体的实际尺寸较小。

collocations: an example of a relative size cue

words.enDefinition: Statistic quantifying score consistency for a specified design and measurement purpose

examples.en: The results table pairs each reliability coefficient with the replication design used to estimate it.
examples.zh: 结果表把每个「信度系数」与用于估计它的重复测量设计配列在一起。

examples.en: We asked which reliability coefficient was appropriate for the scores from two different raters.
examples.zh: 我们问，对于两位不同评分者给出的分数，哪种「信度系数」合适。

words.enDefinition: A sleep stage characterized by rapid eye movements and low skeletal muscle tone.

examples.en: The class shaded the intervals of REM sleep in the fictional overnight chart with a single color.
examples.zh: 全班用同一种颜色标出虚构的整夜图表中「快速眼动睡眠」的各个时段。

examples.en: The lecture compared REM sleep with other stages and noted that dreams can occur outside it.
examples.zh: 老师比较了「快速眼动睡眠」与其他阶段，并指出其他阶段也可能做梦。

words.enDefinition: Return of an extinguished response when the context changes after extinction

examples.en: The simulated renewal effect appears when the screen returns to its original background color.
examples.zh: 屏幕回到起初的背景色时，出现了模拟的「更新效应」。

examples.en: We compared the renewal effect with recovery after a delay in the same setting.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「更新效应」与在同一情境下延迟后的恢复。

words.enDefinition: Change in processing an item following earlier exposure to the same item

examples.en: The simulation shows repetition priming when viewers identify a repeated shape's color more quickly.
examples.zh: 模拟中，观察者辨认重复图形的颜色更快，显示出「重复启动」。

examples.en: We tested for repetition priming by comparing naming times for repeated and new words.
examples.zh: 我们比较了说出重复单词和新单词的用时，以检验「重复启动」。

words.enDefinition: judging the probability of membership or an event by how much it resembles a typical case

examples.en: The representativeness heuristic made a fictional profile seem likely because it resembled a typical example in the worksheet.
examples.zh: 由于虚构简介与练习中的典型示例相似，「代表性启发式」让该归类显得很可能正确。

examples.en: We discussed the representativeness heuristic after comparing resemblance judgments with the stated base rates for each group.
examples.zh: 我们将相似性判断与各组所给的基准发生率比较后，讨论了「代表性启发式」。

words.enDefinition: A postparticipation explanation of a study's purpose or procedures and an opportunity for questions.

examples.en: The simulation ended with research debriefing, when the instructor explained the purpose of comparing the two displays.
examples.zh: 模拟活动以「研究结束说明」收尾，老师在这一环节解释了对比两种显示方式的目的。

examples.en: We discussed what research debriefing could clarify for the fictional participants once the activity was complete.
examples.zh: 我们讨论活动结束后，「研究结束说明」能为虚构参与者解释哪些内容。

words.enDefinition: A testable claim about an expected relationship, difference, or pattern.

examples.en: The research hypothesis predicted that students would recognize words faster after seeing related pictures in the simulation.
examples.zh: 「研究假设」预测，在模拟中，学生看过相关图片后会更快认出单词。

examples.en: We rewrote the research hypothesis when the first version did not specify any observable outcome.
examples.zh: 第一版没有说明要观察什么结果，所以我们重写了「研究假设」。

words.enDefinition: Course credit awarded for taking part in an eligible research activity.

examples.en: The mock syllabus explained how students could earn research participation credit through eligible classroom activities.
examples.zh: 模拟教学大纲说明学生如何通过符合要求的课堂活动获得「研究参与学分」。

examples.en: We checked whether research participation credit was listed as optional in the fictional department's course information.
examples.zh: 我们核对虚构院系的课程信息是否把获取「研究参与学分」列为可选事项。

words.enDefinition: Recording specified study plans with a date before the relevant research steps begin.

examples.en: The research preregistration recorded the planned task comparison before the class revealed the synthetic response data.
examples.zh: 在课堂公布合成作答数据之前，「研究预注册」记录了计划进行的任务比较。

examples.en: We consulted the research preregistration to see which outcome the fictional project had identified before analysis.
examples.zh: 我们查阅「研究预注册」，查看虚构项目在分析前指定了哪项结果指标。

collocations: compare findings with a research preregistration

words.zhGloss: 研究者的分析选择空间
words.enDefinition: Choices about data collection, inclusion, and analysis that can influence study results.
acceptedZhAnswers: 研究者的分析选择空间

examples.en: The seminar discussed researcher degrees of freedom when the same synthetic responses supported several reasonable summaries.
examples.zh: 由于同一组合成作答可以用几种合理方式汇总，讨论课探讨了「研究者的分析选择空间」。

examples.en: We compared two dated plans to see how explicitly they addressed researcher degrees of freedom.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两份注明日期的计划，看看它们对「研究者的分析选择空间」说明得有多明确。

collocations: the scope of researcher degrees of freedom

words.enDefinition: an infant-caregiver classification in the Strange Situation that may include both seeking and resisting contact at reunion, often with difficulty settling

examples.en: The video example describes resistant attachment when the child both seeks and resists contact at reunion.
examples.zh: 视频示例将儿童在重聚时既寻求接触又抵触接触的情形描述为「抗拒型依恋」。

examples.en: We identified the resistant attachment pattern from the sequence of observations described in the fictional textbook example.
examples.zh: 我们从虚构教材示例所述的一连串观察中辨认「抗拒型依恋」模式。

words.enDefinition: replacing or substantially revising learned norms and behaviors in a new social setting

examples.en: The case study shows resocialization as the fictional participants adapt to a setting with sharply different expectations.
examples.zh: 个案研究用虚构参与者适应预期显著不同的环境，展示了「再社会化」。

examples.en: We distinguished resocialization from adding one new skill to an otherwise unchanged role in the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 课堂练习中，我们区分「再社会化」与在原有角色基本不变的情况下添加一种技能。

words.enDefinition: a theory emphasizing how access to people, money and organizational resources shapes a social movement's development

examples.en: The lecture uses resource mobilization theory to compare what two fictional groups could sustain with different resources.
examples.zh: 讲义用「资源动员理论」比较资源不同的两个虚构团体各自能够维持哪些活动。

examples.en: We read a resource mobilization theory explanation alongside the classroom timeline of the group's organizational changes.
examples.zh: 我们将一种「资源动员理论」解释与小组组织变化的课堂时间线一并阅读。

collocations: explanation based on resource mobilization theory

words.enDefinition: An ethical principle recognizing autonomy and protecting people with diminished autonomy.

examples.en: The ethics seminar linked respect for persons to giving fictional volunteers a meaningful choice about taking part.
examples.zh: 伦理讨论课把「尊重个人原则」与让虚构志愿者能够真正自主决定是否参与联系起来。

examples.en: We discussed how respect for persons guided the wording of the fictional study invitation and information sheet.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「尊重个人原则」如何影响虚构研究邀请和信息表的措辞。

collocations: the principle of respect for persons
safeguards grounded in respect for persons

words.enDefinition: The proportion of responses meeting the correct-answer rule in a task.

examples.en: Response accuracy was higher for the large symbols in the simulated classroom data shown on the slide.
examples.zh: 投影片的模拟课堂数据中，较大的符号对应较高的「作答正确率」。

examples.en: We checked response accuracy separately from speed because quick answers were sometimes wrong in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们把「作答正确率」和速度分开核对，因为练习中答得快也可能答错。

words.enDefinition: Labels or examples defining the meanings of points on a response scale

examples.en: The worksheet shows response anchors that describe what the ends of the scale mean.
examples.zh: 习题展示了说明量表两端含义的「作答等级锚点」。

examples.en: We compared two sets of response anchors for the same fictional item.
examples.zh: 我们对照了同一道虚构题目的两套「作答等级锚点」。

words.enDefinition: A systematic tendency to favor one response apart from perceptual sensitivity.

examples.en: The two groups showed different response bias even though their discrimination scores were nearly identical.
examples.zh: 两组的辨别得分几乎一样，却显示出不同的「反应偏向」。

examples.en: In the classroom analysis, response bias described how readily the simulated listener reported hearing a signal.
examples.zh: 在课堂分析中，「反应偏向」描述模拟听者有多倾向于报告听到信号。

words.enDefinition: Event following a behavior that can modify its future occurrence

examples.en: A point on the screen serves as the response consequence in our simulation.
examples.zh: 在我们的模拟中，屏幕上增加一分就是「反应后果」。

examples.en: We identified the response consequence that followed a correct selection in the practice game.
examples.zh: 我们辨认出了练习游戏中正确选择之后出现的「反应后果」。

words.enDefinition: The internal cutoff for deciding which response to give in a task.

examples.en: The classroom model illustrated how a stricter response criterion reduced both hits and false alarms.
examples.zh: 课堂模型展示了更严格的「反应判准」如何同时减少命中和虚报。

examples.en: We drew the response criterion as a vertical line across the two simulated evidence distributions.
examples.zh: 我们在两个模拟证据分布上画出一条竖线，表示「反应判准」。

words.enDefinition: The latest time at which a task accepts or counts a response.

examples.en: The second version of the classroom task used a shorter response deadline for the same symbols.
examples.zh: 课堂任务第二版使用同样的符号，但「作答时限」更短。

examples.en: We marked the response deadline on the timeline before counting how many fictional responses arrived too late.
examples.zh: 我们先在时间线上标出「作答时限」，再统计虚构结果中有多少次作答超时。

words.enDefinition: The rule linking particular stimuli or judgments to specified responses.

examples.en: The response mapping assigned one key to circles and another to squares in the practice task.
examples.zh: 练习任务的「反应映射」为圆形和正方形指定了不同的按键。

examples.en: We checked the response mapping before deciding whether the recorded key press matched the target.
examples.zh: 我们先核对「反应映射」，再判断记录的按键是否与目标匹配。

collocations: a response mapping between symbols and keys

words.enDefinition: Findings about whether respondents use the processes assumed by the score interpretation

examples.en: The class reviews response process evidence from fictional students discussing how they interpreted an item.
examples.zh: 课堂审阅了虚构学生讲述如何理解一道题时提供的「作答过程证据」。

examples.en: We identified which explanation counted as response process evidence for the proposed score use.
examples.zh: 我们辨认出哪项说明可作为预定分数用途的「作答过程证据」。

words.enDefinition: The time interval during which a task accepts and records a response.

examples.en: The diagram showed the response window opening only after the target appeared in the example task.
examples.zh: 图中示例任务要等目标出现才打开「有效作答时段」。

examples.en: The response window in the practice example covered more time than the one in the test condition.
examples.zh: 练习示例的「有效作答时段」比正式测试条件下的更长。

words.enDefinition: Data available only to authorized users under stated access conditions.

examples.en: The fictional study described restricted-access data alongside a public summary that anyone could read.
examples.zh: 虚构研究在介绍谁都可以阅读的公开摘要时，也说明了「受限访问数据」。

examples.en: We discussed why the paper listed restricted-access data rather than placing individual records in the open supplement.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了论文为何列出「受限访问数据」，而没有把每个人的记录放进开放的补充材料。

words.enDefinition: Time separating initial learning from a later test of memory

examples.en: The review chart lists the retention interval for each hypothetical memory test.
examples.zh: 复习图表列出了每次假设记忆测验的「保持间隔」。

examples.en: Our group compared two scores obtained after the same retention interval in the simulation.
examples.zh: 我们组比较了模拟中相同「保持间隔」之后得到的两个分数。

words.enDefinition: The difference in corresponding image locations on the two retinas.

examples.en: The diagram showed retinal disparity by comparing where the same point appeared in the two eye images.
examples.zh: 示意图对比同一点在两眼图像中的位置，从而展示「视网膜视差」。

examples.en: In the classroom example, changing retinal disparity made one part of the image appear nearer than another.
examples.zh: 在课堂示例中，改变「视网膜视差」使图像的一部分看起来比另一部分更近。

collocations: a cue based on retinal disparity

words.enDefinition: Hint that helps someone access information already stored in memory

examples.en: In the worksheet, the first letter serves as a retrieval cue for the word.
examples.zh: 在习题中，该单词的首字母充当它的「提取线索」。

examples.en: We tested whether a picture was an effective retrieval cue for a studied name.
examples.zh: 我们检验了图片能否作为所学姓名的有效「提取线索」。

words.enDefinition: Inability to access stored information at the time it is needed

examples.en: The example illustrates retrieval failure when a familiar word comes back after prompting.
examples.zh: 示例用提示后想起熟悉单词的情形说明先前发生了「提取失败」。

examples.en: We distinguished retrieval failure from never forming a usable memory of the item.
examples.zh: 我们把「提取失败」与一开始就没有形成可用记忆区分开来。

words.enDefinition: Practice that requires actively bringing previously learned information to mind

examples.en: Our study group used retrieval practice by answering questions with the book closed.
examples.zh: 我们学习小组通过合上书回答问题来做「提取练习」。

examples.en: The article compares retrieval practice with rereading the same short explanation about memory.
examples.zh: 文章比较了「提取练习」与重读同一段关于记忆的简短说明。

words.enDefinition: Disruption of memory for earlier information by new learning or experiences

examples.en: The simulation depicts retroactive interference when the second list disrupts recall of the first.
examples.zh: 模拟用第二份列表妨碍回忆第一份列表来说明「倒摄干扰」。

examples.en: Our worksheet uses two lists of made-up words to demonstrate retroactive interference.
examples.zh: 我们的习题用两份虚构词汇列表展示「倒摄干扰」。

words.enDefinition: An account of an experience or action given after it has occurred.

examples.en: The retrospective report asked fictional students to describe which study activity they had chosen the previous week.
examples.zh: 「回顾性报告」让虚构学生描述前一周选了哪项学习活动。

examples.en: We compared the retrospective report with records that were made as the simulated task was happening.
examples.zh: 我们把「回顾性报告」与模拟任务进行时所作的记录作比较。

collocations: a retrospective report of an experience
compare retrospective reports with current reports

words.enDefinition: behavior observed when an attachment figure returns following a separation in the stated observation context

examples.en: The note describes reunion behavior by recording how the fictional child responded when the caregiver came back.
examples.zh: 记录通过描述照护者回来时虚构儿童的反应，说明其「重聚行为」。

examples.en: We compared reunion behavior with behavior during the separation phase of the same classroom video example.
examples.zh: 我们对照「重聚行为」与同一课堂视频示例中分离阶段的行为。

words.enDefinition: A single-case design comparing repeated measurements as a study condition is introduced and withdrawn.

examples.en: The toy reversal design returned to the original screen layout after a block using the changed layout.
examples.zh: 在简化的「反转设计」中，使用新版布局完成一个区段后，屏幕恢复到了原来的布局。

examples.en: We read the reversal design graph to see whether the fictional scores returned to their earlier levels.
examples.zh: 我们阅读「反转设计」的图，查看虚构得分是否回到了之前的水平。

collocations: a graph from a reversal design

words.enDefinition: Item whose numerical scoring runs opposite to its presented response order

examples.en: The scoring sheet shows how the point values change for a reverse-scored item.
examples.zh: 计分表展示了一道「反向计分题」的分值如何调整。

examples.en: We marked the reverse-scored item before comparing scores across the two sample versions.
examples.zh: 我们在比较两个示例版本的分数之前标出了「反向计分题」。

words.zhGloss: 皮亚杰理论中的可逆性
words.enDefinition: the ability to mentally undo an operation and understand that the original state can be restored
acceptedZhAnswers: 皮亚杰理论中的可逆性

examples.en: The tutor illustrated reversibility in Piaget's theory by asking students to imagine undoing the movement of objects.
examples.zh: 老师请学生设想撤回对物件的移动，以说明「皮亚杰理论中的可逆性」。

examples.en: We discussed reversibility in Piaget's theory after the fictional learner described how to restore the original arrangement.
examples.zh: 虚构学习者描述如何恢复原来的排列之后，我们讨论了「皮亚杰理论中的可逆性」。

collocations: task illustrating reversibility in Piaget's theory
reasoning with reversibility in Piaget's theory

words.enDefinition: An evaluation of a study's foreseeable harms and anticipated benefits.

examples.en: The classroom risk-benefit assessment considered the time burden and the information a fictional study might provide.
examples.zh: 课堂上的「风险与益处评估」考虑了时间负担，以及虚构研究可能提供的信息。

examples.en: We read the risk-benefit assessment to see which parts of the fictional proposal it discussed.
examples.zh: 我们阅读「风险与益处评估」，查看它讨论了虚构申请方案的哪些部分。

words.enDefinition: incompatible expectations arising from two or more social roles held by the same person

examples.en: The example illustrates role conflict when a fictional learner's work shift overlaps a required class meeting.
examples.zh: 虚构学习者的工作班次与必到的课堂会议时间重叠，示例用此说明「角色冲突」。

examples.en: We identified role conflict by showing which competing expectations came from different positions held by the character.
examples.zh: 我们指出人物担任的哪些不同身份带来了相互竞争的预期，以辨认「角色冲突」。

collocations: role conflict between work and study

words.enDefinition: The way someone performs the behaviors associated with a social position.

examples.en: The reading compared role enactment by two fictional librarians working under the same stated job expectations.
examples.zh: 阅读材料比较了两名虚构图书管理员在相同岗位预期下如何「践行角色」。

examples.en: We studied role enactment by comparing how the same person performed an assigned role in two settings.
examples.zh: 我们比较同一个人在两种情境中如何履行指定角色，借此研究「角色践行」。

words.enDefinition: the process of disengaging from a social role and adjusting to an identity or routine after leaving it

examples.en: The case study describes role exit as a fictional student organizer hands over responsibilities and changes their routine.
examples.zh: 个案研究描述虚构学生组织者移交职责并改变日常安排的「角色退出」过程。

examples.en: We traced the role exit timeline from initial doubts to the point when the new identity became familiar.
examples.zh: 我们沿「角色退出」时间线，从最初的疑虑追踪到新身份逐渐熟悉的时刻。

words.enDefinition: organized expectations about the typical conduct and responsibilities of a person in a particular social role

examples.en: The classroom example used a role schema for the chairperson to explain the fictional group's initial expectations.
examples.zh: 课堂示例用对主持人的「角色图式」解释虚构小组最初的预期。

examples.en: We compared two role schema descriptions to see which expectations changed when the meeting context differed.
examples.zh: 我们对照两项「角色图式」描述，查看会议情境不同时哪些预期发生改变。

words.enDefinition: the several role relationships and expectations associated with one social position

examples.en: The worksheet shows a teacher's role set by mapping relationships with students, colleagues and supervisors in the example.
examples.zh: 习题在示例中标出与学生、同事及主管的关系，展示一名教师的「角色集合」。

examples.en: We counted the distinct relationships within the role set for the fictional librarian in the classroom model.
examples.zh: 我们数出课堂模型中虚构图书管理员的「角色集合」包含哪些不同关系。

collocations: role set of an occupational position

words.enDefinition: difficulty meeting multiple expectations attached to a single social role

examples.en: The tutor used role strain to describe a fictional instructor's difficulty balancing several demands within the same job.
examples.zh: 老师用「角色紧张」描述虚构教师难以平衡同一职务中的若干要求。

examples.en: We distinguished role strain within one position from a conflict between two different positions in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中，我们区分同一身份内的「角色紧张」与两个不同身份之间的冲突。

words.enDefinition: imagining another person's position and expectations to understand how a situation may appear to them

examples.en: The exercise uses role taking when students explain the same meeting from another participant's position in the story.
examples.zh: 习题要求学生从故事中另一位参与者的身份解释同一次会议，运用了「角色采择」。

examples.en: We discussed role taking after the fictional group anticipated how newcomers would understand its unspoken expectations.
examples.zh: 虚构团体设想新人会怎样理解未说出的预期后，我们讨论了「角色采择」。

words.enDefinition: the role of an attachment figure as a source of comfort or protection when someone is distressed

examples.en: The classroom story illustrates a safe haven when the child returns for comfort after an unexpected sound.
examples.zh: 课堂故事中，儿童听到意外声音后回来寻求安慰，展示了「安全避风港」的作用。

examples.en: We compared the safe haven function with exploration from a secure base in the textbook's drawing.
examples.zh: 我们在教材图中，对照「安全避风港」的功能与以安全基地为起点的探索。

words.enDefinition: In a factor model, equality of item intercepts or thresholds across groups along with equality of corresponding factor loadings.

examples.en: The workbook shows scalar invariance after adding equality constraints on item intercepts.
examples.zh: 练习册在增加题目截距相等的约束后展示了「截距不变性」。

examples.en: We discussed scalar invariance using continuous indicators in the fictional factor model.
examples.zh: 我们用虚构因子模型中的连续指标讨论了「截距不变性」。

words.enDefinition: a specialty using psychology to support learning, development and well-being in school settings

examples.en: The school psychology reading discusses how a team can interpret learning information from different classroom activities.
examples.zh: 「学校心理学」阅读材料讨论一个团队如何解读来自不同课堂活动的学习信息。

examples.en: We compared a school psychology question about classroom support with a general research question about memory.
examples.zh: 我们将「学校心理学」中有关课堂支持的问题与普通记忆研究问题比较。

words.enDefinition: Range of scores grouped together for reporting or interpretation

examples.en: The mock report groups similar scores in a single score band.
examples.zh: 模拟报告将相近的分数归入同一个「分数区间」。

examples.en: We noted that each score band in the table had its own description.
examples.zh: 我们注意到表里的每个「分数区间」都有对应的说明。

collocations: assign scores to a score band

words.enDefinition: Property that scores from different forms carry the same intended meaning

examples.en: The tutor discussed score equivalence after showing two versions of the same fictional assessment.
examples.zh: 老师展示同一虚构测验的两个版本后，讨论了「分数等值性」。

examples.en: We checked whether the report provided any evidence of score equivalence across forms.
examples.zh: 我们查看报告是否提供了不同卷本之间的「分数等值性」证据。

words.enDefinition: Consistency of test scores across replications under specified measurement conditions

examples.en: The report discusses score reliability using two comparable administrations of the fictional test.
examples.zh: 报告用两次可比较的虚构测验施测来讨论「分数信度」。

examples.en: We considered score reliability before deciding how much to read into small score differences.
examples.zh: 在判断应如何看待小幅分差之前，我们先考虑了「分数信度」。

words.enDefinition: an incorrect belief about what another person believes, involving nested representation of another mind

examples.en: The story illustrates a second-order false belief when one character guesses incorrectly what another character thinks happened.
examples.zh: 故事中的一个人物错误猜测另一个人物对所发生事情的看法，说明了「二阶错误信念」。

examples.en: We mapped the layers of belief on the board to clarify the second-order false belief in the example.
examples.zh: 我们在黑板上画出信念的各层关系，以厘清示例中的「二阶错误信念」。

collocations: reason about a second-order false belief

words.enDefinition: learning roles and expectations associated with settings beyond one's earliest social environment

examples.en: The classroom example describes secondary socialization when a fictional student learns the expectations of a new institution.
examples.zh: 课堂示例描述虚构学生学习新机构各种预期时发生的「次级社会化」。

examples.en: We compared experiences of secondary socialization in a workplace and a fictional student organization in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们比较工作场所与虚构学生组织里的「次级社会化」经历。

words.enDefinition: In Allport's theory, a more limited preference or tendency that becomes evident in particular situations.

examples.en: The fictional profile presents a preference for quiet study rooms as a secondary trait in this textbook framework.
examples.zh: 在教材的这个框架下，虚构人物画像把偏好安静自习室写作一项「次要特质」。

examples.en: Our assignment asks students to identify a secondary trait that appears only in a narrow set of circumstances.
examples.zh: 作业要求学生找出只在少数特定情境中表现出来的一项「次要特质」。

words.enDefinition: an attachment pattern in which a person readily uses the caregiver for comfort and as a base for exploration

examples.en: The classroom recording describes secure attachment through a pattern of seeking comfort and returning to exploration afterward.
examples.zh: 课堂录像通过寻求安慰后又回到探索中的行为模式，描述「安全型依恋」。

examples.en: We read the discussion of secure attachment as a pattern in a relationship observed under specific conditions.
examples.zh: 我们阅读有关「安全型依恋」的讨论，将它理解为在特定条件下观察到的关系模式。

words.enDefinition: an attachment figure's availability that supports exploration away from them while they remain accessible

examples.en: The story shows a secure base when the child explores while checking that the caregiver remains available.
examples.zh: 故事中，儿童探索房间，同时确认照护者仍可接近，展示了「安全基地」的作用。

examples.en: We related the child's exploration to the secure base shown in the fictional classroom video example.
examples.zh: 我们将儿童的探索行为和课堂虚构视频示例里的「安全基地」联系起来。

collocations: use a caregiver as a secure base

words.enDefinition: Prioritizing particular information while filtering out competing information.

examples.en: The lecture illustrated selective attention with a recording in which students followed one of two voices.
examples.zh: 老师播放一段录音，让学生从两个人声中选一个专心听，以说明「选择性注意」。

examples.en: We discussed selective attention after comparing the features students noticed while focusing on different moving shapes.
examples.zh: 我们比较了学生留意不同运动图形时发现的特征，然后讨论了「选择性注意」。

words.enDefinition: a lifespan framework involving choosing important goals, investing resources to pursue them and adapting when resources decline

examples.en: The fictional example of selective optimization with compensation describes prioritizing a goal and adapting the means used.
examples.zh: 有关「选择性优化与补偿」的虚构示例描述优先追求一个目标，并调整所用手段。

examples.en: We identified three parts of selective optimization with compensation in the classroom case of an older musician.
examples.zh: 我们在关于一位老年音乐家的课堂案例中，辨认出「选择性优化与补偿」的三个部分。

collocations: model of selective optimization with compensation
example of selective optimization with compensation

words.enDefinition: A theory of how people see themselves as individuals or as group members depending on the context.

examples.en: The lecture introduces self-categorization theory using a fictional student who describes themselves differently across two classroom settings.
examples.zh: 讲座用一名在两个课堂情境中有不同自我描述的虚构学生，介绍「自我分类理论」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks what changes when the group level becomes important in the example of self-categorization theory.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，在「自我分类理论」的示例中，群体层面变得重要时会发生什么变化。

words.enDefinition: The degree to which a person's beliefs about themselves are clearly defined, internally consistent, and stable over time.

examples.en: The fictional diary exercise illustrates self-concept clarity by comparing statements about personal interests across several months.
examples.zh: 虚构日记练习比较了数月间有关个人兴趣的表述，用以说明「自我概念清晰性」。

examples.en: Our reading asks whether self-concept clarity concerns having consistent self-beliefs even when their content is complex.
examples.zh: 读物询问，即使信念内容复杂，「自我概念清晰性」是否仍涉及自我认识的一致程度。

words.enDefinition: An expectation that helps produce the outcome it anticipates by influencing behaviour or interactions.

examples.en: The textbook illustrates a self-fulfilling prophecy through a fictional club member whose expectations change their participation.
examples.zh: 教材用一名因预期而改变参与方式的虚构社团成员来说明「自我实现的预言」。

examples.en: In the seminar, a self-fulfilling prophecy explains why the character's initial prediction eventually came to pass.
examples.zh: 在研讨课示例中，「自我实现的预言」解释了角色最初的预测后来为何成真。

words.enDefinition: In personality and social psychology, the tendency to observe and adjust one's social presentation in response to situational cues.

examples.en: The example illustrates self-monitoring through a fictional character who changes their conversational style across two settings.
examples.zh: 示例通过虚构角色在两个场合改变说话风格，说明「自我监控」。

examples.en: Our seminar uses self-monitoring to describe attention to social cues when someone manages how they present themselves.
examples.zh: 研讨课用「自我监控」描述一个人在调整自我呈现时对社交线索的留意。

words.enDefinition: The theory that people can infer their attitudes or feelings by observing their own behaviour and its circumstances.

examples.en: The textbook uses self-perception theory to discuss how a fictional student infers an interest from repeated choices.
examples.zh: 教材用「自我知觉理论」讨论虚构学生怎样根据反复作出的选择推断自己的兴趣。

examples.en: Our seminar compares self-perception theory with another account of how the character arrived at a stated preference.
examples.zh: 研讨课对照了「自我知觉理论」与另一种解释，二者都说明角色如何形成其所述偏好。

words.enDefinition: Instrument that obtains information from respondents about their own experiences or behavior

examples.en: The fictional self-report measure asks participants to describe their own study habits.
examples.zh: 虚构的「自陈测量工具」请作答者描述自己的学习习惯。

examples.en: We compared a self-report measure of practice habits with a mock observation record.
examples.zh: 我们将一份关于练习习惯的「自陈测量工具」与模拟观察记录作了比较。

collocations: compare a self-report measure with observer ratings

words.enDefinition: an organized set of beliefs and expectations about a particular aspect of oneself

examples.en: The example shows how a self-schema about being organized changed which details a fictional learner recalled.
examples.zh: 示例展示，对自己做事有条理的「自我图式」如何改变虚构学习者能回想起哪些细节。

examples.en: We discussed the self-schema concept using different descriptions of how students see themselves in class.
examples.zh: 我们使用不同的学生自我描述，讨论「自我图式」概念。

words.enDefinition: A tendency to explain outcomes in ways that favour one's self-image, such as taking credit for successes more readily than failures.

examples.en: The tutor introduces self-serving attribution bias by comparing a fictional student's explanations for positive and negative results.
examples.zh: 老师比较虚构学生对正面和负面结果的解释，以介绍「自利性归因偏差」。

examples.en: Our classroom example asks whether self-serving attribution bias could explain the contrasting accounts in the fictional diary.
examples.zh: 课堂示例询问，「自利性归因偏差」是否能解释虚构日记中截然不同的记述。

words.enDefinition: the availability of more than one plausible interpretation of a word, phrase or sentence based on meaning

examples.en: The class identified semantic ambiguity because the word bat could mean an animal or sports equipment.
examples.zh: 由于 bat 可指一种动物，也可指一种体育器材，全班辨认出了「语义歧义」。

examples.en: We resolved semantic ambiguity after the next sentence described a bat flying out of a cave.
examples.zh: 下一句描述了蝙蝠从洞里飞出，我们由此消除了「语义歧义」。

words.enDefinition: Forming a memory representation based on the meaning of information

examples.en: The activity illustrates semantic encoding by asking students to sort words by meaning.
examples.zh: 活动让学生按意思给词汇分类，以此说明「语义编码」。

examples.en: We compared semantic encoding with a task that focused only on a word's sound.
examples.zh: 我们将「语义编码」与仅关注词语读音的任务作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Long-term knowledge of facts, concepts, and meanings detached from particular episodes

examples.en: The diagram links semantic memory with knowing what a familiar academic term means.
examples.zh: 示意图将「语义记忆」与知道熟悉的学术术语的意思联系起来。

examples.en: The class contrasted semantic memory with remembering where a definition was first learned.
examples.zh: 课堂将「语义记忆」与记得最初在哪里学到某一定义相对照。

words.enDefinition: Change in processing a target after exposure to a related meaning

examples.en: The animation uses semantic priming to explain faster responses after a related word appears.
examples.zh: 动画用「语义启动」解释为何呈现相关单词后的反应更快。

examples.en: We tested for semantic priming in a fictional dataset containing related and unrelated word pairs.
examples.zh: 我们在包含相关和无关词对的虚构数据里检验是否存在「语义启动」。

words.enDefinition: A personality tendency involving interest in novel, varied, and intense experiences.

examples.en: The fictional participant's interest in exploring unfamiliar music and performance styles illustrates one aspect of sensation seeking.
examples.zh: 虚构参与者对探索不熟悉的音乐和表演风格感兴趣，体现了「感觉寻求」的一方面。

examples.en: The classroom reading discusses sensation seeking using preferences reported across several ordinary leisure activities in a fictional survey.
examples.zh: 课堂读物根据虚构调查中对几种普通休闲活动的偏好，讨论了「感觉寻求」。

words.enDefinition: a developmental interval when a particular experience has an unusually strong effect, although learning can continue later

examples.en: The text describes a sensitive period as a time of increased responsiveness to experience in its example.
examples.zh: 教材在示例中将「敏感期」描述为对经验更敏感的一段时间。

examples.en: We discussed how learning later in life could coexist with a sensitive period for earlier learning.
examples.zh: 我们讨论成年后仍可学习，如何与早年存在学习的「敏感期」相容。

words.enDefinition: Heightened responsiveness to stimulation following prior exposure to a stimulus

examples.en: The graph illustrates sensitization with a stronger response to the same gentle sound.
examples.zh: 图表用对同一轻柔声音更强的反应来说明「敏感化」。

examples.en: Our group contrasted sensitization with habituation using the two simulated response curves.
examples.zh: 我们组用两条模拟反应曲线对照了「敏感化」与习惯化。

words.enDefinition: Piaget's earliest stage of cognitive development, when infants learn mainly through perceptual and motor activity

examples.en: The classroom reading connects the sensorimotor stage with exploring objects through repeated looking and reaching in infancy.
examples.zh: 课堂阅读材料把「感知运动阶段」与婴儿反复注视及伸手探索物体联系起来。

examples.en: We compared two kinds of action shown during the sensorimotor stage in the textbook's theoretical timeline.
examples.zh: 我们对照教材理论时间线上「感知运动阶段」出现的两类动作。

words.enDefinition: Brief persistence of sensory information after the original stimulation ends

examples.en: The class diagram places sensory memory just after the first visual or auditory input.
examples.zh: 课堂示意图把「感觉记忆」放在最初的视觉或听觉输入之后。

examples.en: We compared the visual and auditory forms of sensory memory in the lecture.
examples.zh: 我们在讲座中比较了「感觉记忆」的视觉形式和听觉形式。
