words.enDefinition: upset that can occur when a person is separated from an attachment figure

examples.en: The observation sheet marked separation distress after the familiar caregiver left the room in the fictional demonstration.
examples.zh: 在虚构演示中，熟悉的照护者离开房间后，观察表记下一次「分离苦恼」。

examples.en: We discussed why separation distress can vary with the setting and the preceding events in the example.
examples.zh: 我们讨论在示例中，「分离苦恼」为何可能随场景和先前事件不同而变化。

collocations: separation distress during an unfamiliar event

words.enDefinition: Variation in memory performance with an item's position in a sequence

examples.en: The chart depicts the serial position effect by plotting recall against each item's list position.
examples.zh: 图表按各项目在列表中的位置绘制其回忆表现，以展示「系列位置效应」。

examples.en: Our seminar used a short word list to introduce the serial position effect.
examples.zh: 研讨课用一个简短词表来介绍「系列位置效应」。

collocations: tests of the serial position effect

words.enDefinition: Retrieval of previously presented items in their original presentation order

examples.en: The exercise uses serial recall to check whether students remember the original order.
examples.zh: 练习用「序列回忆」检查学生是否记得原先的顺序。

examples.en: We counted misplaced letters as order errors in the serial recall condition.
examples.zh: 在「序列回忆」条件下，我们把放错位置的字母计为顺序错误。

words.enDefinition: arranging items in order according to a graded property, such as length, weight or magnitude

examples.en: The seriation task asked the group to arrange several rods from shortest to longest in the exercise.
examples.zh: 「按属性排序」任务要求小组在练习中把几根棒按从短到长排列。

examples.en: We compared two strategies for seriation by examining how fictional learners inserted a new item in order.
examples.zh: 我们观察虚构学习者怎样依序插入一个新物件，以比较两种「按属性排序」策略。

words.enDefinition: a reciprocal exchange in which a child's signal or action receives a responsive reply from another person

examples.en: The animation illustrates serve-and-return interaction when a caregiver responds to the child's gesture and the child responds again.
examples.zh: 动画中，照护者回应儿童手势，儿童又再次回应，展示了「往返式回应互动」。

examples.en: We marked each turn in the serve-and-return interaction to show how the exchange continued in the example.
examples.zh: 我们标出「往返式回应互动」中的每轮来回，说明示例中的交流如何持续。

words.enDefinition: A change in search performance as the number of displayed items changes.

examples.en: The graph showed a set-size effect because responses became slower when more distractors appeared on the screen.
examples.zh: 图中，屏幕上的干扰项变多时反应变慢，说明存在「项目数量效应」。

examples.en: The instructor compared the set-size effect across two tasks with different ways of defining the target.
examples.zh: 老师比较了两种不同目标定义的任务中的「项目数量效应」。

collocations: a set-size effect on reaction time

words.enDefinition: Perceiving an object's shape as stable across changes in viewing angle.

examples.en: The instructor used shape constancy to explain why an angled door still looked rectangular in the video.
examples.zh: 老师用「形状恒常性」解释为什么视频中侧着看的门仍显得是长方形。

examples.en: Shape constancy mattered in the example even though the outline on the screen changed with the camera angle.
examples.zh: 虽然屏幕上的轮廓随拍摄角度改变，例子中的「形状恒常性」仍然起了作用。

words.enDefinition: Developing a target behavior by reinforcing progressively closer versions of it

examples.en: The textbook uses shaping by successive approximations to explain a fictional sequence of closer matches.
examples.zh: 教材用「逐次逼近塑造」来解释一系列越来越接近目标的虚构匹配。

examples.en: We identified shaping by successive approximations on the simulation chart beside the changing criteria.
examples.zh: 我们在模拟图表不断变化的标准旁标出了「逐次逼近塑造」。

collocations: example of shaping by successive approximations
stages of shaping by successive approximations

words.enDefinition: A tendency for groups to discuss information already known to several members more than information held by only one or a few.

examples.en: The mock committee transcript illustrates shared information bias because members repeatedly discuss details they all already know.
examples.zh: 模拟委员会记录里，成员反复讨论大家已经知道的细节，体现了「共享信息偏差」。

examples.en: Our class counted references to unshared facts before considering whether shared information bias appeared in the fictional meeting.
examples.zh: 全班统计了提及未共享事实的次数，再考虑虚构会议是否出现了「共享信息偏差」。

words.enDefinition: Limited retention of information over a brief period of time

examples.en: In the demo, students use short-term memory to report a color sequence immediately.
examples.zh: 在演示中，学生用「短时记忆」立即说出颜色序列。

examples.en: The worksheet distinguishes short-term memory from remembering material learned in an earlier semester.
examples.zh: 习题把「短时记忆」和记得上学期学过的内容区分开来。

words.enDefinition: A detection trial containing background activity without the target signal.

examples.en: The recording contained only background noise during the signal-absent trial illustrated on the classroom slide.
examples.zh: 课堂投影片展示的「无信号试次」中，录音里只有背景噪声。

examples.en: Our worksheet included a signal-absent trial with a yes response to illustrate a false alarm.
examples.zh: 我们的习题用回答有信号的「无信号试次」来说明什么是虚报。

collocations: a response on a signal-absent trial
a correct response on a signal-absent trial

words.enDefinition: Requesting a participant report whenever a study prompt or notification arrives.

examples.en: In the signal-contingent sampling example, the fictional diary entry was made when a study notification arrived.
examples.zh: 在「信号触发取样」示例中，收到研究通知后才填写虚构日记。

examples.en: The class compared signal-contingent sampling with reports triggered by an everyday event instead of a notification.
examples.zh: 全班比较了「信号触发取样」与由日常事件触发、无须通知的报告方式。

words.enDefinition: A framework separating detection sensitivity from the criterion for reporting a signal.

examples.en: Signal detection theory explained why two observers with similar hearing sensitivity sometimes gave different answers.
examples.zh: 「信号检测理论」解释了为何听觉敏感性相近的两名观察者有时会给出不同回答。

examples.en: The seminar used signal detection theory to distinguish better discrimination from a willingness to answer yes.
examples.zh: 讨论课运用「信号检测理论」区分了辨别力提高和更倾向于回答检出。

collocations: a model from signal detection theory
an introduction to signal detection theory

words.enDefinition: A detection trial in which the target signal is actually present.

examples.en: The faint tone made that example a signal-present trial even though the listener answered no.
examples.zh: 听者虽然回答没有，但这一试次确实播放了微弱音调，所以属于「有信号试次」。

examples.en: We marked each signal-present trial using the stimulus record before looking at the simulated responses.
examples.zh: 我们根据刺激记录标出每个「有信号试次」，再看模拟作答。

collocations: a response on a signal-present trial

words.enDefinition: The delay between one known signal and one predefined response.

examples.en: The simple reaction time example used a single symbol and the same response on every trial.
examples.zh: 「简单反应时」示例只用一种符号，每个试次要求作出相同反应。

examples.en: We calculated simple reaction time from the appearance of the symbol to the recorded key press.
examples.zh: 我们以符号出现到记录下按键的间隔计算「简单反应时」。

words.enDefinition: An experimental design using repeated observations within one or more cases to evaluate condition changes.

examples.en: The single-case experimental design tracked one fictional student's responses across several versions of a classroom task.
examples.zh: 「单案例实验设计」追踪一名虚构学生在课堂任务不同版本中的作答。

examples.en: We compared patterns within each fictional case before discussing what the single-case experimental design showed overall.
examples.zh: 讨论「单案例实验设计」整体说明了什么之前，我们先比较各虚构案例内部的数据模式。

collocations: repeated observations in a single-case experimental design

words.enDefinition: The extent to which clear expectations, constraints, or consequences in a setting narrow the range of behaviour.

examples.en: Our textbook illustrates situation strength by comparing a structured exercise with an open discussion of the same topic.
examples.zh: 教材比较结构固定的练习与关于同一主题的开放讨论，用以说明「情境强度」。

examples.en: The seminar asks whether differences in situation strength help explain the fictional participants' more similar behaviour there.
examples.zh: 研讨课讨论「情境强度」的差异是否有助于解释虚构参与者在该场景中的行为为何更相似。

words.enDefinition: An explanation of behaviour that focuses on external circumstances rather than a personal characteristic.

examples.en: The worksheet calls the explanation about a changed meeting time a situational attribution for the fictional student's lateness.
examples.zh: 练习单将虚构学生迟到解释为会议时间改变，并称之为「情境归因」。

examples.en: Our discussion compares a situational attribution with an explanation centred on the fictional character's usual habits.
examples.zh: 我们将「情境归因」与以虚构角色的平时习惯为中心的解释作比较。

words.enDefinition: The tendency for a behaviour or response to be tied to particular features of the setting.

examples.en: The classroom profile illustrates situational specificity when a fictional student volunteers ideas only during small group meetings.
examples.zh: 课堂人物画像借一名虚构学生只在小组会议上主动提意见来说明「情境特异性」。

examples.en: Our discussion considers whether situational specificity explains the different responses recorded in the two fictional classroom settings.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「情境特异性」能否解释两个虚构课堂场景中记录的不同反应。

words.enDefinition: Perceiving an object's size as stable across changes in viewing distance.

examples.en: The size constancy slide showed why a receding object need not appear physically smaller to the viewer.
examples.zh: 「大小恒常性」投影片说明，物体逐渐远去时，观察者感知的实际大小不一定变小。

examples.en: We discussed size constancy after comparing pictures of the same box at two different distances.
examples.zh: 我们比较了同一个盒子在不同距离拍摄的两张照片，然后讨论了「大小恒常性」。

words.enDefinition: The overall pattern and distribution of sleep stages across a sleep period.

examples.en: We compared sleep architecture in two simulated nights that had the same total amount of sleep.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两夜模拟记录的「睡眠结构」，它们的总睡眠时长相同。

examples.en: The lecture illustrated sleep architecture by plotting changes in stage across the complete fictional recording.
examples.zh: 老师把整份虚构记录中的阶段变化绘成图，以展示「睡眠结构」。

words.enDefinition: A recurring progression through non-REM and REM stages during a sleep period.

examples.en: The classroom chart showed one sleep cycle in detail before turning to the remaining night.
examples.zh: 课堂图表先详细展示了一个「睡眠周期」，然后才展示当晚的其余时段。

examples.en: We traced a sleep cycle by following the sequence of stages on the simulated graph.
examples.zh: 我们沿着模拟图上的阶段顺序，梳理了一个「睡眠周期」。

words.enDefinition: The proportion of time in bed or the recording period actually spent asleep.

examples.en: Our worksheet defined sleep efficiency as time asleep divided by total time in bed for the example.
examples.zh: 习题在这个例子中将「睡眠效率」定义为睡眠时长除以卧床总时长。

examples.en: The two fictional charts showed different sleep efficiency despite recording the same total time in bed.
examples.zh: 两张虚构图表记录的卧床总时长相同，但显示的「睡眠效率」不同。

words.enDefinition: Temporary grogginess or reduced alertness immediately after waking from sleep.

examples.en: The example described sleep inertia as a short period of reduced alertness after the fictional participant woke.
examples.zh: 示例把「睡眠惯性」描述为虚构参与者醒来后警觉性暂时较低的一小段时间。

examples.en: We discussed sleep inertia when the simulated scores improved across the first several observations after waking.
examples.zh: 模拟得分在醒来后的前几次观察中逐步提高，我们就此讨论了「睡眠惯性」。

words.enDefinition: The time from a specified bedtime or sleep opportunity to sleep onset.

examples.en: The worksheet measured sleep latency from the start of the observation window to the first sleep interval.
examples.zh: 习题从观察时段开始算到第一个睡眠时段，以测量「入睡潜伏期」。

examples.en: The second simulated record had a longer sleep latency even though both observation windows started together.
examples.zh: 尽管两个观察时段同时开始，第二份模拟记录的「入睡潜伏期」更长。

words.enDefinition: A brief burst of rhythmic brain activity commonly seen during N2 sleep.

examples.en: The instructor circled a sleep spindle because the short rhythmic burst stood out from the surrounding trace.
examples.zh: 老师圈出了「睡眠纺锤波」，因为这段短暂的节律波在周围记录中很突出。

examples.en: We compared a sleep spindle with a slower waveform on the synthetic classroom recording.
examples.zh: 我们将课堂合成记录中的「睡眠纺锤波」与一种更慢的波形作比较。

collocations: the shape of a sleep spindle

words.enDefinition: The daily pattern of alternating sleep and wakefulness.

examples.en: The diagram placed the sleep-wake cycle beside the simulated changes in alertness over one day.
examples.zh: 图中把「睡眠觉醒周期」与一天内模拟的警觉性变化并列展示。

examples.en: We used a full day of synthetic data to trace changes in the sleep-wake cycle.
examples.zh: 我们用一整天的合成数据梳理了「睡眠觉醒周期」的变化。

collocations: the timing of the sleep-wake cycle
a feature of the sleep-wake cycle

words.enDefinition: resources accessible through social relationships or networks, such as information, support or opportunities

examples.en: The reading uses social capital to explain how fictional students learned about different resources through their relationships.
examples.zh: 阅读材料用「社会资本」解释虚构学生如何通过自己的人际关系了解各种资源。

examples.en: We compared two forms of social capital in the classroom example about information shared across student groups.
examples.zh: 在关于学生群体间信息共享的课堂示例中，我们对照两种「社会资本」。

words.enDefinition: a grouping based on a person's economic and social position, defined according to the theoretical framework being used

examples.en: The textbook compares two definitions of social class using income, occupation and control of resources as criteria.
examples.zh: 教材以收入、职业和对资源的控制为判断标准，对照「社会阶级」的两种定义。

examples.en: We discussed how different measures of social class could classify the same fictional household differently in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「社会阶级」的不同度量怎样可能将习题中同一虚构家庭归入不同类别。

words.enDefinition: a process by which a group restricts access to valued opportunities or resources to preserve its advantages

examples.en: The reading describes social closure when a fictional association limited entry and thereby restricted access to its benefits.
examples.zh: 阅读材料用虚构协会限制加入、从而限制福利获得的方式描述「社会封闭」。

examples.en: We discussed how social closure could occur through both explicit rules and informal barriers in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 我们讨论课堂示例中，「社会封闭」如何既可能通过明示规则，也可能通过非正式障碍发生。

words.enDefinition: the process by which shared interactions and institutions produce meanings treated as common reality

examples.en: The lecture uses the social construction of reality to examine how repeated interaction established a shared classroom routine.
examples.zh: 讲义借「现实的社会建构」考察反复互动如何形成共同的课堂惯例。

examples.en: We discussed the social construction of reality after several fictional groups assigned different meanings to the same event.
examples.zh: 数个虚构小组为同一事件赋予不同意义后，我们讨论了「现实的社会建构」。

collocations: study the social construction of reality
process of the social construction of reality
examples of the social construction of reality

words.enDefinition: formal or informal mechanisms through which a group encourages conformity with its norms and discourages deviation

examples.en: The reading compares social control through a written rule with control through reactions in the fictional group.
examples.zh: 阅读材料比较虚构群体通过书面规则和通过成员反应实现「社会控制」的两种方式。

examples.en: We identified different forms of social control in the classroom case by looking at how expectations were enforced.
examples.zh: 我们通过查看如何落实各项行为预期，在课堂案例中辨认出不同形式的「社会控制」。

words.enDefinition: A tendency to report answers perceived as socially approved.

examples.en: The worksheet considered social desirability bias when fictional survey answers seemed more favorable than the activity records.
examples.zh: 虚构问卷答案似乎比活动记录更正面，习题据此考察了「社会赞许偏差」。

examples.en: We discussed social desirability bias before treating every response in the example as an accurate account of behavior.
examples.zh: 在把例题中的每个作答都视为准确的行为描述之前，我们先讨论了「社会赞许偏差」。

collocations: a possible sign of social desirability bias

words.enDefinition: an account distinguishing moral concerns, social conventions and personal choices as domains of social judgment

examples.en: The lecture uses social domain theory to contrast judgments about harm with judgments about an ordinary classroom convention.
examples.zh: 讲义用「社会领域理论」对照有关伤害的判断与有关普通课堂惯例的判断。

examples.en: We applied social domain theory to three fictional rules and discussed how the reasons for them differed.
examples.zh: 我们将「社会领域理论」用于三条虚构规则，讨论支持它们的理由有什么不同。

words.enDefinition: a consequence of a practice or institution that reduces the adaptation or functioning of a specified social system

examples.en: The worksheet labels the added barriers as a social dysfunction of the otherwise useful procedure in the example.
examples.zh: 习题把示例中一种通常有用的程序所造成的额外障碍标为「社会失功能」。

examples.en: We discussed who was affected by the social dysfunction before generalizing about the whole institution in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们先讨论哪些人受到「社会失功能」影响，再对整个制度作概括。

words.enDefinition: restricted participation in social, economic or civic life because important opportunities or resources are inaccessible

examples.en: The report uses social exclusion when discussing barriers that prevented participation in two fictional community services.
examples.zh: 报告讨论虚构社区两项服务的参与障碍时，使用了「社会排斥」。

examples.en: We identified one form of social exclusion by checking which residents lacked invitations and transport to community events.
examples.zh: 我们查看哪些居民缺少参加社区活动的邀请和交通条件，辨认出一种「社会排斥」。

words.enDefinition: In one common usage, improved performance in the presence of others, especially on simple or well-practised tasks.

examples.en: Several students sorted familiar shapes faster while a classmate watched, illustrating social facilitation in the example.
examples.zh: 几名学生在同学注视下更快地分拣熟悉的形状，示例用这个现象说明「社会促进」。

examples.en: Our reading notes that social facilitation in the example concerns performance on a task already well practised.
examples.zh: 读物指出，示例中的「社会促进」涉及已经很熟练的任务表现。

words.enDefinition: in Durkheim's sociology, an established way of acting or thinking that exists beyond individuals and influences their behavior

examples.en: The reading describes a shared scheduling rule as a social fact that shapes individual choices in the example.
examples.zh: 阅读材料把共同遵守的排程规则描述为一种会影响个人选择的「社会事实」。

examples.en: We discussed why a social fact can persist even as the people following the practice change over time.
examples.zh: 我们讨论即使遵循做法的人随时间更替，一项「社会事实」为何仍可持续存在。

words.enDefinition: a graded pattern in an outcome across levels of social or economic position

examples.en: The chart illustrates a social gradient in recorded access across several ordered resource groups in the fictional data.
examples.zh: 图表说明虚构数据中，依资源多寡排序的多个群体在实测获得机会方面呈现「社会梯度」。

examples.en: We checked intermediate groups before concluding that the example showed a social gradient across the full range.
examples.zh: 我们先检查中间群体，再判断示例是否在整个范围内呈「社会梯度」。

words.enDefinition: The part of a person's self-concept derived from group memberships and the significance attached to them.

examples.en: The fictional campus profile illustrates social identity through a character's sense of belonging to several activity groups.
examples.zh: 虚构校园人物画像通过角色对几个活动小组的归属感，说明「社会认同」。

examples.en: Our seminar considers how social identity can reflect different group memberships in different settings across the fictional story.
examples.zh: 研讨课讨论，在虚构故事的不同情境中，「社会认同」如何体现不同的群体归属。

words.enDefinition: A theory explaining how group membership and comparisons between groups can shape self-concept and intergroup behaviour.

examples.en: The textbook introduces social identity theory with fictional examples of how students describe their group memberships.
examples.zh: 教材用虚构学生描述自身群体归属的例子，介绍「社会认同理论」。

examples.en: Our class uses social identity theory to interpret a fictional comparison between two teams sharing a workspace.
examples.zh: 全班用「社会认同理论」解读一项关于共用工作场地的两个团队的虚构比较。

collocations: research informed by social identity theory

words.enDefinition: The effect of other people or groups on an individual's thoughts, feelings, or behaviour.

examples.en: The introductory seminar illustrates social influence using a fictional group's changing preferences during a shared reading activity.
examples.zh: 入门研讨课用虚构小组在共读活动里不断变化的偏好说明「社会影响」。

examples.en: Our class discusses whether social influence could account for the change recorded in the imaginary group's notes.
examples.zh: 全班讨论「社会影响」能否解释虚构小组笔记记录的变化。

words.enDefinition: In group performance research, a decline in performance in the presence of others, often on unfamiliar or difficult tasks.

examples.en: The summary illustrates social inhibition with weaker performance on a new task while fictional observers are present.
examples.zh: 摘要用虚构观察者在场时新任务表现较差的例子说明「社会抑制」。

examples.en: Our class discusses whether social inhibition might explain the difference between the two fictional performance scores here.
examples.zh: 全班讨论「社会抑制」是否可能解释本例中两个虚构表现分数之间的差距。

words.enDefinition: an enduring set of roles, rules and practices organizing an important area of social life

examples.en: The lecture describes schooling as a social institution with established roles, functions and expectations in the example.
examples.zh: 讲义把学校教育描述为示例中的一种「社会制度」，具有既定的角色、功能和预期。

examples.en: We compared a social institution with a particular organization that operates within it in the classroom discussion.
examples.zh: 课堂讨论中，我们对照一项「社会制度」与在其中运作的某个具体组织。

words.enDefinition: reciprocal action or communication through which people influence and respond to one another

examples.en: The class observed social interaction by noting how one fictional participant's greeting changed the next person's response.
examples.zh: 全班记录一位虚构参与者的问候如何改变下一个人的回答，以观察「社会互动」。

examples.en: We compared social interaction in two situations where the same phrase carried a different meaning for participants.
examples.zh: 我们比较两种情境中的「社会互动」，同一个短语对参与者的含义不同。

words.enDefinition: A tendency to exert less individual effort on some collective tasks than when doing the same task alone.

examples.en: The fictional table illustrates social loafing by comparing an individual's effort on the same solo and pooled task.
examples.zh: 虚构表格对照同一个人在独立完成和集体完成同一任务时的投入程度，说明「社会惰化」。

examples.en: Our seminar treats social loafing as one possible account of the effort pattern in the fictional group.
examples.zh: 研讨课把「社会惰化」当作解释虚构小组投入模式的一种可能说法。

words.enDefinition: processes that push people or groups away from full participation, voice or access to valued resources

examples.en: The case study describes social marginalization through repeated exclusion from decision making in a fictional community organization.
examples.zh: 个案研究通过虚构社区组织里一再被排除在决策之外的经历，描述「社会边缘化」。

examples.en: We discussed social marginalization when the classroom model showed weakening access to several ordinary spaces over time.
examples.zh: 课堂模型展示进入若干普通场所的机会随时间减弱时，我们讨论了「社会边缘化」。

words.enDefinition: movement of a person or group between positions in a system of social stratification

examples.en: The exercise illustrates social mobility by comparing positions at two points in the fictional participant's working life.
examples.zh: 练习比较虚构参与者在职业生涯两个时间点的社会地位，展示「社会流动」。

examples.en: We discussed social mobility after reading the classroom table comparing occupational groups across generations in the model.
examples.zh: 阅读模型中各世代职业群体对照表后，我们在课堂上讨论了「社会流动」。

words.enDefinition: a sustained collective effort seeking to promote, resist or reverse change in society

examples.en: The classroom case describes a social movement that organized recurring public events around a stated shared goal.
examples.zh: 课堂案例描述一项围绕明示共同目标组织多次公共活动的「社会运动」。

examples.en: We distinguished a social movement from one isolated gathering by examining continuity across the fictional timeline.
examples.zh: 我们考察虚构时间线中的持续性，将「社会运动」与单独一次聚集区分开。

words.enDefinition: the proportion of all possible connections among actors that are present in a specified network representation

examples.en: The worksheet calculates social network density from the number of recorded ties and all possible ties between members.
examples.zh: 习题用已记录的联系数和成员之间所有可能的联系数计算「社会网络密度」。

examples.en: We compared social network density across sample groups with different numbers of people in the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 课堂练习中，我们比较人数不同的样例群体的「社会网络密度」。

words.enDefinition: a relationship or connection between two actors represented in a social network

examples.en: The network diagram draws one social network tie for each pair who regularly exchanged messages in the example.
examples.zh: 示例中，网络图用一条「社会网络联结」表示两人经常互发消息。

examples.en: We checked the definition of a social network tie before comparing the two simulated network graphs.
examples.zh: 比较两张模拟网络图之前，我们先核对什么算作一条「社会网络联结」。

words.enDefinition: public decisions and programs concerning social welfare, access to services and related social conditions

examples.en: The course compared two social policy approaches to supporting access to education in fictional communities with different resources.
examples.zh: 课程对照帮助资源不同的虚构社区获得教育的两种「社会政策」取向。

examples.en: We discussed which institution implemented the social policy described in the classroom's sample report on service provision.
examples.zh: 我们讨论是哪个机构实施了课堂服务供给样例报告所述的「社会政策」。

words.enDefinition: the study of how real or imagined social contexts influence thoughts, feelings and behavior

examples.en: The social psychology experiment compared individual answers with answers given in the presence of a group.
examples.zh: 这项「社会心理学」实验比较个人独自回答与在群体在场时给出的回答。

examples.en: We studied a social psychology example in which a perceived group norm changed a fictional participant's choice.
examples.zh: 我们学习了一个「社会心理学」示例，其中虚构参与者所感知的群体规范改变了其选择。

words.enDefinition: using another person's emotional cues to interpret an unfamiliar or ambiguous situation

examples.en: The fictional child in the animation used social referencing by looking at the caregiver's expression before approaching.
examples.zh: 动画中的虚构儿童先看照护者的表情再靠近，运用了「社会参照」。

examples.en: We discussed social referencing after watching how a reaction from the adult changed the character's interpretation.
examples.zh: 我们观看成人反应怎样改变人物的解读后，讨论了「社会参照」。

collocations: use social referencing in an unfamiliar situation

words.enDefinition: processes by which existing social relations, advantages or inequalities are sustained or transmitted over time

examples.en: The reading examines social reproduction by tracing how unequal access to education can persist across generations.
examples.zh: 阅读材料通过追踪教育机会的不平等如何在代际延续，探讨「社会再生产」。

examples.en: We identified a mechanism of social reproduction in the classroom example involving family resources and institutional expectations.
examples.zh: 我们在涉及家庭资源与制度预期的课堂示例中，找出一种「社会再生产」机制。

words.enDefinition: A shared expectation to help people who need assistance, even when no return favour is expected.

examples.en: The fictional case illustrates a social responsibility norm when students feel an obligation to help unfamiliar peers.
examples.zh: 虚构案例用学生认为有义务帮助不熟悉的同龄人来说明「社会责任规范」。

examples.en: Our discussion compares the social responsibility norm with an expectation of returning a specific favour in the example.
examples.zh: 我们将示例中的「社会责任规范」与回报特定帮助的期待作比较。

collocations: expectation under a social responsibility norm
influence of a social responsibility norm

words.enDefinition: A pattern of expected behaviour associated with a position within a group or social setting.

examples.en: The classroom case assigns a social role to each character in the fictional student society's meeting.
examples.zh: 课堂案例为虚构学生社团会议中的每个角色安排了一种「社会角色」。

examples.en: Our discussion compares the social role of a meeting chair with the expectations for other members.
examples.zh: 我们把会议主持人的「社会角色」与其他成员行为受到的期待作比较。

collocations: expectations associated with a social role

words.enDefinition: public or other organized support intended to reduce hardship when people face specified risks or insufficient resources

examples.en: The policy diagram shows a social safety net covering several types of hardship in a fictional system.
examples.zh: 政策图表示一个涵盖虚构制度中若干类困难的「社会保障网」。

examples.en: We compared two social safety net programs by examining which situations each was designed to address in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们考察两个「社会保障网」项目各自旨在解决哪些情形，并作对照。

collocations: program in the social safety net

words.enDefinition: a social response that rewards conformity or discourages violations of a group expectation

examples.en: The seminar used a public compliment as one example of a social sanction in the fictional setting.
examples.zh: 研讨课把公开称赞作为虚构情境中「社会制裁」的一例。

examples.en: We classified the social sanction after checking which behavior the group's response reinforced in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 我们核查课堂示例中的群体回应强化了哪种行为，再将其归入某类「社会制裁」。

words.enDefinition: the ties and shared commitments that hold members of a group or society together

examples.en: The lecture describes social solidarity through examples of people cooperating across different roles in the fictional community.
examples.zh: 讲义通过虚构社区中不同角色的人相互合作的实例，描述「社会团结」。

examples.en: We compared two forms of social solidarity in the chapter on changing patterns of social organization.
examples.zh: 我们在讨论社会组织模式变化的一章里，对照了两种「社会团结」形式。

words.enDefinition: a recognized position a person occupies in a social system, sometimes associated with rank or prestige

examples.en: The worksheet treats being a student as a social status with expected behavior in the fictional institution.
examples.zh: 习题把学生身份视为虚构机构内伴随行为预期的一种「社会地位」。

examples.en: We compared two positions to see how social status shaped the relationships shown in the sample network.
examples.zh: 我们比较两个位置，考察「社会地位」怎样塑造样例关系网中所示的关系。

words.enDefinition: Interpreting individuals through generalised beliefs associated with their perceived social group membership.

examples.en: Our fictional example illustrates social stereotyping when an observer assumes all members of a club share identical motives.
examples.zh: 虚构示例中，观察者假定某个社团所有成员动机相同，体现了「社会刻板化」。

examples.en: The class discusses social stereotyping after checking whether the observations actually support the observer's broad assumption.
examples.zh: 全班先查明观察记录是否确实支持观察者的宽泛假设，再讨论「社会刻板化」。

words.enDefinition: the organization of society into unequal layers associated with differences in resources, status or power

examples.en: The chart illustrates social stratification by showing unequal access to three resources in the fictional society.
examples.zh: 图表通过展示虚构社会获取三种资源的机会不均，说明「社会分层」。

examples.en: We compared models of social stratification that gave different weight to occupation, wealth and prestige in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们对照对职业、财富和声望给予不同权重的「社会分层」模型。

words.enDefinition: relatively persistent patterns of relationships, positions and institutions that organize social life

examples.en: The diagram represents social structure through recurrent links between families, schools and workplaces in the example.
examples.zh: 图中用家庭、学校和工作场所之间反复出现的联系表示示例中的「社会结构」。

examples.en: We examined which features of social structure persisted after individuals moved into different roles in the classroom model.
examples.zh: 我们考察课堂模型中的人换到不同角色之后，「社会结构」的哪些特征仍然存在。

words.enDefinition: the process through which people learn social expectations, roles and ways of participating in groups

examples.en: The socialization example shows a new member learning how people take turns in a fictional club.
examples.zh: 「社会化」示例展示虚构社团的新成员怎样学习成员轮流发言的办法。

examples.en: We discussed socialization by comparing what participants learned at home with what they learned in school.
examples.zh: 我们通过对比参与者在家与在校习得的内容，讨论「社会化」。

words.enDefinition: an approach associated with Vygotsky that explains development through social activity and the use of cultural tools

examples.en: The lecture connects the sociocultural theory of development with how learners use shared language while solving a problem.
examples.zh: 讲义将「发展的社会文化理论」与学习者解题时怎样使用共同语言联系起来。

examples.en: We interpreted the guided classroom task using the sociocultural theory of development in the discussion.
examples.zh: 我们在讨论中依据「发展的社会文化理论」，解读有人指导的课堂任务。

collocations: apply the sociocultural theory of development
explanation from the sociocultural theory of development

words.enDefinition: position relative to other people or households, commonly assessed using indicators such as education, occupation and income

examples.en: The classroom exercise compares two ways of measuring socioeconomic status using fictional household records.
examples.zh: 课堂练习用虚构的住户记录，比较衡量「社会经济地位」的两种方法。

examples.en: We checked which indicators were included in the socioeconomic status measure before interpreting the table in class.
examples.zh: 课堂解读表格之前，我们先核对「社会经济地位」指标包括了哪些方面。

words.enDefinition: changes in emotional expression, regulation and social relationships across development

examples.en: The socioemotional development unit describes changing ways of expressing feelings and joining peer activities over time.
examples.zh: 「社会情绪发展」单元描述表达感受和参与同伴活动的方式如何随时间变化。

examples.en: We compared socioemotional development examples from home and school in the fictional child's case study.
examples.zh: 我们在虚构儿童个案研究中，对照家庭与学校里的「社会情绪发展」示例。

words.enDefinition: a theory proposing that a more limited perceived future shifts priority toward emotionally meaningful goals and relationships

examples.en: The lecture uses socioemotional selectivity theory to compare preferences under two different imagined future time horizons in class.
examples.zh: 课堂讲义用「社会情绪选择理论」比较两种不同的想象未来时限下的偏好。

examples.en: We discussed socioemotional selectivity theory when the study compared long-term goals with immediate emotionally meaningful choices.
examples.zh: 研究对照长期目标与当下具有情感意义的选择时，我们讨论了「社会情绪选择理论」。

words.enDefinition: the ability to connect individual experiences with historical conditions and the wider organization of society

examples.en: The exercise uses sociological imagination to connect one student's commute with the distribution of campus housing.
examples.zh: 这个练习用「社会学想象力」将一名学生的通勤经历与校园住房分布联系起来。

examples.en: We practiced sociological imagination by looking for institutional factors behind an apparently private problem in the story.
examples.zh: 我们通过在故事里寻找一个表面上很个人的问题背后的制度因素，练习「社会学想象力」。

words.enDefinition: the systematic study of social life, social relationships and the organization of societies

examples.en: The sociology lecture compared how two institutions organize similar responsibilities through different rules and routines.
examples.zh: 「社会学」讲义比较两个机构怎样通过不同规则与惯例安排相近的职责。

examples.en: We used a sociology example to connect a personal experience with broader patterns of education and employment.
examples.zh: 我们用一个「社会学」示例，把个人经历与更广泛的教育和就业模式联系起来。

words.enDefinition: Identifying the apparent position of a sound source.

examples.en: The lecture illustrated sound localization by asking where on the screen the recorded click seemed to originate.
examples.zh: 老师问大家，录音里的咔嗒声听起来来自屏幕的什么位置，以说明「声源定位」。

examples.en: We explained the sound localization judgments using differences in the signals reaching the two simulated ears.
examples.zh: 我们用到达两只模拟耳朵的信号差异解释「声源定位」判断。

words.enDefinition: Process of deciding where a remembered detail or impression came from

examples.en: The source monitoring exercise asks whether a fact came from reading or discussion.
examples.zh: 「来源监测」练习要求判断某条事实来自阅读还是讨论。

examples.en: We discussed source monitoring when participants confused two speakers in the fictional transcript.
examples.zh: 参与者混淆了虚构笔录中的两名说话者，我们借此讨论了「来源监测」。

words.enDefinition: Better later memory for study episodes separated in time than compressed together

examples.en: The sample data illustrate the spacing effect when the same study time is spread out.
examples.zh: 样本数据用同等学习时间分散安排的情形说明「间隔效应」。

examples.en: We compared two schedules before interpreting the spacing effect in the fictional results.
examples.zh: 我们先比较了两种时间安排，再解释虚构结果中的「间隔效应」。

words.enDefinition: Using a cue to direct attention toward a possible target location.

examples.en: The spatial cueing demonstration compared responses to targets that appeared on the left or right.
examples.zh: 「空间线索提示」演示比较了目标出现在左右两侧时的作答。

examples.en: We used the spatial cueing diagram to see which locations were indicated before the target appeared.
examples.zh: 我们查看「空间线索提示」示意图，找出目标出现前哪些位置得到了提示。

words.enDefinition: Formula relating reliability to changes in length under parallel measurement assumptions

examples.en: The tutor used the Spearman-Brown formula to illustrate how test length affects estimated reliability.
examples.zh: 老师用「斯皮尔曼布朗公式」说明测验长度如何影响信度估计值。

examples.en: We checked the assumptions behind the Spearman-Brown formula before interpreting the predicted reliability.
examples.zh: 解读预测的信度之前，我们核对了「斯皮尔曼布朗公式」所依据的假设。

words.enDefinition: identifying word or other linguistic boundaries in a stream of spoken language

examples.en: The speech segmentation task asked listeners to mark where one word ended and another began in class.
examples.zh: 课堂「语流切分」任务要求听者标出一个词在哪里结束、另一个词从哪里开始。

examples.en: We discussed how familiar sound patterns can help speech segmentation when there are few pauses between words.
examples.zh: 我们讨论词与词之间很少停顿时，熟悉的语音模式怎样帮助「语流切分」。

words.enDefinition: Internal consistency estimate based on scores from two parts of a test

examples.en: The workbook illustrates split-half reliability by comparing scores from odd and even items.
examples.zh: 练习册用比较奇数题和偶数题得分来说明「分半信度」。

examples.en: We discussed why split-half reliability might change when the test is split differently.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么采用不同分题方式时，「分半信度」可能会变化。

words.enDefinition: Reappearance of an extinguished learned response after a period of rest

examples.en: The model shows spontaneous recovery when a weak learned response returns after a pause.
examples.zh: 模型用停顿后弱化的习得反应重新出现来说明「自发恢复」。

examples.en: We found spontaneous recovery after the break but before any new stimulus pairing.
examples.zh: 我们发现「自发恢复」发生在休息之后、任何新的刺激配对之前。

words.enDefinition: A tendency to overestimate how much other people notice one's actions or appearance.

examples.en: The fictional example illustrates the spotlight effect when a speaker overestimates how many classmates notice a small stumble.
examples.zh: 虚构示例中，发言者高估了注意到轻微磕绊的同学人数，用以说明「聚光灯效应」。

examples.en: Our worksheet compares students' guesses with fictional observers' recollections to illustrate how the spotlight effect is studied.
examples.zh: 练习单对照学生的猜测和虚构观察者的回忆，以说明如何研究「聚光灯效应」。

words.enDefinition: Estimated standard deviation of score errors under specified measurement conditions

examples.en: The score table gives one overall standard error of measurement beneath the hypothetical test results.
examples.zh: 分数表在假设测验结果下方给出一项总体的「测量标准误」。

examples.en: We used the standard error of measurement to discuss uncertainty around the simulated test score.
examples.zh: 我们用「测量标准误」来讨论模拟测验分数的不确定性。

collocations: estimate the standard error of measurement
report the standard error of measurement

words.enDefinition: Group whose assessment results are used to establish norms or scoring references

examples.en: The manual identifies the standardization sample used to generate its reference scores.
examples.zh: 手册说明了用于生成参照分数的「标准化样本」。

examples.en: Our group discussed whether the standardization sample resembled the population in the workbook.
examples.zh: 我们组讨论了「标准化样本」是否与练习册里的目标总体相似。

words.enDefinition: Conducting a test under consistent, specified instructions and conditions

examples.en: Both simulated sessions use the same instructions to illustrate standardized administration in the workbook.
examples.zh: 练习册中的两次模拟施测采用相同说明，以演示「标准化施测」。

examples.en: The class discussed how standardized administration supports more consistent comparisons across mock sessions.
examples.zh: 课堂讨论了「标准化施测」如何让各次模拟施测之间的比较更一致。

words.enDefinition: Task directions presented consistently across participants or conditions.

examples.en: Both groups received standardized instructions before seeing different versions of the fictional sorting task in class.
examples.zh: 两组收到相同的「标准化指导语」，随后在课堂上看到虚构分类任务的不同版本。

examples.en: We compared two sets of standardized instructions to see whether their wording differed across the examples.
examples.zh: 我们比较两组「标准化指导语」，看看不同示例中的措辞是否有差别。

words.enDefinition: the degree to which a person's position is similar across several dimensions of social rank

examples.en: The exercise illustrates status consistency with a fictional position ranked highly on both pay and prestige.
examples.zh: 习题用收入和声望两方面排名都较高的虚构社会位置，说明「地位一致性」。

examples.en: We measured status consistency by comparing where the same fictional cases ranked on each of three indicators.
examples.zh: 我们比较同批虚构案例在三个指标上各自的排名，以衡量「地位一致性」。

words.enDefinition: a mismatch among a person's rankings on different dimensions such as income, education and prestige

examples.en: The example illustrates status inconsistency by ranking one fictional job high in prestige and low in pay.
examples.zh: 示例将一项虚构职业的声望排名列高、收入排名列低，说明「地位不一致」。

examples.en: We classified the pattern as status inconsistency after comparing the position's different rankings in the classroom table.
examples.zh: 我们对照课堂表格中同一地位在多个维度的排名，将该模式归为「地位不一致」。

words.enDefinition: a preference for keeping an existing arrangement over comparable alternatives partly because it is already in place

examples.en: The example shows status quo bias when students favor their current timetable despite equivalent alternatives in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习给出等价备选项时，学生仍偏好现用课表，示例显示了「现状偏差」。

examples.en: We distinguished status quo bias from a reasonable preference based on lower cost in the classroom comparison.
examples.zh: 在课堂对照中，我们区分「现状偏差」与基于较低成本的合理偏好。

collocations: status quo bias in decision making

words.enDefinition: the collection of different social positions that one individual occupies at the same time

examples.en: The class illustrated a status set by listing the positions one fictional person held across three institutions.
examples.zh: 全班列出虚构人物在三个机构同时拥有的身份，用来说明「地位集合」。

examples.en: We compared the status set for two people with different combinations of school and family positions in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们比较学校与家庭身份组合不同的两个人的「地位集合」。

words.enDefinition: Depth perception arising from differences between the two eyes' images.

examples.en: The instructor used paired pictures to illustrate stereopsis even though each picture alone looked completely flat.
examples.zh: 老师用成对图画展示「双眼立体视觉」，尽管单看每幅图都显得完全是平面的。

examples.en: The reading distinguished stereopsis from depth impressions that could arise when viewing with just one eye.
examples.zh: 阅读材料区分了「双眼立体视觉」和仅用一只眼睛观察时也能产生的深度感。

words.enDefinition: The particular traits or expectations that make up a stereotype about a group.

examples.en: The class discusses stereotype content by comparing the assumptions that fictional observers attach to two invented clubs.
examples.zh: 课堂比较虚构观察者对两个虚构社团抱有的假设，以讨论「刻板印象的具体内容」。

examples.en: Our worksheet analyses stereotype content without treating the reported assumptions as facts about any actual group.
examples.zh: 练习单分析「刻板印象的具体内容」，并把材料中的假设与任何实际群体的事实区分开。

words.enDefinition: A model that organises many stereotypes along dimensions of perceived warmth and competence.

examples.en: The seminar introduces the stereotype content model by comparing two dimensions in a set of invented profiles.
examples.zh: 研讨课比较一组虚构画像中的两个维度，介绍「刻板印象内容模型」。

examples.en: Our worksheet uses the stereotype content model to distinguish descriptions of presumed intentions from presumed ability.
examples.zh: 练习单用「刻板印象内容模型」区分对假定意图与假定能力的描述。

collocations: dimensions of the stereotype content model
assumptions examined in the stereotype content model

words.enDefinition: A model relating sensation magnitude to a power of stimulus intensity.

examples.en: Stevens' power law allowed the two example judgments to follow curves with different exponents.
examples.zh: 「史蒂文斯幂定律」允许用指数不同的曲线表示两种示例判断。

examples.en: The instructor compared Stevens' power law with a logarithmic model on the same classroom plot.
examples.zh: 老师在同一幅课堂图中比较了「史蒂文斯幂定律」与对数模型。

collocations: a prediction from Stevens' power law
the exponent in Stevens' power law

words.enDefinition: Learned difference in responding to stimuli that signal different events

examples.en: The game illustrates stimulus discrimination by associating only one of two shapes with points.
examples.zh: 游戏只将两种图形中的一种与得分关联起来，以说明「刺激辨别」。

examples.en: We compared stimulus discrimination and generalization using the same simulated set of colors.
examples.zh: 我们用同一组模拟颜色比较了「刺激辨别」与泛化。

words.enDefinition: Transfer of a learned response to stimuli resembling the original cue

examples.en: The stimulus generalization exercise uses several shades of blue to represent similar cues.
examples.zh: 「刺激泛化」练习用深浅不同的蓝色代表相似线索。

examples.en: We saw stimulus generalization when similar sounds produced responses in the classroom simulation.
examples.zh: 在课堂模拟中，相似的声音也引起反应时，我们看到了「刺激泛化」。

words.enDefinition: The point in time when a stimulus ends or disappears.

examples.en: The worksheet showed stimulus offset at the moment the target picture disappeared from the simulated display.
examples.zh: 习题在目标图片从模拟画面消失的时刻标注了「刺激结束呈现」。

examples.en: We measured the following blank interval from stimulus offset to the appearance of the next picture.
examples.zh: 我们从「刺激结束呈现」到下一幅图出现，测量随后的空白间隔。

words.enDefinition: The point in time when a stimulus first appears or begins.

examples.en: The graph aligned the recordings at stimulus onset so that we could compare the response times.
examples.zh: 图中将各条记录对齐在「刺激开始呈现」的时间点，以便比较反应时。

examples.en: We marked stimulus onset on the slide at the moment the target became visible in the center.
examples.zh: 我们在投影片上把目标在中央变得可见的时刻标为「刺激开始呈现」。

words.enDefinition: The time from the beginning of one stimulus to the beginning of another.

examples.en: We calculated stimulus onset asynchrony using the two start markers rather than the end of either stimulus.
examples.zh: 我们根据两个开始标记计算「刺激呈现起始间隔」，没有使用任何一个刺激的结束时间。

examples.en: The plot compared two stimulus onset asynchrony values with the same duration for each stimulus.
examples.zh: 图中比较了两种「刺激呈现起始间隔」，两种情况下单个刺激的持续时间都相同。

collocations: plot performance against stimulus onset asynchrony

words.enDefinition: Presentation of two stimuli in relation to one another during conditioning

examples.en: The first section of the animation illustrates stimulus pairing with two simple symbols.
examples.zh: 动画的第一部分用两个简单符号说明「刺激配对」。

examples.en: We labeled the stimulus pairing phase separately from the trials with one cue alone.
examples.zh: 我们将「刺激配对」阶段与只呈现一个线索的试次分开标注。

words.enDefinition: Repeating the same response across a series of survey items

examples.en: The simulated row illustrates straightlining by repeating the same answer across several items.
examples.zh: 模拟数据用一行多道题都选相同答案的情形说明「直线式作答」。

examples.en: We discussed why straightlining may occur even when responses are given thoughtfully.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么即使经过认真思考，也可能出现「直线式作答」。

words.enDefinition: a standardized observation of infant exploration, brief separations and reunions used in attachment research

examples.en: The lecture reviews Strange Situation procedure clips to illustrate how researchers classify patterns across parts of the observation.
examples.zh: 讲义回顾「陌生情境程序」的视频片段，说明研究者如何根据观察各环节的模式作分类。

examples.en: We used the Strange Situation procedure diagram to identify where reunion was assessed in the classroom reading.
examples.zh: 我们利用「陌生情境程序」图找出课堂阅读中在哪个环节评估重聚情况。

collocations: history of the Strange Situation procedure

words.enDefinition: caution or hesitation around an unfamiliar person, especially in descriptions of early social development

examples.en: The example shows stranger wariness when the child pauses before responding to an unfamiliar adult in the story.
examples.zh: 故事中的儿童在回应不认识的成人前先停顿，示例由此展示「陌生人戒备」。

examples.en: We contrasted two fictional observations of stranger wariness in settings that differed in familiarity to the child.
examples.zh: 我们对照两次「陌生人戒备」的虚构观察，两个环境对儿童的熟悉程度不同。

words.enDefinition: frontline public service in which officials use discretion to apply policy to individual cases

examples.en: The seminar uses street-level bureaucracy to analyze how workers interpret general rules in a fictional service office.
examples.zh: 研讨课用「街头官僚体系」分析虚构办事机构里的工作人员怎样理解一般规则。

examples.en: We discussed street-level bureaucracy when the example showed how repeated individual decisions affected everyday access to services.
examples.zh: 示例展示反复作出的个别决定如何影响日常服务获取时，我们讨论了「街头官僚体系」。

words.enDefinition: Equality of residual variances in addition to scalar measurement invariance

examples.en: The final model adds equal residual variances for the strict invariance comparison.
examples.zh: 最终模型加入残差方差相等的约束，以便进行「严格不变性」比较。

examples.en: We checked what the strict invariance model assumed beyond the previous model.
examples.zh: 我们检查了与上一个模型相比，「严格不变性」模型多了哪些假设。

words.enDefinition: a social connection marked by relatively frequent contact, emotional closeness or substantial mutual support

examples.en: The diagram classifies the closest friendship as a strong tie using the fictional survey's stated criteria.
examples.zh: 图按虚构调查所给标准，将最亲密的友谊归为一条「强关系」。

examples.en: We compared a strong tie within the group with a looser connection to someone outside it in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们将小组内的一条「强关系」与连接组外某人的较松散关系相比较。

words.enDefinition: The performance difference between conflicting and matching word-meaning and ink-color conditions in the classic task.

examples.en: The Stroop effect appeared when students took longer to name conflicting ink colors on the screen.
examples.zh: 学生说出与字义冲突的墨水颜色时用时更长，出现了「斯特鲁普效应」。

examples.en: The instructor used the Stroop effect to illustrate competition between a word meaning and a color response.
examples.zh: 老师用「斯特鲁普效应」展示字义与颜色作答之间的竞争。

collocations: a classroom example of the Stroop effect

words.enDefinition: a sociological perspective examining how interrelated institutions and practices contribute to continuity or change in society

examples.en: The instructor applied structural functionalism to ask how institutions in the fictional town organized recurring social tasks.
examples.zh: 老师用「结构功能主义」追问虚构城镇里的制度怎样安排反复出现的社会任务。

examples.en: We used structural functionalism to map relationships among education, work and family on the classroom diagram.
examples.zh: 我们用「结构功能主义」在课堂图上标出教育、工作和家庭间的关系。

words.enDefinition: persistent unequal opportunities or outcomes generated by the organization of multiple social systems and practices

examples.en: The course uses structural inequality to analyze how housing, education and employment jointly shaped the fictional group's opportunities.
examples.zh: 课程用「结构性不平等」分析住房、教育和就业如何共同塑造虚构群体的机会。

examples.en: We identified several connected mechanisms before describing the pattern as structural inequality in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 我们找到数个相互关联的机制之后，将课堂示例的模式描述为「结构性不平等」。

words.enDefinition: movement between social positions caused by changes in the distribution of available positions across society

examples.en: The classroom chart illustrates structural mobility after the fictional economy gains many more positions in one occupational group.
examples.zh: 虚构经济在一个职业群体中增加许多岗位后，课堂图用它说明「结构性流动」。

examples.en: We discussed how structural mobility can raise observed mobility even when patterns of relative advantage remain similar.
examples.zh: 我们讨论即使相对优势格局基本相同，「结构性流动」也可能使观测到的流动增加。

words.enDefinition: an early school of psychology that tried to analyze conscious experience into its basic elements

examples.en: The lecture introduces structuralism through historical attempts to describe the elements of a simple sensory experience.
examples.zh: 讲义通过历史上试图描述简单感觉经验各要素的做法，介绍「构造主义心理学」。

examples.en: We compared structuralism with a school that asked what a mental activity accomplishes for the person.
examples.zh: 我们把「构造主义心理学」与一个追问心理活动对个人有何作用的学派作比较。

words.enDefinition: Observation using a defined task, setting, or recording procedure applied consistently.

examples.en: The structured observation example gave each fictional group the same puzzle before coding their visible actions.
examples.zh: 「结构化观察」示例让各虚构小组完成同一道谜题，再给他们的可见行为编码。

examples.en: We used a structured observation template to record how often each action appeared in the sample clip.
examples.zh: 我们用「结构化观察」模板记录示例短片中每项动作出现的次数。

words.enDefinition: a group or shared way of life with distinctive practices or meanings within a wider society

examples.en: The reading illustrates a subculture through a fictional hobby group with distinctive language and shared meeting customs.
examples.zh: 阅读材料通过一个具有独特语言及共同聚会习惯的虚构兴趣小组，说明「亚文化」。

examples.en: We identified features of the subculture while noting that its members also participated in the wider community.
examples.zh: 我们辨认「亚文化」的特征，同时注意其成员也参加更广泛的社区活动。

words.enDefinition: an intermediate objective whose achievement can help make progress toward the overall goal of a problem

examples.en: The group set a subgoal of placing the corners before trying to complete the rest of the puzzle.
examples.zh: 小组设定先摆好各个角这一「子目标」，再尝试完成谜题的其余部分。

examples.en: We identified the subgoal that made it possible to apply the next move in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 我们找出课堂示例中使下一步操作得以实施的「子目标」。

words.enDefinition: how old a person feels or perceives themselves to be, which may differ from their chronological age

examples.en: The classroom survey on subjective age asked fictional respondents to report how old they felt on most days.
examples.zh: 有关「主观年龄」的课堂调查要求虚构受访者报告自己多数时候觉得有多大年龄。

examples.en: We compared subjective age with recorded chronological age in the anonymized example table from the course.
examples.zh: 我们在课程匿名示例表中，将「主观年龄」与记录的实际年龄对照。

collocations: difference between subjective age and chronological age

words.enDefinition: In the theory of planned behaviour, a person's perception of whether relevant others expect them to perform a behaviour.

examples.en: The fictional questionnaire illustrates a subjective norm through perceived expectations from classmates about attending a community event.
examples.zh: 虚构问卷以对同学希望自己参加社区活动的感知来说明「主观规范」。

examples.en: Our tutor distinguishes a subjective norm from the actions that other people actually take in the example.
examples.zh: 老师把「主观规范」与示例中他人实际采取的行为区分开来。

words.enDefinition: Processing of stimuli below a specified threshold for conscious awareness.

examples.en: The seminar discussed subliminal perception and asked how the fictional study assessed awareness of the image.
examples.zh: 讨论课以「阈下知觉」为主题，并追问虚构研究是怎样检验受试者是否察觉图像的。

examples.en: Our notes separated evidence for subliminal perception from claims about lasting effects on behavior.
examples.zh: 我们的笔记区分了「阈下知觉」的证据和关于持久影响行为的说法。

words.enDefinition: a more specific grouping contained within a broader category

examples.en: An office chair appears as a subordinate category under the broader heading chair in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 在课堂示例中，办公椅作为较宽泛标题椅子之下的「下位类别」。

examples.en: We chose a subordinate category to label only the examples that shared the narrower set of features.
examples.zh: 我们选用一个「下位类别」，只标记具有这组较窄特征的示例。

collocations: classify an item in a subordinate category

words.enDefinition: Score based on items assessing one part of a broader measure

examples.en: The mock report lists a subscale score for each section of the questionnaire.
examples.zh: 模拟报告列出了问卷各部分的「分量表得分」。

examples.en: We discussed why a subscale score could differ from the pattern in the overall score.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么某个「分量表得分」的表现可能与总分的趋势不同。

words.enDefinition: Score obtained by adding the assigned points from specified items

examples.en: The worksheet shows how a summed score combines points from several related questions.
examples.zh: 习题展示了「加总分」如何把几道相关题目的分值相加。

examples.en: We compared the summed score with a score that gave some items extra weight.
examples.zh: 我们把「加总分」与某些题目权重更高的得分作了比较。

words.enDefinition: a broad category containing several more specific categories

examples.en: The diagram places furniture as a superordinate category covering chairs, desks and other objects in the example.
examples.zh: 示例图把家具作为包含椅子、书桌及其他物件的「上位类别」。

examples.en: We added a superordinate category above several familiar groups to complete the classroom hierarchy chart.
examples.zh: 我们在几个熟悉的类别上方加上一个「上位类别」，完成课堂层级图。

words.zhGloss: 群体间的共同上位目标
words.enDefinition: A goal valued by different groups that requires their cooperation to achieve.
acceptedZhAnswers: 群体间的共同上位目标

examples.en: The vignette introduces a superordinate goal requiring the two fictional clubs to complete one joint exhibition.
examples.zh: 材料引入一个「群体间的共同上位目标」，需要两家虚构社团合办一场展览才能实现。

examples.en: Our class asks whether the assignment could qualify as a superordinate goal for the groups in the scenario.
examples.zh: 全班讨论，对于情境中的几组成员，这项任务能否算作「群体间的共同上位目标」。

words.enDefinition: A stimulus above the specified sensory threshold under stated conditions.

examples.en: One suprathreshold stimulus on the demonstration graph fell well above the estimated detection level.
examples.zh: 演示图上的一个「阈上刺激」远高于估计的检测水平。

examples.en: The instructor used a suprathreshold stimulus to discuss differences in appearance after detection became reliable.
examples.zh: 老师用一个「阈上刺激」讨论可靠检出以后仍能感知到的外观差异。

words.enDefinition: Maintaining engagement with a task or stream over an extended period.

examples.en: The sustained attention task involved watching for the same target throughout a long classroom simulation.
examples.zh: 「持续性注意」任务要求在较长的课堂模拟中始终留意同一种目标。

examples.en: The plot showed how sustained attention differed across successive blocks in the hypothetical data set.
examples.zh: 图中显示，在这组假想数据的连续几个试验区段里，「持续性注意」有何不同。

words.enDefinition: deductive reasoning in which a conclusion is drawn from two premises in a specified logical form

examples.en: The exercise tested syllogistic reasoning by asking learners whether a conclusion necessarily followed from the two statements.
examples.zh: 练习询问学习者结论是否必然由两个陈述推出，以测试「三段论推理」。

examples.en: We used a diagram of three categories to work through the syllogistic reasoning in the class example.
examples.zh: 我们用包含三个类别的示意图分析课堂示例中的「三段论推理」。

words.enDefinition: prestige, recognition or legitimacy that gives people or institutions influence in a particular social field

examples.en: The reading describes symbolic capital when a widely recognized distinction increased someone's credibility in the fictional organization.
examples.zh: 阅读材料把虚构组织里一项能提升个人可信度的荣誉作为「象征资本」的例子。

examples.en: We discussed which forms of recognition counted as symbolic capital in each setting of the classroom example.
examples.zh: 我们讨论在课堂示例的各个环境里，哪些认可形式算作「象征资本」。

words.enDefinition: a sociological perspective emphasizing how people create and revise meanings through interaction and the use of symbols

examples.en: The lecture uses symbolic interactionism to explain why identical gestures can receive different interpretations across settings.
examples.zh: 讲义用「符号互动论」解释同样的手势为何在不同情境里得到不同解读。

examples.en: We applied symbolic interactionism to compare the meanings the fictional participants attached to the same classroom object.
examples.zh: 我们用「符号互动论」比较虚构参与者赋予同一课堂物品的意义。

words.enDefinition: pretend activity in which one object, action or role stands for another

examples.en: The scene shows symbolic play when the child uses an ordinary block to represent an imaginary telephone.
examples.zh: 场景中，儿童用普通积木充当想象中的电话，表现出「符号性游戏」。

examples.en: We coded symbolic play separately from simple repetition of the object's usual movement in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中，我们将「符号性游戏」和只是重复物件通常的动作分别编码。

words.enDefinition: a form of mental representation in which discrete symbols and rules encode objects, properties or relations

examples.en: The reasoning model uses symbolic representation by assigning separate tokens to the objects and their relations.
examples.zh: 推理模型采用「符号表征」，为对象及其关系分别分配符号。

examples.en: We described the symbolic representation in the worksheet before applying any of the model's inference rules.
examples.zh: 在应用示例模型的任何推理规则之前，我们先描述练习中的「符号表征」。

words.enDefinition: the availability of more than one grammatical structure for the same sequence of words

examples.en: The example has syntactic ambiguity because the final phrase can attach to two different parts of the sentence.
examples.zh: 该例有「句法歧义」，因为最后一个短语可附接到句子的两个不同部分。

examples.en: We drew two structure trees to show where the syntactic ambiguity came from in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 我们画出两棵句法树，展示课堂示例中的「句法歧义」来自哪里。

words.enDefinition: Standardized score commonly scaled to mean fifty and standard deviation ten

examples.en: The class worksheet locates a T score on a scale with a labeled center.
examples.zh: 课堂习题在标出中心值的量尺上确定了一个「T分数」的位置。

examples.en: We checked that the T score column used the reporting scale described above.
examples.zh: 我们核对了「T分数」一栏是否采用上文描述的报告量尺。

words.enDefinition: early-emerging individual differences in emotional and behavioral reactivity and self-regulation that can develop over time

examples.en: The lecture introduces temperament by comparing how two fictional infants respond to the same unfamiliar classroom sound.
examples.zh: 讲义对照两名虚构婴儿对相同陌生课堂声音的反应，以介绍「气质」。

examples.en: We discussed temperament in the context of several observations rather than drawing conclusions from one isolated behavior.
examples.zh: 讨论「气质」时，我们以多次观察为背景，单独一次行为不足以得出结论。

words.enDefinition: Occurrence of two events close together in time during learning

examples.en: The animation uses closely spaced flashes to illustrate temporal contiguity between two events.
examples.zh: 动画用间隔很短的闪光说明两个事件之间的「时间邻近性」。

examples.en: We discussed temporal contiguity without assuming that either simulated event predicted the other.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「时间邻近性」，没有预设任何一个模拟事件会预测另一个。

words.enDefinition: Extent to which intended respondents can take a test without irrelevant barriers

examples.en: The practice report discusses test accessibility when the screen layout obscures instructions.
examples.zh: 练习报告讨论了屏幕布局遮住说明时的「测验可及性」。

examples.en: We considered test accessibility separately from differences in the skill being measured.
examples.zh: 我们把「测验可及性」与被测技能的差异分开考虑。

words.enDefinition: Adjustment reducing an irrelevant barrier while preserving the intended measurement construct

examples.en: The example describes a test accommodation that makes the fictional instructions easier to access.
examples.zh: 示例描述了一项让参与者更容易获取虚构测验的说明的「测验便利安排」。

examples.en: We discussed how a test accommodation might preserve access without changing the target skill.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「测验便利安排」如何在不改变目标技能的情况下保障参与。

words.enDefinition: Modification of an assessment for use in a new linguistic or cultural context

examples.en: The class examines test adaptation across two fictional language versions of a questionnaire.
examples.zh: 课堂考察了一份问卷的两种虚构语言版本之间的「测验调适」。

examples.en: We discussed test adaptation as involving more than translating response options word for word.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「测验调适」并不只是逐字翻译作答选项。

words.enDefinition: Plan specifying the content and skills an assessment should cover

examples.en: The test blueprint assigns space to pattern recognition and interpretation in the sample assessment.
examples.zh: 「测验蓝图」在样例测验中为规律识别和解释预留了题量。

examples.en: We checked the fictional questions against the topics listed in the test blueprint.
examples.zh: 我们将虚构题目与「测验蓝图」列出的主题逐一对照。

words.enDefinition: Statistical adjustment intended to make scores from comparable test forms interchangeable

examples.en: The fictional testing program uses test equating to account for differences in form difficulty.
examples.zh: 虚构测验项目用「测验分数等值」处理不同卷本难度上的差异。

examples.en: We discussed test equating after noticing that one mock form was slightly harder.
examples.zh: 注意到一份模拟卷稍难后，我们讨论了「测验分数等值」。

words.enDefinition: Principle of equitable access and appropriate score interpretations across intended groups

examples.en: The seminar treats test fairness as involving both access and interpretation of scores.
examples.zh: 研讨课认为「测验公平性」既涉及参与测验的条件，也涉及分数解释。

examples.en: Our group discussed test fairness using a fictional test that relied on unfamiliar language.
examples.zh: 我们组用一份使用陌生语言的虚构测验来讨论「测验公平性」。

words.enDefinition: Specific version of a test containing a particular set of items

examples.en: The two versions share a topic, but each test form presents distinct questions.
examples.zh: 两个版本涵盖同一主题，但每份「测验卷本」的题目不同。

examples.en: We checked whether each test form covered every skill on the blueprint.
examples.zh: 我们检查了每份「测验卷本」是否涵盖蓝图上的所有技能。

words.enDefinition: Function describing the measurement precision of a test across latent trait levels

examples.en: The test information function peaks above the center of the scale in this illustration.
examples.zh: 在这幅示意图中，「测验信息函数」在高于量尺中心的位置达到峰值。

examples.en: We compared the test information function for two invented assessments with different item mixtures.
examples.zh: 我们比较了题目构成不同的两份虚构测验的「测验信息函数」。

collocations: peak of the test information function

words.enDefinition: Consistency of scores when the same measure is administered on different occasions

examples.en: The worksheet estimates test-retest reliability using the same fictional questionnaire on two occasions.
examples.zh: 习题用同一份虚构问卷在两次施测中的数据估计「重测信度」。

examples.en: We discussed how a longer gap might affect the estimate of test-retest reliability.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了更长的时间间隔可能如何影响「重测信度」估计值。

words.enDefinition: Support from evidence and theory for interpreting scores for intended uses

examples.en: The lecture explains test score validity in relation to what the fictional scores are used for.
examples.zh: 讲座结合虚构分数的用途来解释「测验分数效度」。

examples.en: We discussed why test score validity could differ for two interpretations of the same scores.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么同一组分数用于两种解释时，「测验分数效度」可能不同。

words.enDefinition: A trial contributing to the main measurement after any introductory practice.

examples.en: The first test trial began once the fictional student had completed the examples in the practice block.
examples.zh: 虚构学生完成练习区块的例题后，第一个「正式测试试次」开始。

examples.en: We calculated the score from each test trial but left out the initial practice responses.
examples.zh: 我们用各个「正式测试试次」计算得分，把最初的练习作答排除在外。

words.enDefinition: Improved later retention from taking a memory test compared with restudying

examples.en: The graph illustrates the testing effect using later scores after initial testing or rereading.
examples.zh: 图表对照了先测试和先重读两组的后续分数，以此说明「测试效应」。

examples.en: We discussed the testing effect using delayed scores from a fictional vocabulary study.
examples.zh: 我们用虚构词汇研究的延迟测验分数讨论了「测试效应」。

words.enDefinition: A change in apparent texture density or scale that signals depth.

examples.en: The pebble photograph showed a texture gradient as the visible gaps narrowed toward the far end.
examples.zh: 卵石照片中的缝隙在画面远端看起来更窄，展示了「纹理梯度」。

examples.en: A texture gradient made the flat drawing of a tiled courtyard seem to extend into the distance.
examples.zh: 「纹理梯度」让平面图上铺瓷砖的庭院看起来向远处延伸。

words.enDefinition: understanding that people have beliefs, desires and knowledge that can differ from one's own or from reality

examples.en: The theory of mind activity asks students to predict where a fictional character will look for an object.
examples.zh: 「心理理论」活动要求学生预测虚构人物会去哪里找一个物件。

examples.en: We used a theory of mind example to distinguish what a character knew from what the audience knew.
examples.zh: 我们用一个「心理理论」示例区分人物掌握的信息与观众掌握的信息。

words.enDefinition: A theory linking action intentions to attitudes, perceived social expectations, and perceived control over the behaviour.

examples.en: The class uses the theory of planned behaviour to interpret fictional survey answers about joining a reading group.
examples.zh: 全班用「计划行为理论」解读关于加入读书小组的虚构调查答案。

examples.en: Our diagram of the theory of planned behaviour connects the three explanatory factors to an intention.
examples.zh: 我们绘制的「计划行为理论」示意图把三个解释因素关联到一个行为意向。

collocations: apply the theory of planned behaviour
constructs of the theory of planned behaviour
study using the theory of planned behaviour

words.enDefinition: An impression or assessment made from a brief sample of another person's behaviour.

examples.en: The class discusses a thin-slice judgment after hearing just a few seconds from a fictional dialogue.
examples.zh: 全班只听几秒钟的虚构对话，就围绕「基于短片段的判断」展开讨论。

examples.en: Our tutor notes that a thin-slice judgment uses less information than the later accounts in the exercise.
examples.zh: 老师指出，「基于短片段的判断」所用的信息比练习后半部分的记述更少。

words.enDefinition: A procedure in which participants verbalize thoughts while carrying out a task.

examples.en: The think-aloud protocol asked the fictional student to describe each option while working through the puzzle.
examples.zh: 「出声思考方案」要求虚构学生解谜时边做边说出正在考虑的各个选项。

examples.en: We discussed how a think-aloud protocol could reveal which parts of the problem received attention.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「出声思考方案」如何帮助发现作答者注意到了问题的哪些部分。

words.enDefinition: the principle that an interpretation of a situation can produce real social consequences when people act on it

examples.en: The Thomas theorem explained why a mistakenly expected shortage still changed what people bought in the classroom model.
examples.zh: 「托马斯定理」解释了为什么在课堂模型中，即使短缺预期有误，仍会改变人们购买的物品。

examples.en: We discussed the Thomas theorem by separating a belief's accuracy from the consequences of acting on it.
examples.zh: 我们区分信念是否准确与据此行动会产生什么后果，以讨论「托马斯定理」。

collocations: social consequences in the Thomas theorem

words.enDefinition: Binary response model with item difficulty, discrimination, and a lower asymptote

examples.en: In the three-parameter logistic model, each simulated curve can approach a nonzero lower limit.
examples.zh: 在「三参数逻辑斯蒂模型」中，各条模拟曲线可以逼近一个非零下限。

examples.en: Our tutorial identifies the extra parameter in the three-parameter logistic model fitted to synthetic responses.
examples.zh: 辅导课指出了拟合到合成作答的「三参数逻辑斯蒂模型」里多出的参数。

collocations: estimates from a three-parameter logistic model

words.enDefinition: Recording behavior during selected moments or time windows rather than throughout an observation period.

examples.en: The time sampling worksheet recorded activity during selected parts of the fictional session at regular intervals.
examples.zh: 「时间取样」习题按固定间隔记录虚构活动中选定时段的行为。

examples.en: We compared time sampling with a complete recording to see which brief classroom events were missed.
examples.zh: 我们把「时间取样」与完整记录作比较，看看漏掉了哪些短暂的课堂事件。

words.enDefinition: Temporary inability to retrieve a familiar word despite feeling it is accessible

examples.en: The lecture illustrates the tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon with a familiar title that temporarily escapes recall.
examples.zh: 讲座用暂时想不起一个熟悉标题的情形说明「舌尖现象」。

examples.en: We used the tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon to discuss why a word can feel almost accessible.
examples.zh: 我们用「舌尖现象」讨论为什么有时觉得一个词马上就能想起来。

words.enDefinition: Perception shaped by prior knowledge, expectations, or the surrounding context.

examples.en: The blurry letter was easier to identify in a word, illustrating top-down processing in the lecture.
examples.zh: 模糊的字母放在完整单词中更容易认出，这是课上展示的「自上而下加工」。

examples.en: The instructor used top-down processing to explain why a meaningful sentence helped listeners interpret an unclear syllable.
examples.zh: 老师用「自上而下加工」解释为什么有明确含义的句子能帮助听者听懂含糊的音节。

words.enDefinition: The expression of a personality trait in response to situational cues relevant to that trait.

examples.en: The fictional teamwork exercise illustrates trait activation through different opportunities for social participation across two settings.
examples.zh: 虚构团队练习用两个场景中不同的社交参与机会说明「特质激活」。

examples.en: Trait activation may explain why the fictional student is more expressive during an informal discussion.
examples.zh: 「特质激活」可能解释这名虚构学生为什么在非正式讨论中更愿意表达。

words.enDefinition: An approach to personality that describes individual differences in terms of relatively enduring dimensions or dispositions.

examples.en: The textbook introduces the trait approach by comparing several hypothetical patterns of behaviour across different settings.
examples.zh: 教材比较不同情境下几种假设的行为模式，以介绍「特质取向」。

examples.en: In the classroom debate, the trait approach provides one framework for summarising the imaginary students' tendencies.
examples.zh: 在课堂讨论中，「特质取向」提供了一种概括虚构学生行为倾向的框架。

words.enDefinition: A narrower component within a broader personality trait or domain.

examples.en: The class treats orderliness as a trait facet within a wider group of tendencies in the example.
examples.zh: 全班将条理性视为示例中某组较宽泛倾向下的一个「特质侧面」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which trait facet is illustrated by consistently keeping shared materials organised after group activities.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，小组活动后总是把共有材料摆放整齐体现了哪一个「特质侧面」。

words.enDefinition: application of a previously learned solution method to another problem, often by recognizing a shared structure

examples.en: The class measured transfer of a solution by presenting a new puzzle with the same underlying structure.
examples.zh: 全班呈现一个底层结构相同的新谜题，测量是否出现「解法迁移」。

examples.en: The new example tested transfer of a solution after changing every surface detail of the original problem.
examples.zh: 新示例改变原问题的全部表面细节，从而检验「解法迁移」。

collocations: evidence of transfer of a solution

words.enDefinition: Influence of earlier practice on performance in a different task

examples.en: The transfer of training exercise compares practice on one keyboard with performance on another.
examples.zh: 「训练迁移」练习比较了在一种键盘上练习与在另一种键盘上操作的表现。

examples.en: Our group studied transfer of training using two fictional tasks with different button layouts.
examples.zh: 我们组用按钮布局不同的两个虚构任务研究「训练迁移」。

words.enDefinition: inferring a relation between two items by chaining known relations through an intermediate item

examples.en: The fictional learner used transitive inference to rank two sticks after comparing each with a middle length stick.
examples.zh: 虚构学习者先将两根棒各与中等长度的棒比较，再用「传递性推理」排出两者次序。

examples.en: We tested transitive inference by requesting a comparison that had never been directly shown in the activity.
examples.zh: 我们提出比较活动里从未直接展示过的两项，以检验「传递性推理」。

words.enDefinition: Degree to which translated test wording preserves the intended original meaning

examples.en: The tutorial discusses translation equivalence after comparing the meaning of two invented translations.
examples.zh: 辅导课比较了两个虚构译本的含义，随后讨论「翻译等值性」。

examples.en: We distinguished translation equivalence from evidence that the two language versions yield comparable scores.
examples.zh: 我们区分了「翻译等值性」与两个语言版本能否产生可比较分数的证据。

words.enDefinition: a problem-solving method that tests possible actions and uses their results to guide further attempts

examples.en: The trial-and-error strategy produced several unsuccessful arrangements before the group found one that met the stated condition.
examples.zh: 在小组找到满足指定条件的布局之前，「试误策略」产生了几个不成功的布局。

examples.en: We recognized the trial-and-error strategy when the learner tried several moves and kept the one that worked.
examples.zh: 学习者尝试多个操作并保留奏效的一项，据此我们辨认出了「试误策略」。

words.enDefinition: A sequence of task trials treated as a unit.

examples.en: The first trial block used one symbol set before the task switched to a different set.
examples.zh: 第一个「试次区块」使用一组符号，之后任务换成另一组。

examples.en: We summarized the accuracy of each trial block before comparing the earlier and later parts.
examples.zh: 我们先汇总各个「试次区块」的正确率，再对比前后两部分。

collocations: a trial block of practice items

words.enDefinition: Sternberg's theoretical framework distinguishing analytical, creative and practical aspects of intelligent behavior

examples.en: The instructor used the triarchic theory of intelligence to compare school puzzles with novel and everyday tasks.
examples.zh: 老师运用「智力三元理论」，将学校解谜题与新颖任务及日常任务作比较。

examples.en: We labeled three branches of the triarchic theory of intelligence in the summary diagram used in class.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂所用总结图上标出「智力三元理论」的三个方面。

collocations: study the triarchic theory of intelligence
components of the triarchic theory of intelligence

words.enDefinition: Expected score over hypothetical repetitions under the same defined measurement conditions

examples.en: The classical model defines a true score using the average across hypothetical repeated tests.
examples.zh: 经典模型用多次假设重复测验的平均值来定义「真分数」。

examples.en: We discussed why one observed score cannot establish the simulated person's true score.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么单次观测分数不能确定模拟人物的「真分数」。

collocations: distinguish an observed score from a true score

words.enDefinition: Erikson's early psychosocial conflict concerning whether caregiving and the immediate world are experienced as reliable

examples.en: The reading illustrates trust versus mistrust by discussing the fictional infant's expectations about caregiver availability over time.
examples.zh: 阅读材料通过讨论虚构婴儿对照护者长期是否可接近的预期，说明「信任对不信任」。

examples.en: We placed trust versus mistrust at the beginning of the timeline of Erikson's proposed challenges in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们把「信任对不信任」放在埃里克森提出的各项挑战时间线的起点。

words.enDefinition: A task design requiring a response from two specified alternatives on every trial.

examples.en: Our two-alternative forced choice example asked which of two intervals contained the faint tone.
examples.zh: 我们的「二选一迫选」示例要求判断微弱音调出现在哪一个时段。

examples.en: In the two-alternative forced choice task, a guess still counted as one of the two options.
examples.zh: 在「二选一迫选」任务中，即使靠猜，作答也只能从两个选项中选一个。

words.enDefinition: Binary response model allowing item difficulty and discrimination to vary

examples.en: The two-parameter logistic model allows the two simulated items to have different slopes.
examples.zh: 「双参数逻辑斯蒂模型」允许两道模拟题的曲线斜率不同。

examples.en: We compared a two-parameter logistic model with a model using one common slope.
examples.zh: 我们比较了一个「双参数逻辑斯蒂模型」与采用共同斜率的模型。

collocations: item estimates from a two-parameter logistic model
assumptions of the two-parameter logistic model

words.enDefinition: An account combining homeostatic sleep pressure with the influence of circadian timing.
acceptedEnVariants: two process model of sleep regulation

examples.en: The two-process model of sleep regulation showed why time awake alone did not explain the simulated pattern.
examples.zh: 「睡眠调节双过程模型」说明了为什么单靠清醒时长并不能解释模拟模式。

examples.en: We drew two curves in class to represent the two-process model of sleep regulation.
examples.zh: 我们在课上画了两条曲线来表示「睡眠调节双过程模型」。

collocations: the homeostatic component of the two-process model of sleep regulation
compare predictions of the two-process model of sleep regulation
apply the two-process model of sleep regulation

words.enDefinition: an evolutionary explanation of why a trait or behavior may have arisen or persisted across generations

examples.en: The ultimate explanation proposed a possible adaptive function for the behavior in the assigned evolutionary psychology reading.
examples.zh: 进化心理学指定阅读中的「终极解释」为这种行为提出一种可能的适应性功能。

examples.en: We asked what comparative evidence would support an ultimate explanation of the pattern discussed in class.
examples.zh: 我们问，怎样的比较证据能够支持课堂所讨论现象的「终极解释」。

words.enDefinition: Reaction elicited by a stimulus without the need for learning

examples.en: The first panel shows the unconditioned response before the two events have ever occurred together.
examples.zh: 第一幅图显示，在两个事件首次同时出现之前就有「无条件反应」。

examples.en: We labeled the blink to the puff in the illustration as an unconditioned response.
examples.zh: 我们将图中气流引起的眨眼标为「无条件反应」。

words.enDefinition: Stimulus that elicits a particular response without prior associative learning

examples.en: In our simulated diagram, the unconditioned stimulus already elicits a response before training begins.
examples.zh: 在模拟示意图中，「无条件刺激」在训练开始前就能引发反应。

examples.en: The worksheet asks which event represents the unconditioned stimulus in this example.
examples.zh: 习题问，示例中的哪个事件是「无条件刺激」。

words.enDefinition: Assumption that one latent dimension accounts for the measured item responses

examples.en: The class checks unidimensionality before interpreting scores using a single skill dimension.
examples.zh: 课堂在用单一技能维度解读分数之前，先检查「单维性」。

examples.en: We discussed unidimensionality after comparing one-factor and two-factor models for the fictional items.
examples.zh: 我们比较了虚构题目的单因子和双因子模型，接着讨论了「单维性」。

words.enDefinition: The tendency to perceive connected elements within a uniform region as one unit.
