examples.en: The slide illustrated uniform connectedness by linking distant dots with lines of the same color.
examples.zh: 投影片用同色线条连接相隔很远的圆点，以展示「一致连接原则」。

examples.en: Uniform connectedness helped explain why the linked shapes looked more unified than some much closer pairs.
examples.zh: 「一致连接原则」有助于解释为何连起来的形状看起来比某些离得近得多的成对形状更像一个整体。

words.enDefinition: Group effect on item responses without an interaction with measured trait level

examples.en: The synthetic example shows uniform differential item functioning with parallel logit curves across groups.
examples.zh: 合成示例用不同组的平行对数优势曲线来展示「一致性项目功能差异」。

examples.en: We checked whether the model for uniform differential item functioning included a trait interaction.
examples.zh: 我们检查了「一致性项目功能差异」模型是否包含特质交互项。

collocations: test for uniform differential item functioning
evidence of uniform differential item functioning

words.enDefinition: a pattern of parenting described as relatively low in both responsiveness and expectations or monitoring

examples.en: The worksheet places an uninvolved parenting style in the quadrant with low responsiveness and low demands.
examples.zh: 练习将「疏离型养育方式」标在模型中回应与要求均低的象限。

examples.en: We discussed the uninvolved parenting style using the textbook's categories for its fictional set of examples.
examples.zh: 我们用教材为虚构示例设定的类别讨论「疏离型养育方式」。

collocations: example of an uninvolved parenting style
compare an uninvolved parenting style with other styles

words.enDefinition: The entity or event to which one observation record refers.

examples.en: The worksheet treated each conversation turn as a unit of observation rather than each individual student.
examples.zh: 习题把每个对话轮次作「观察单位」，没有按每个学生分别记录。

examples.en: We clarified the unit of observation before comparing two tables with very different numbers of rows.
examples.zh: 在比较行数相差很大的两张表格之前，我们先明确了「观察单位」。

words.enDefinition: a benefit available to all members of a specified population or category without an income or assets test

examples.en: The worksheet labels the payment a universal benefit because every fictional household in the defined group qualifies.
examples.zh: 由于所定群组内的每个虚构家庭都有资格，习题把这笔款项标为「普惠性福利」。

examples.en: We compared a universal benefit with a payment linked to income in the policy diagram used for class.
examples.zh: 我们把「普惠性福利」与课堂政策图中取决于收入的给付作比较。

words.enDefinition: movement to a position ranked higher in a specified system of social stratification

examples.en: The table shows upward mobility when the fictional participant moves into a higher-ranked occupational position over time.
examples.zh: 当虚构参与者随时间进入排名更高的职业位置时，表中显示「向上流动」。

examples.en: We explained which ranking made the change count as upward mobility in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 我们解释课堂示例中的变化依据哪种排名才算「向上流动」。

words.enDefinition: A cue correctly indicating where or when a target will appear.

examples.en: In the example, a valid cue pointed toward the same square where the target eventually appeared.
examples.zh: 例子中，「有效线索」指向的正是目标后来出现的方框。

examples.en: The worksheet compared response times after a valid cue with times when no direction was given.
examples.zh: 习题比较给出「有效线索」后与没有提供方向时的反应时间。

collocations: a trial with a valid cue
the benefit of a valid cue

words.enDefinition: a deductive inference whose form guarantees a true conclusion whenever all its premises are true

examples.en: The worksheet asks whether the argument is a valid inference even though the story uses imaginary objects.
examples.zh: 习题询问，尽管故事采用虚构物件，这一论证是否仍构成「有效推论」。

examples.en: We recognized a valid inference after ruling out every case with true premises and a false conclusion.
examples.zh: 我们排除了所有前提为真而结论为假的情形，从而辨认出「有效推论」。

words.enDefinition: Reasoned case linking evidence and assumptions to an intended score interpretation

examples.en: The class read a validation argument for one proposed use of the fictional scores.
examples.zh: 课堂阅读了一份针对虚构分数某项拟定用途的「效度论证」。

examples.en: Our group identified one assumption in the validation argument that remained untested.
examples.zh: 我们组找出了「效度论证」中一个尚未检验的假设。

words.enDefinition: Information bearing on whether intended interpretations or uses of scores are justified

examples.en: The workbook groups validity evidence by the questions it addresses about score interpretation.
examples.zh: 练习册按所要回答的分数解释问题对「效度证据」分类。

examples.en: We identified the validity evidence that speaks to the intended interpretation in the example.
examples.zh: 我们找出了示例中与预期解释有关的「效度证据」。

words.enDefinition: Schedule reinforcing the first response after each varying time interval

examples.en: In the model, eligible responses occur after different waits under a variable-interval schedule.
examples.zh: 模型采用「可变时距时程」，符合得分条件的反应出现在不等长的等待之后。

examples.en: We identified the variable-interval schedule because the waiting time changed across simulated rounds.
examples.zh: 我们通过模拟各轮的等待时间不同辨认出「可变时距时程」。

words.enDefinition: Reinforcement schedule varying the response count needed around an average

examples.en: The simulated variable-ratio schedule awards points after different numbers of correct matches.
examples.zh: 模拟「可变比率时程」在正确匹配达到不同次数后发放积分。

examples.en: The example lists an average response count for the variable-ratio schedule used in class.
examples.zh: 示例列出了课堂演示的「可变比率时程」的平均反应次数。

collocations: compare a variable-ratio schedule with a fixed ratio

words.enDefinition: A shift in perceived sound location toward a visible event.

examples.en: The ventriloquism effect made the recorded voice seem to come from the moving puppet on the screen.
examples.zh: 受「腹语效应」影响，录制的人声听起来像是屏幕上活动的木偶发出的。

examples.en: The ventriloquism effect diagram marked the actual speaker and the location where listeners thought the sound originated.
examples.zh: 「腹语效应」示意图标出了扬声器的实际位置和听者以为声音传出的位置。

collocations: a demonstration of the ventriloquism effect

words.enDefinition: A spoken description of a participant's experience, judgment, or thought process.

examples.en: The lecture compared a verbal report about the picture with the response chosen on the classroom worksheet.
examples.zh: 老师把关于图片的「言语报告」与课堂习题中选出的答案作比较。

examples.en: We checked the verbal report to see how the fictional learner described the route in their own words.
examples.zh: 我们查看「言语报告」，看虚构学习者如何用自己的话描述这条路线。

words.enDefinition: interpretive understanding that seeks to grasp the meanings people attach to their own social actions

examples.en: The lecture introduces verstehen by asking why a routine mattered to the fictional participants who performed it.
examples.zh: 讲义询问某一惯例对实践它的虚构参与者为何重要，由此介绍「理解式解释」。

examples.en: We used verstehen to compare participants' explanations with an external description of the same event in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们以「理解式解释」对照参与者自己的说明与对同一事件的外部描述。

words.enDefinition: movement up or down a hierarchy of social positions

examples.en: The worksheet uses arrows in both directions to show vertical mobility between levels in the fictional classification.
examples.zh: 习题用双向箭头表示虚构分类的各层级之间的「垂直流动」。

examples.en: We counted examples of vertical mobility separately from moves between positions of the same rank in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们将「垂直流动」实例与同一等级地位之间的变动分别计数。

words.enDefinition: Reduced tendency to imitate after observing negative consequences for a model

examples.en: The mock game illustrates vicarious punishment when observers avoid a move that cost someone points.
examples.zh: 模拟游戏用观察者避开曾让别人扣分的操作来说明「替代性惩罚」。

examples.en: The worksheet classifies the change as vicarious punishment because only the model lost points.
examples.zh: 习题把这一变化归为「替代性惩罚」，因为只有示范者被扣分。

collocations: distinguish vicarious punishment from direct punishment

words.enDefinition: Increased tendency to imitate after observing a model receive reinforcement

examples.en: The animation illustrates vicarious reinforcement when viewers copy the player who earns points.
examples.zh: 动画用观众模仿得分玩家的情形说明「替代性强化」。

examples.en: We identified vicarious reinforcement even though the observers had received no points themselves.
examples.zh: 尽管观察者自己没有得到积分，我们仍辨认出了「替代性强化」。

words.enDefinition: A decline in detecting occasional targets during prolonged monitoring.

examples.en: The simulated data showed a vigilance decrement as learners detected fewer rare targets later in the task.
examples.zh: 模拟数据显示，学习者在任务后段检出的少见目标更少，出现了「警觉性衰减」。

examples.en: We compared the first and last blocks to estimate the vigilance decrement in the classroom record.
examples.zh: 我们比较了课堂记录中的首个和最后一个区段，以估计「警觉性衰减」。

collocations: the size of a vigilance decrement

words.enDefinition: a research approach using differences in responses to expected and unexpected events as evidence about expectations

examples.en: The lecture's violation-of-expectation paradigm compares looking times for two events in an animated scenario involving hidden shapes.
examples.zh: 讲义的「预期违背范式」比较隐藏图形动画情景中两个事件的注视时间。

examples.en: We discussed which alternative explanation might produce longer looking in the example of a violation-of-expectation paradigm.
examples.zh: 我们讨论用「预期违背范式」的示例中，哪种其他解释也可能产生较长注视时间。

words.enDefinition: Reduced visibility of a target due to another visual stimulus close in time or space.

examples.en: The visual masking example showed a faint shape whose outline became harder to report amid another pattern.
examples.zh: 「视觉掩蔽」示例中，微弱形状被另一图案干扰，因此更难报告它的轮廓。

examples.en: We compared visual masking across two versions of the slide that used different surrounding patterns.
examples.zh: 我们比较了采用不同干扰图案的两版幻灯片中的「视觉掩蔽」。

words.enDefinition: Looking for a target in a display that also contains other items.

examples.en: In the visual search example, students looked for a curved symbol among several straight ones.
examples.zh: 「视觉搜索」示例中，学生在几个直线符号中寻找一个弯曲符号。

examples.en: The instructor varied the number of distractors to illustrate how visual search time could change.
examples.zh: 老师改变干扰项的数量，以说明「视觉搜索」所用时间可能如何变化。

words.enDefinition: A difference in search ease when the roles of target and distractor are exchanged.

examples.en: The paired displays illustrated visual search asymmetry by switching which of the two shapes counted as the target.
examples.zh: 成对的展示图对调两种形状中的目标与干扰角色，以说明「视觉搜索不对称」。

examples.en: We found visual search asymmetry when the two reversed tasks produced different response times in the simulation.
examples.zh: 两个互换目标和干扰项的模拟任务产生了不同的反应时间，我们由此发现「视觉搜索不对称」。

collocations: an example of visual search asymmetry

words.enDefinition: Working memory component for temporarily holding and manipulating visual or spatial information

examples.en: The model uses the visuospatial sketchpad to explain mentally tracking locations on a grid.
examples.zh: 模型用「视觉空间画板」解释人们如何在心中跟踪网格上的位置。

examples.en: Our class related the visuospatial sketchpad to holding a shape in mind while rotating it.
examples.zh: 课堂将「视觉空间画板」与在脑海中保留并旋转图形联系起来。

words.enDefinition: Taking part in research by free choice, without undue pressure.

examples.en: The fictional course notice explained voluntary participation before listing any activities eligible for research credit.
examples.zh: 虚构课程通知先说明「自愿参与」，再列出可获得研究参与学分的活动。

examples.en: In the ethical case discussion, voluntary participation meant students could decline without losing ordinary course options.
examples.zh: 在伦理案例讨论中，「自愿参与」意味着学生可以拒绝，而且普通课程选项仍然可选。

words.enDefinition: The total time spent awake after falling asleep and before the final awakening.

examples.en: In the classroom record, wake after sleep onset included three separate intervals before the final awakening.
examples.zh: 课堂记录里的「入睡后清醒时间」包括最后醒来之前三个彼此分开的时段。

examples.en: We summed the short awakenings in the simulated plot to find wake after sleep onset.
examples.zh: 我们把模拟图上各个短暂的清醒时段相加，算出「入睡后清醒时间」。

collocations: a measure of wake after sleep onset
compare wake after sleep onset across records

words.enDefinition: unequal distribution of net assets among people, households or groups in a specified population

examples.en: The chart illustrates wealth inequality by comparing the net assets held by different groups of fictional households.
examples.zh: 图表通过比较不同虚构家庭群体持有的净资产，说明「财富不平等」。

examples.en: We examined wealth inequality separately from annual earnings in the classroom example about resources across generations.
examples.zh: 课堂讨论世代间资源的示例中，我们分别考察「财富不平等」和年收入。

words.enDefinition: The ratio of a difference threshold to its reference stimulus magnitude.

examples.en: The example divided the weight increment by the reference weight to obtain the Weber fraction.
examples.zh: 例题将重量增量除以参照重量，得到了「韦伯分数」。

examples.en: Our two examples gave similar values for the Weber fraction despite using different reference weights.
examples.zh: 尽管参照重量不同，两道例题算出的「韦伯分数」相近。

collocations: compare estimates of the Weber fraction

words.enDefinition: The approximate rule that detectable increments scale with the starting stimulus magnitude.

examples.en: Weber's law predicts that the heavier reference object requires a larger increase to feel different.
examples.zh: 「韦伯定律」预测，参照物体越重，就需要增加更多重量才能感觉到不同。

examples.en: The lecturer used Weber's law to explain why the ratio mattered in that range.
examples.zh: 老师用「韦伯定律」解释了为什么在这个范围内要看比值。

words.enDefinition: Chance-adjusted agreement coefficient giving different weights to different category disagreements

examples.en: In our tutorial, weighted kappa treats adjacent rating disagreements differently from larger ones.
examples.zh: 辅导课上，「加权κ系数」对相邻等级的评分分歧和跨度更大的分歧区别处理。

examples.en: We compared weighted kappa with an index that treats all disagreements equally.
examples.zh: 我们将「加权κ系数」与对所有分歧同等处理的指标作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Score calculated by assigning specified relative contributions to its components

examples.en: The sample worksheet gives the reasoning section a larger contribution to the weighted score.
examples.zh: 样本习题中，推理部分在「加权分」中所占比重更大。

examples.en: We compared a weighted score with the simple sum from the same responses.
examples.zh: 我们比较了同一组回答计算出的「加权分」与直接加总的分数。

words.enDefinition: a problem with a clear starting state, allowed operations and criteria for a correct solution

examples.en: The instructor chose a well-defined problem with explicit move rules and a single stated goal in class.
examples.zh: 老师选择一个写明操作规则、只有一个指定目标的「界定清晰的问题」在课堂上讨论。

examples.en: We explained why the puzzle counted as a well-defined problem after finding its exact success criterion.
examples.zh: 我们找到谜题的确切成功判据后，解释它为何属于「界定清晰的问题」。

words.enDefinition: Scoring an interval positive only when a target behavior continues throughout it.

examples.en: Whole-interval recording marked the segment only when the fictional student kept reading throughout the entire interval.
examples.zh: 只有虚构学生在整个时段都在阅读时，「全区间记录」才给该段标记。

examples.en: The class compared whole-interval recording with a method that counted a brief occurrence anywhere in the segment.
examples.zh: 全班把「全区间记录」与一种在时段内任何位置短暂出现就记一次的方法作比较。

words.enDefinition: An experiment in which the same participants complete every relevant condition.

examples.en: The within-participants design let us compare each fictional student's response times under both display conditions.
examples.zh: 「被试内设计」让我们能比较每名虚构学生在两种显示条件下的反应时间。

examples.en: The worksheet identified a within-participants design because each participant code appeared under both conditions.
examples.zh: 习题将此归为「被试内设计」，因为每个参与者编号都出现在两种条件下。

collocations: a study using a within-participants design

words.enDefinition: Limited system for temporarily holding and manipulating information during current tasks

examples.en: The task uses working memory to keep two numbers available while adding them.
examples.zh: 这项任务需要用「工作记忆」在做加法时暂时记住两个数字。

examples.en: Our notes distinguish working memory from simply repeating a few letters in order.
examples.zh: 我们的笔记区分了「工作记忆」与单纯按顺序重复几个字母。

words.enDefinition: Amount of information a person can actively maintain during processing

examples.en: The exercise compares estimates of working memory capacity from two short classroom tasks.
examples.zh: 练习对比了两项短时课堂任务估得的「工作记忆容量」。

examples.en: Our group discussed why working memory capacity estimates can depend on the task used.
examples.zh: 我们组讨论了为什么「工作记忆容量」的估计值可能取决于所用任务。

collocations: individual differences in working memory capacity

words.enDefinition: A task asking whether a signal was present on each trial.

examples.en: The yes-no detection task included silent trials as well as trials containing a brief tone.
examples.zh: 「是否检出任务」既有静默试次，也有播放短音的试次。

examples.en: In the simulated yes-no detection task, responses were recorded separately for each type of trial.
examples.zh: 在模拟「是否检出任务」中，不同类型试次的作答分别记录。

collocations: a yes-no detection task with tones
responses in a yes-no detection task
compare a yes-no detection task with forced choice

words.enDefinition: the range between what a learner can do independently and what they can do with suitable support

examples.en: The tutor identified the zone of proximal development by comparing unsupported answers with answers after a hint.
examples.zh: 老师对照无帮助时和提示后的回答，辨认出「最近发展区」。

examples.en: We placed the tasks the learner could complete with guidance inside the zone of proximal development.
examples.zh: 我们将学习者在指导下可以完成的任务放入「最近发展区」。

collocations: work within the zone of proximal development
identify a zone of proximal development
task in the zone of proximal development
